extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 매출 means "sales; revenue" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "sales; revenue" is 매출 (maechul). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 매출이 오르다 ("sales go up"). Watch the particle attached to 매출 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about talking about work, schedules, tasks, and obligations first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 오르다 intransitive 'rise', sales rise on their own
떨어지다 'fall', the natural opposite
올리다 transitive 'raise', you actively raise it
목표 (目標) 'goal/target', a constant team phrase

examples.en: How are this month's sales?
examples.note: simple: 어때요 'how is it' asks for an assessment

examples.en: During COVID sales dropped by half.
examples.note: everyday: 반으로 '(down) to half', 으로 marks the result

examples.ko: 매출 목표를 못 채워서 팀 전체가 스트레스받고 있어요.
examples.romanization: maechul mokpyoreul mot chaewoseo tim jeonchega seuteureseubatgo isseoyo.
examples.en: We couldn't hit the sales target, so the whole team is stressed.
examples.note: real situation: 채우다 'fill/meet (a quota)' is the set verb with 목표

extendedVocab.nuance: 매출 is top-line sales/revenue — the gross money coming in before any costs are subtracted. It is Sino-Korean 賣出, literally 'sell-out', i.e. what you sold out the door. The crucial business-vocabulary contrast is 매출 (revenue, total inflow) vs 이익/수익 (利益/收益, profit = what's left after costs): a company can have huge 매출 but tiny 이익. Its life-partners are the rise/fall pair 오르다/떨어지다 (intransitive) and 올리다/낮추다 (transitive), plus 매출 목표 and 매출을 채우다 (meet the sales quota). The English-speaker pitfall is twofold: (1) confusing 'sales/revenue' with 'profit' — keep 매출 ≠ 이익 firmly apart; and (2) describing a big figure with 많다 ('many') as in 매출이 많다 — for a high amount Koreans say 매출이 높다 ('high'), since 매출 is a measured level, not a count of items.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 매출 (revenue, total sales) with 이익 or 수익 (profit after costs) — a firm with high 매출 can still have low 이익
Saying 매출이 많다 for a big figure — use 매출이 높다 ('high'); 많다 is for countable quantities, 높다 for measured levels
Saying 매출을 벌다 ('earn sales') from English habit — you 매출을 올리다/내다 (raise/post sales); 벌다 ('earn') goes with 돈 (돈을 벌다)

extendedVocab.nuance: 부서 is the general word for an organizational unit inside a company — a department or division. It is Sino-Korean 部署, where 部 means 'section/division' (the same 部 in 부장 department head) and 署 'a post/office'. The structural distinction newcomers must internalize: a 부서 is the broad department, a 팀 (team) is usually a smaller working unit inside or alongside it, and 부 alone (영업부, 인사부) is the formal divisional name. Beware the look-alike trap 부서 (the department, a place/unit) vs 부장 (部長, the department HEAD, a person) — one letter apart but unit vs human. New hires hear 어느 부서예요? on loop during introductions, so keep it primed. The English-speaker pitfall is treating 부서 and 팀 as interchangeable the way English flips 'department/team'; in a Korean org chart they sit at different levels, and you transfer between them with 옮기다, not 바꾸다 ('swap/change an object').
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Mixing up 부서 (the department/unit) with 부장 (the department HEAD, a person) — they differ by one syllable but one is a place and one is your boss
Treating 부서 and 팀 as identical — a 팀 is normally a smaller unit within a 부서; Korean org charts keep them at distinct levels
Saying 부서를 바꾸다 for a transfer — 바꾸다 means swapping an object; moving yourself to another department is 부서를 옮기다

extendedVocab.nuance: 팀장 is the team leader — in many Korean companies your most immediate boss, the person you report to daily. It is Sino-Korean 팀(team) + 長 ('head/chief'), the same 長 that ends every Korean rank title: 부장 (department head), 사장 (company president), 회장 (chairman). Two register rules are non-negotiable: (1) you almost always attach 님 — 팀장님 — when speaking to or about them, and (2) you can use the bare rank 팀장 as a respectful address by itself, but never 팀장씨, because 씨 is a peer-level marker that, attached to a superior's title, sounds rude. Knowing 팀장 anchors the whole ladder (팀장 → 부장 → 이사 → 대표). The English-speaker pitfall is importing the Western habit of first names or a flat 'you' for managers: dropping 님 or using 씨 with a boss is a real status error Koreans notice instantly.

Saying 팀장씨 — 씨 is for peers and juniors; attached to a superior's rank it sounds disrespectful, so use 팀장님
Calling them just 너/당신 ('you') — never use second-person pronouns up the ladder; address a superior by 직급(rank)+님, e.g. 팀장님

extendedVocab.nuance: 첨부 means attaching a file to a message, and 첨부 파일 (attached file) is one of the highest-frequency phrases in Korean work email. It is Sino-Korean 添附, literally 'add-attach', both characters meaning to append something extra. The distinction to keep is digital 첨부하다 (attach an email file) vs physical 붙이다 (stick/glue something to a surface) vs 부착하다 (affix a label/poster) — English says 'attach' for all three, but a file is only ever 첨부하다. Its fixed companion line 첨부 파일을 확인해 주세요 is basically email etiquette you can paste anywhere. The English-speaker pitfall, beyond reaching for 붙이다, is spacing: in careful business writing it is two words, 첨부 파일, not 첨부파일 (though the squished form is tolerated in casual chat). Also note 첨부 has no plain past on its own — you write 첨부했어요/첨부했습니다, never 첨부 했어요 with a gap.

Writing 첨부파일 as one word in formal mail — the standard spacing is 첨부 파일 (two words); the joined form reads as casual
Saying 첨부 파일을 보다 to ask the reader to look — politely you say 확인해 주세요 ('please confirm/check'); plain 보다 sounds like a bare command

extendedVocab.nuance: 외근 means working outside the office — visiting clients, sites, or branches during the workday. It is Sino-Korean 外勤, literally 'outside-duty', and its exact mirror is 내근 (內勤, 'inside-duty' = desk/in-office work); the 勤 ('duty/labor') here is the same character in 출근 (going to work) and 야근 (night work). The synonym line learners must draw is 외근 vs 출장 (出張): 외근 is a same-day excursion you return from by evening, while 출장 is a longer trip, often overnight or to another city. Saying 외근 중이에요 is the neat, professional way to explain why a coworker isn't at their seat. The English-speaker pitfall is treating 'out of the office' as one bucket: don't use 외근 for going home, taking leave, or a multi-day trip — it specifically means leaving the building on work business and coming back. Use the action verb 나가다 (외근 나가다), not 가다 alone, for heading out.

Confusing 외근 (a same-day off-site excursion) with 출장 (a longer, often overnight business trip to another place) — duration is the divider
Saying 외근 가다 to mean leaving for the day/going home — 외근 is specifically leaving the office for work duties and returning; for going home use 퇴근하다
Mixing 외근 with 내근 (desk work in the office) — they are exact opposites, 外 'outside' vs 內 'inside'

extendedVocab.nuance: 재택근무 is the formal term for working from home, very commonly clipped to just 재택 in speech (오늘 재택이에요). It is fully Sino-Korean 在宅勤務, parsing as 在 'be located' + 宅 'home/residence' + 근무 'duty/work' — literally 'home-located work duty'. It exploded into daily vocabulary after COVID, so 재택근무 가능해요? is now a normal thing to ask when job hunting. The synonym field: 재택근무 (at home specifically) sits inside the broader 원격근무 (遠隔, 'remote work' from anywhere), while 외근 (off-site duty) is its near-opposite — leaving to go OUT, not staying in. The English-speaker pitfall is inventing a descriptive phrase like 집에서 근무 or 집에서 일해요 as if it were the term: those describe the activity, but the fixed noun is 재택근무. Also keep it apart from 외근 — both involve not sitting at your assigned office desk, but 재택은 home, 외근 is the field.

Confusing it with 외근, which means going OUT for work duties — 재택근무 is staying HOME (在宅)
Saying 재택근무를 가다 ('go to WFH') — you don't go anywhere; use 재택근무를 하다 or 오늘 재택이에요

extendedVocab.nuance: 야근 specifically means staying at the office working late into the night — the iconic symbol of old-school Korean work culture. It is Sino-Korean 夜勤, literally 'night-duty', sharing the 勤 ('duty/labor') of 외근 and 출근. The contrast to nail: 야근 is overtime that runs LATE/at night, whereas 특근 (特勤, 'special duty') and 추가 근무 cover extra work generally, including daytime, weekends, or holidays — so weekend morning work is 특근, not 야근. Its cultural foil is the slang 칼퇴 ('knife-exit' = leaving on the dot at quitting time), the thing everyone dreams of instead. And the carrot is 야근 수당 (overtime pay), which is 나오다 (paid out), not 받다-only. The English-speaker pitfall is using 야근 as a blanket word for all 'overtime' — keep the time-of-day nuance — and saying 야근을 가다 ('go to overtime'); you don't go to it, you 야근을 하다.

Saying 야근을 가다 ('go to overtime') — you don't travel to it; the verb is 야근을 하다 (or just 야근해요)

extendedVocab.nuance: 연차 is your annual paid-vacation entitlement, counted and consumed in days. It is Sino-Korean 年次, literally 'year-order/yearly' (short for 연차 휴가, 年次休暇 'annual leave'). The synonym boundary learners blur: 휴가 (休暇) is the broad umbrella 'leave/vacation' of any kind (including 병가 sick leave, 여름 휴가 summer vacation), while 연차 is the specific paid days you accrue per year — so 연차 is one type of 휴가. A vital partner word is 반차 (半次, 'half-day leave') for slipping out for just a morning or afternoon. The verbs are fixed: you 연차를 쓰다 (use) or 연차를 내다 (file/submit), and your balance 남다 (remains). The English-speaker pitfall is twofold: treating 연차 and 휴가 as fully interchangeable (휴가 is broader), and reaching for 하다 — there is no 연차를 하다; the leave is something you 쓰다 or 내다, not 'do'.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 연차 (specific accrued paid days) with 휴가 — 휴가 is the broad word for any leave/vacation; 연차 is one kind of 휴가
Saying 연차를 하다 — leave is not 'done'; you 연차를 쓰다 ('use') or 연차를 내다 ('file/submit')
Forgetting 반차 (半次, half-day leave) and saying 반 연차 — the established word for a half day off is 반차

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 장바구니 means "shopping cart (online or physical basket)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 장바구니 (jangbaguni) means "shopping cart (online or physical basket)". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 장바구니에 담다 ("to add to the cart"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 장바구니 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: the standard verb is 담다 (to put into a container), not 사다 or 넣다, for online carts

usagePhrases.en: to keep it saved in the cart
usagePhrases.note: -아 두다 = leave it there for later, classic 'wishlist' behavior
비우다 = empty out; the literal button text on most shopping apps
passive 담기다 describes items already waiting to be bought

examples.en: I'll add this to the cart.
examples.note: the bare beginner pattern: object + 장바구니에 담다

examples.ko: 일단 장바구니에 담아 놓고 월급날에 살게요.
examples.romanization: ildan jangbagunie dama noko wolgeumnare salgeyo.
examples.en: I'll just add it to the cart for now and buy it on payday.
examples.note: 담아 놓다 captures 'saved for later'; very common window-shopping phrasing

examples.ko: 할인 시작하면 바로 사려고 장바구니에 미리 담아 뒀어요.
examples.romanization: harin sijakamyeon baro saryeogo jangbagunie miri dama dwosseoyo.
examples.en: I added it to the cart in advance to buy the moment the sale starts.
examples.note: real-situation: 미리 담아 두다 = pre-load the cart before a sale

extendedVocab.nuance: '장바구니'는 마트의 손바구니와 인터넷 쇼핑몰의 카트를 둘 다 가리키는 한 단어라 일상에서 정말 자주 들립니다. 구성은 '장'(market/shopping)+'바구니'(basket)예요. 핵심은 동사 선택: 카트에는 '담다'(put into a container)를 쓰고, '넣다'(put in)도 통하지만 앱 버튼에는 거의 항상 '담기'로 표기됩니다. 영어 화자가 흔히 하는 실수는 'add to cart'를 직역해 '장바구니에 더하다'라고 하거나, 최종 구매 동사 '사다'를 카트 단계에 써 버리는 것 — 담는 것(담다)과 결제하는 것(결제하다)은 분리된 두 단계예요. 비슷해 보이는 '바구니'는 그냥 아무 바구니지만, '장바구니'는 반드시 '쇼핑'을 함의합니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 장바구니에 사다 — 사다 is the final purchase; you 담다 (add) to a cart first, then 결제 (check out). The cart stage and the buy stage are separate.
Direct-translating 'add to cart' as 장바구니에 더하다 — 더하다 means mathematical addition; the real verb is 담다.
Confusing it with bare 바구니 — 바구니 is any basket (laundry, picnic), while 장바구니 specifically implies shopping.

structuredNuance.t: '장바구니'는 마트의 손바구니와 인터넷 쇼핑몰의 카트를 둘 다 가리키는 한 단어라 일상에서 정말 자주 들립니다. 핵심은 동사 선택: 카트에는 '담다'(put into a container)를 쓰고, '넣다'(put in)도 통하지만 앱 버튼에는 거의 항상 '담기'로 표기됩니다.
비슷해 보이는 '바구니'는 그냥 아무 바구니지만, '장바구니'는 반드시 '쇼핑'을 함의합니다.
구성은 '장'(market/shopping)+'바구니'(basket)예요.
영어 화자가 흔히 하는 실수는 'add to cart'를 직역해 '장바구니에 더하다'라고 하거나, 최종 구매 동사 '사다'를 카트 단계에 써 버리는 것 — 담는 것(담다)과 결제하는 것(결제하다)은 분리된 두 단계예요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 배송 means "delivery / shipping (of an ordered item)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "delivery / shipping (of an ordered item)" is 배송 (baesong). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 배송이 빠르다 ("the shipping is fast"). Watch the particle attached to 배송 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 빠르다 (르 irregular) — the #1 thing Koreans praise sellers for
받다 pairs naturally with 배송 for ordered products
조회 = look-up; the menu label for tracking your parcel
늦어지다 = (gradually) becomes late, beyond the promised date

examples.en: The shipping is fast.
examples.note: beginner: 배송 + 빠르다, the single most common review phrase

examples.ko: 주문한 지 이틀 됐는데 아직 배송 안 왔어요.
examples.romanization: jumunhan ji iteul dwaenneunde ajik baesong an wasseoyo.
examples.en: It's been two days since I ordered but the delivery still hasn't come.
examples.note: everyday: 배송이 오다/안 오다 is how spoken Korean treats it, as if it 'comes'

examples.ko: 배송 조회해 보니까 지금 터미널에 있대요.
examples.romanization: baesong johoehae bonikka jigeum teomineore itdaeyo.
examples.en: I checked the tracking and it says it's at the terminal now.
examples.note: real-situation: -대요 reports the tracking screen's info secondhand

extendedVocab.nuance: '배송' 配送 은 한자 그대로 '나누어(配) 보내다(送)', 즉 파는 사람 쪽에서 주문품을 보내는 과정 전체를 뜻해요. 가장 헷갈리는 짝은 '택배'(宅配, home-delivery): '배송'은 보내는 행위/서비스 단계를 가리키고, '택배'는 그것을 실어 나르는 운송 서비스나 도착한 물건 자체(예: '택배 왔어요')를 말합니다. 또 음식점·치킨처럼 즉시 가져다주는 건 '배달'(配達)이라 영역이 달라요 — 쇼핑몰 상품엔 '배송', 짜장면엔 '배달'. 회화에서는 '배송이 왔다/안 왔다'처럼 마치 배송이 스스로 오는 것처럼 자연스럽게 쓰고, 후기에서 '배송 빠르다'는 거의 칭찬의 기본값입니다. 발음은 [배ː송].
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 배달 instead of 배송 for shopping parcels — 배달 is for food/restaurant delivery (피자 배달), while ordered products from a store use 배송.
Equating 배송 and 택배 — 배송 is the shipping process, 택배 is the courier service or the arrived box itself; '택배 왔어요' (the parcel came) cannot become '배송 왔어요' as naturally for the physical box.
Saying 배송을 보내다 about your own received item — as the buyer you 배송을 받다 (receive); the seller is the one who 배송을 보내다.

structuredNuance.t: '배송'은 파는 사람 쪽에서 주문품을 보내는 과정 전체를 뜻해요. 회화에서는 '배송이 왔다/안 왔다'처럼 마치 배송이 스스로 오는 것처럼 자연스럽게 쓰고, 후기에서 '배송 빠르다'는 거의 칭찬의 기본값입니다. 발음은 [배ː송].
가장 헷갈리는 짝은 '택배'(宅配, home-delivery): '배송'은 보내는 행위/서비스 단계를 가리키고, '택배'는 그것을 실어 나르는 운송 서비스나 도착한 물건 자체(예: '택배 왔어요')를 말합니다. 또 음식점·치킨처럼 즉시 가져다주는 건 '배달'(配達)이라 영역이 달라요 — 쇼핑몰 상품엔 '배송', 짜장면엔 '배달'.
'배송' 配送 은 한자 그대로 '나누어(配) 보내다(送)'예요.

extendedVocab.english: waybill / tracking (invoice) number for a parcel
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 송장 means "waybill / tracking (invoice) number for a parcel" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 송장 (songjang) = "waybill / tracking (invoice) number for a parcel". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 송장 번호 ("tracking (waybill) number") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 송장, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: almost always said as a set phrase, not 송장 alone
등록되다 = gets entered, meaning the seller has shipped it
뜨다 = pop up on screen, spoken shorthand for 'it's been issued'
입력 = input; the field label when reporting a return

examples.en: Please tell me the tracking number.
examples.note: beginner: a polite request you send a seller after buying

examples.ko: 판매자가 송장 등록을 안 해서 아직 발송이 안 됐나 봐요.
examples.romanization: panmaejaga songjang deungnogeul an haeseo ajik balsongi an dwaenna bwayo.
examples.en: The seller hasn't registered the waybill, so it seems it hasn't shipped yet.
examples.note: everyday: 송장 등록 = the act that flips a parcel to 'shipped'

examples.ko: 반송할 때 송장 번호를 꼭 사진 찍어 두세요.
examples.romanization: bansonghal ttae songjang beonhoreul kkok sajin jjigeo duseyo.
examples.en: When you send it back, be sure to photograph the waybill number.
examples.note: real-situation: practical return tip; -아 두다 = do it and keep it for safety

extendedVocab.nuance: '송장' 送狀 은 한자로 '보내는(送) 문서(狀)', 곧 택배 상자에 붙은 운송장(라벨)과 거기에 적힌 번호를 뜻해요. 가장 가까운 혼동어는 '영수증'인데, '영수증'은 돈을 냈다는 결제 증빙이고 '송장'은 어디로 어떻게 보내는지를 적은 배송 라벨이라 기능이 완전히 다릅니다. 회화에서는 거의 항상 '송장 번호'로 붙여 말하고, '송장 떴어요?'(번호 나왔어요?)처럼 줄여 쓰기도 해요. 영어 화자의 함정은 영어 invoice를 떠올려 '대금 청구서'로 오해하는 것 — 한국 쇼핑 맥락의 송장은 청구서가 아니라 추적용 운송 라벨/번호입니다. 발음은 적힌 그대로 [송장]이고(앞 받침 ㅇ 뒤라 된소리가 나지 않아요), 같은 소리의 동음이의어 '송장'(시체)과는 맥락으로 구별됩니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 송장 with 영수증 — 영수증 is a payment receipt proving you paid; 송장 is the shipping/tracking label proving how it's sent.
Assuming 송장 = invoice (a bill to pay) because of the English cognate — in shopping it's the waybill/tracking number, not a charge.
Over-tensifying it to [송짱] — there is no 경음화 after the ㅇ batchim here, so 송장 is simply read [송장] as written.

structuredNuance.t: '송장'은 택배 상자에 붙은 운송장(라벨)과 거기에 적힌 번호를 뜻해요. 회화에서는 거의 항상 '송장 번호'로 붙여 말하고, '송장 떴어요?'(번호 나왔어요?)처럼 줄여 쓰기도 해요. 발음은 적힌 그대로 [송장]이고(앞 받침 ㅇ 뒤라 된소리가 나지 않아요), 같은 소리의 동음이의어 '송장'(시체)과는 맥락으로 구별됩니다.
가장 가까운 혼동어는 '영수증'인데, '영수증'은 돈을 냈다는 결제 증빙이고 '송장'은 어디로 어떻게 보내는지를 적은 배송 라벨이라 기능이 완전히 다릅니다.
'송장' 送狀 은 한자로 '보내는(送) 문서(狀)'예요.
영어 invoice를 떠올려 '대금 청구서'로 오해하는 것 — 한국 쇼핑 맥락의 송장은 청구서가 아니라 추적용 운송 라벨/번호입니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 적립 means "points accrual / earning reward points" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 적립 (jeongnip) means "points accrual / earning reward points". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 포인트 적립 ("earning points"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 적립 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: the most common collocation; 적립 needs an object like 포인트/마일리지
-금 (sum of money) = the spendable balance built up from 적립
되다 frames it as happening automatically at checkout

usagePhrases.en: shall I add the points (to your account)?
usagePhrases.note: -아 드리다 = the humble service form a cashier uses

examples.en: If you enter your phone number, you earn points.
examples.note: beginner: heard at almost every Korean checkout, 입력하다 + 적립되다

examples.en: I had 5,000 won in points so I paid with that.
examples.note: everyday: 적립금 is treated like real currency you can spend

examples.en: They give good points here so I come often.
examples.note: real-situation: 적립이 잘되다 = the point rate is generous

extendedVocab.nuance: '적립' 積立 은 한자로 '쌓아(積) 세우다(立)', 즉 결제할 때마다 포인트나 마일리지를 차곡차곡 모으는 걸 말하고, 그렇게 쌓인 돈은 '적립금'이라고 해요. 반드시 구별해야 할 짝은 '할인'입니다 — '할인'은 지금 이 결제에서 값을 즉시 깎아 주는 거고, '적립'은 다음에 쓸 포인트를 모아 두는 거라 시점이 다릅니다(지금 vs 나중). 매장 계산대에서 '적립하시겠어요? 전화번호 뒷자리 불러 주세요'를 거의 매번 듣게 돼요. 영어 화자의 함정은 'save money'의 save를 떠올려 적립을 곧장 '돈 절약'으로 이해하는 것인데, 적립은 절약이 아니라 미래에 쓸 포인트 적립이에요. 또 '적립금을 적립하다'는 겹말이라 어색합니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Mixing up 적립 (accruing points for later) and 할인 (an immediate price cut) — different mechanics and different timing.
Saying 적립금을 적립하다 redundantly — you 포인트를 적립하다 to build the balance, then use 적립금 to pay.
Translating 적립 as plain 'save money' — it is earning reward points, not cutting the price you pay now.

structuredNuance.t: '적립'은 결제할 때마다 포인트나 마일리지를 차곡차곡 모으는 걸 말하고, 그렇게 쌓인 돈은 '적립금'이라고 해요. 매장 계산대에서 '적립하시겠어요? 전화번호 뒷자리 불러 주세요'를 거의 매번 듣게 돼요. 또 '적립금을 적립하다'는 겹말이라 어색합니다.
반드시 구별해야 할 짝은 '할인'입니다 — '할인'은 지금 이 결제에서 값을 즉시 깎아 주는 거고, '적립'은 다음에 쓸 포인트를 모아 두는 거라 시점이 다릅니다(지금 vs 나중).
'적립' 積立 은 한자로 '쌓아(積) 세우다(立)'예요.
'save money'의 save를 떠올려 적립을 곧장 '돈 절약'으로 이해하는 것인데, 적립은 절약이 아니라 미래에 쓸 포인트 적립이에요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 무료배송 means "free shipping" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "free shipping" is 무료배송 (muryobaesong). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 무료배송이다 ("to be free shipping"). Watch the particle attached to 무료배송 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: describing a listing; written as one word on product pages
기준 = standard/baseline, the minimum spend to qualify

usagePhrases.en: in order to get free shipping
usagePhrases.note: -으려고 = with the intent to; the motive for adding more
the inverted phrasing; 배송비 = the shipping charge itself

examples.en: This one is free shipping.
examples.note: beginner: noun + 이다, straight off a product page

examples.en: If you spend over 30,000 won it's free shipping.
examples.note: everyday: 넘게 사다 = buy more than (the threshold)

examples.ko: 무료배송 채우려고 안 살 것까지 담았어요.
examples.romanization: muryobaesong chaeuryeogo an sal geotkkaji damasseoyo.
examples.en: I added stuff I didn't even need just to hit free shipping.
examples.note: real-situation: 채우다 = fill up to the threshold; extremely relatable shopper behavior

extendedVocab.nuance: '무료배송' 無料配送 은 한자로 '요금(料)이 없는(無) 배송(配送)', 곧 배송비를 안 받는다는 뜻이고 보통 한 단어로 붙여 씁니다. 같은 의미를 '배송비 무료'로 뒤집어 말하기도 해요. 가장 가까운 혼동 개념은 '조건부 무료배송'인데, 한국 쇼핑몰은 대개 'O만 원 이상 무료배송'처럼 최소 구매 '기준'을 두기 때문에 그 금액을 채우려고 물건을 더 담는 게 흔한 풍경입니다. 반대말은 '배송비 별도'(shipping charged separately)예요. 영어 화자의 함정은 두 가지 — (1) '공짜배송'이라고 말하는 것: '공짜'는 너무 구어/낮은말이라 표준 표기는 '무료'입니다. (2) free라는 단어만 보고 모든 배송이 무료라고 가정하는 것인데, 거의 항상 최소 주문 기준이 붙습니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing 공짜배송 — 공짜 is too casual/colloquial; the standard, neutral term is 무료배송 (or 배송비 무료).
Assuming all shipping is free — most Korean shops require a minimum spend (무료배송 기준), so check the threshold.
Confusing 무료배송 with 배송비 별도 — the latter means the shipping fee is charged on top, the opposite of free.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 당일배송 means "same-day delivery" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 당일배송 (dangilbaesong) = "same-day delivery". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 당일배송 되다 ("to be eligible for same-day delivery") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 당일배송, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.en: to be eligible for same-day delivery
usagePhrases.note: 되다 marks availability for a given item
마감 = closing/deadline; order before it to qualify

usagePhrases.en: to receive it via same-day delivery
usagePhrases.note: -으로 marks the delivery method
-는 걸로 = '(I'll take) the one that...', picking by feature

examples.en: Does this come same-day?
examples.note: beginner: the single question shoppers ask most, 되다 = is it available

examples.ko: 오전에 주문하면 당일배송으로 받을 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: ojeone jumunhamyeon dangilbaesongeuro badeul su isseoyo.
examples.en: If you order in the morning you can get it same-day.
examples.note: everyday: -으로 marks the method; a morning cutoff is typical

examples.ko: 당일배송 마감이 2시라서 지금 시키면 내일 와요.
examples.romanization: dangilbaesong magami 2siraseo jigeum sikimyeon naeil wayo.
examples.en: The same-day cutoff is 2 p.m., so if you order now it comes tomorrow.
examples.note: real-situation: shows the 마감(cutoff) logic that actually governs it

extendedVocab.nuance: '당일배송' 當日配送 은 한자로 '바로 그날(當日) 배송(配送)', 즉 주문한 그 날 안에 받는 걸 말해요. 한국의 빠른 배송 문화에서 형제 같은 말들과 구별이 중요합니다 — '익일배송'(翌日, next-day)은 다음 날, '새벽배송'(자정~이른 아침 도착)은 밤새 배송해 아침에 받는 것, '로켓배송/총알배송'은 업체 브랜드식 빠른 배송이에요. 핵심 함정은 '마감 시간(cutoff)': 당일배송은 거의 항상 'O시 전 주문 시'라는 조건이 붙어, 그 시간을 넘기면 다음 날로 넘어갑니다. 영어 화자는 same-day를 '아무 때나 주문해도 그날 온다'로 오해하기 쉬운데, 반드시 마감 전 주문이라는 전제를 확인해야 해요. '당일'은 '오늘'보다 문어적·약관적인 어감이라 안내문에 잘 쓰입니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 당일배송 (same day) with 익일배송 (next day) or 새벽배송 (overnight/dawn delivery) — they sound similar but land on different days.
Assuming it applies whenever you order — it almost always requires ordering before a cutoff time (마감), or it slips to tomorrow.
Saying 오늘배송 — the fixed, listing-standard term is 당일배송; 당일 is the formal counterpart of 오늘.

structuredNuance.t: '당일배송'은 주문한 그 날 안에 받는 걸 말해요. '당일'은 '오늘'보다 문어적·약관적인 어감이라 안내문에 잘 쓰입니다.

'당일배송' 當日配送 은 한자로 '바로 그날(當日) 배송(配送)'이에요.
핵심 함정은 '마감 시간(cutoff)': 당일배송은 거의 항상 'O시 전 주문 시'라는 조건이 붙어, 그 시간을 넘기면 다음 날로 넘어갑니다. 영어 화자는 same-day를 '아무 때나 주문해도 그날 온다'로 오해하기 쉬운데, 반드시 마감 전 주문이라는 전제를 확인해야 해요.

extendedVocab.english: direct (in-person) trade between buyer and seller
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 직거래 means "direct (in-person) trade between buyer and seller" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 직거래 (jikgeorae) means "direct (in-person) trade between buyer and seller". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 직거래 하다 ("to do a direct trade"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 직거래 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 거래 is Sino-Korean, so it takes 하다 to become a verb
가능 = possible; a common tag in secondhand listings

usagePhrases.en: the meetup spot for a direct trade
usagePhrases.note: 장소 = place; usually a subway exit or convenience store
보조사 -만 = only; a seller refusing to ship

examples.en: Is in-person trade also possible?
examples.note: beginner: a buyer's quick yes/no question to a seller

examples.en: I bought a chair through an in-person trade on Karrot.
examples.note: everyday: 직거래로 사다 = buy via meeting up; 당근(마켓) is the dominant app

examples.ko: 택배는 안 하고 직거래만 한다고 하시네요.
examples.romanization: taekbaeneun an hago jikgeoraeman handago hasineyo.
examples.en: They say they don't ship and only do in-person trades.
examples.note: real-situation: -다고 하다 reports the seller's stated rule

extendedVocab.nuance: '직거래' 直去來 는 한자로 '곧바로(直) 오가며(去來) 거래한다', 곧 중개나 택배 없이 사는 사람과 파는 사람이 직접 만나 물건과 돈을 주고받는 걸 뜻해요. 헷갈리기 쉬운 짝은 발음이 비슷한 '직구'(直購, 직접 구매)인데, '직구'는 해외 사이트에서 중간상 없이 사들이는 해외 직접구매고, '직거래'는 보통 국내 중고 거래에서 얼굴 보고 만나는 방식이에요 — 하나는 해외 온라인, 하나는 국내 대면이라 방향이 정반대입니다. 또 영어 화자가 자주 빠지는 함정은 'direct'를 '직접 깎아 주는 직거래가니까 싸다'처럼 가격 개념으로 오해하는 것인데, 직거래는 가격이 아니라 '거래 방식'(대면)을 가리킵니다. 안전을 위해 사람 많은 지하철역·편의점 앞에서 만나는 게 보통이고, 멀면 '택배 거래'를 해요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Thinking 직거래 means a discount — it refers to the in-person method, not the price; a 직거래 can cost the same as shipping.
Confusing it with 직구 (직접 구매, overseas direct purchase) — 직구 is buying from foreign sites, 직거래 is local face-to-face trade.
Saying 직거래를 하다 with 을/를 then dropping 하다 — 거래 is a noun that needs 하다 (직거래하다) to act as a verb.

structuredNuance.t: '직거래'는 중개나 택배 없이 사는 사람과 파는 사람이 직접 만나 물건과 돈을 주고받는 걸 뜻해요. 안전을 위해 사람 많은 지하철역·편의점 앞에서 만나는 게 보통이고, 멀면 '택배 거래'를 해요.
헷갈리기 쉬운 짝은 발음이 비슷한 '직구'(直購, 직접 구매)인데, '직구'는 해외 사이트에서 중간상 없이 사들이는 해외 직접구매고, '직거래'는 보통 국내 중고 거래에서 얼굴 보고 만나는 방식이에요 — 하나는 해외 온라인, 하나는 국내 대면이라 방향이 정반대입니다.
'직거래' 直去來 는 한자로 '곧바로(直) 오가며(去來) 거래한다'예요.
영어 화자가 자주 빠지는 함정은 'direct'를 '직접 깎아 주는 직거래가니까 싸다'처럼 가격 개념으로 오해하는 것인데, 직거래는 가격이 아니라 '거래 방식'(대면)을 가리킵니다.

extendedVocab.english: (user) review / write-up after using a product
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 후기 means "(user) review / write-up after using a product" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "(user) review / write-up after using a product" is 후기 (hugi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 후기를 보다 ("to read reviews"). Watch the particle attached to 후기 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 보다 (read/look at) is the verb for consuming reviews before buying
남기다 (leave behind) is the idiomatic verb for posting one
shorthand for a product being highly rated
솔직 = candid; a buzzword promising no sugar-coating

examples.en: Are the reviews good?
examples.note: beginner: 후기 + 좋다, the fastest way to ask if something's worth buying

examples.en: From the reviews, it runs small.
examples.note: everyday: 후기 보니까 = judging from the reviews; -대요 relays what they say

examples.ko: 후기 남기면 적립금 준대서 하나 썼어요.
examples.romanization: hugi namgimyeon jeongnipgeum jundaeseo hana sseosseoyo.
examples.en: They said they'd give points for a review, so I wrote one.
examples.note: real-situation: 남기다 for posting; -ㄴ대서 = because they said they would

extendedVocab.nuance: '후기' 後記 는 한자로 '나중에(後) 적은 글(記)', 곧 직접 써 보고 남기는 사용 후기/리뷰예요. 외래어 '리뷰'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 '후기'가 더 한국적이고 일상에서 흔하며, 식당·숙소·제품 어디에나 붙습니다. 짝을 이루는 말은 '별점'(star rating)이고, 진정성을 강조하는 '솔직 후기'·'내돈내산 후기'(내 돈으로 내가 산, 협찬 아님) 같은 표현이 인기예요. 핵심 함정은 시점: '후기'의 '후'가 '나중/이후'라서 반드시 경험한 뒤에 쓰는 글이며, 사기 전 기대나 계획을 '후기'라 부르면 안 됩니다(그건 그냥 '후기'가 아니에요). 또 영어 화자는 동사로 '후기를 쓰다'를 떠올리기 쉬운데, 더 자연스러운 짝은 '후기를 남기다'입니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 후기 for a future plan or pre-purchase expectation — the 後(after) in 후기 means it is strictly an after-the-fact write-up.
Defaulting to 후기를 쓰다 — it's understandable, but the idiomatic verb for posting one online is 후기를 남기다 (leave a review).
Treating 후기 and 예고/기대평 as interchangeable — 후기 is the experience report, not a preview or hype before use.

structuredNuance.t: '후기'는 직접 써 보고 남기는 사용 후기/리뷰예요. 짝을 이루는 말은 '별점'(star rating)이고, 진정성을 강조하는 '솔직 후기'·'내돈내산 후기'(내 돈으로 내가 산, 협찬 아님) 같은 표현이 인기예요.
외래어 '리뷰'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 '후기'가 더 한국적이고 일상에서 흔하며, 식당·숙소·제품 어디에나 붙습니다.
'후기' 後記 는 한자로 '나중에(後) 적은 글(記)'이에요.
핵심 함정은 시점: '후기'의 '후'가 '나중/이후'라서 반드시 경험한 뒤에 쓰는 글이며, 사기 전 기대나 계획을 '후기'라 부르면 안 됩니다. 또 영어 화자는 동사로 '후기를 쓰다'를 떠올리기 쉬운데, 더 자연스러운 짝은 '후기를 남기다'입니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 결제 means "payment / checkout (completing a purchase)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 결제 (gyeolje) = "payment / checkout (completing a purchase)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 결제하다 ("to pay / check out") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 결제, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 결제 is Sino-Korean and takes 하다 to become a verb
안 되다 = fails to process; a frequent checkout error
수단 = means; card, transfer, simple-pay, etc.
간편 = easy; 카카오페이·네이버페이-style PIN payments

examples.en: I've finished paying.
examples.note: beginner: 결제하다 in the past, confirming checkout is done

examples.en: I'm trying to pay by card but an error keeps popping up.
examples.note: everyday: 오류가 뜨다 = an error pops up on screen

examples.ko: 결제는 했는데 아직 배송 준비 중이래요.
examples.romanization: gyeoljeneun haenneunde ajik baesong junbi jungiraeyo.
examples.en: I've paid but they say it's still being prepared for shipping.
examples.note: real-situation: shows the 결제 → 배송 sequence; -대요 relays the status

extendedVocab.nuance: '결제' 決濟 는 한자로 '셈을 매듭지어(決) 치르다(濟)', 곧 돈을 실제로 내어 거래를 끝맺는 과정 전체를 말해요. 가장 가까운 혼동어가 둘 있습니다. 첫째 '계산': 오프라인 계산대에서 값을 치를 땐 '계산'을 많이 쓰지만, 온라인·카드·앱 맥락에서는 '결제'가 기본입니다. 둘째이자 더 위험한 것은 동음이의 '결재' 決裁 — 이건 상사가 서류를 '승인/재가'한다는 완전히 다른 단어라, 쇼핑 글에서 '결재'로 쓰면 틀립니다(받침 ㅔ vs ㅐ 주의). 한국에서는 '간편결제'(카카오페이·네이버페이 등)가 거의 필수라 꼭 알아 두세요. 영어 화자의 함정은 pay를 그냥 '내다'로만 옮겨 '돈을 내다'에 머무는 것인데, 체크아웃 단계 전체는 '결제하다'가 가장 정확합니다. 발음은 [결쩨].
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Spelling it 결재 — 결재 means a manager's sign-off/approval (a document being authorized), a completely different word from 결제 (payment).
Confusing 결제 with 계산 — 계산 leans offline/in-store; for app and card payments use 결제.
Stopping at 돈을 내다 for online checkout — 결제하다 is the precise verb for finalizing a purchase, errors and all.

structuredNuance.t: '결제'는 돈을 실제로 내어 거래를 끝맺는 과정 전체를 말해요. 한국에서는 '간편결제'(카카오페이·네이버페이 등)가 거의 필수라 꼭 알아 두세요. 발음은 [결쩨].
가장 가까운 혼동어가 둘 있습니다. 첫째 '계산': 오프라인 계산대에서 값을 치를 땐 '계산'을 많이 쓰지만, 온라인·카드·앱 맥락에서는 '결제'가 기본입니다. 둘째이자 더 위험한 것은 동음이의 '결재' 決裁 — 이건 상사가 서류를 '승인/재가'한다는 완전히 다른 단어라, 쇼핑 글에서 '결재'로 쓰면 틀립니다(받침 ㅔ vs ㅐ 주의).
'결제' 決濟 는 한자로 '셈을 매듭지어(決) 치르다(濟)'예요.
pay를 그냥 '내다'로만 옮겨 '돈을 내다'에 머무는 것인데, 체크아웃 단계 전체는 '결제하다'가 가장 정확합니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 정품 means "genuine / authentic product (not a fake)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 정품 (jeongpum) means "genuine / authentic product (not a fake)". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 정품이다 ("to be genuine"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 정품 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: the basic noun + 이다 assertion of authenticity
인증 = certification; proof a brand item is real
맞다 = to be correct/right; the question buyers ask sellers
보장 = guarantee; a seller's promise

examples.en: Is this genuine?
examples.note: beginner: 정품 + 이다 question, the core authenticity check

examples.en: The price is so cheap I doubt it's authentic.
examples.note: everyday: 정품인지 의심되다 = suspect it might not be real

examples.en: I bought it because they said it was genuine, but it turned out to be a fake.
examples.note: real-situation: 정품 vs 짝퉁 contrast; -라길래 = because (they) said it was

extendedVocab.nuance: '정품' 正品 은 한자로 '바른(正) 물건(品)', 곧 가짜가 아닌 진짜 정식 제품을 뜻해요. 직접적인 반대말은 '짝퉁'(구어, 가짜)이며 격식체로는 '가품'(假品)·'위조품'이라 합니다. 헷갈리기 쉬운 짝이 둘 있어요. (1) 발음이 비슷한 '정가'(正價, the list/retail price): 하나는 진품 여부, 다른 하나는 정해진 가격이라 뜻이 전혀 다릅니다. (2) '진품'(眞品): '진품'은 주로 미술품·골동품이 진짜라는 맥락에 쓰고, 시중 브랜드 상품의 진위에는 '정품'이 자연스러워요. 명품·전자기기를 중고로 살 때 '정품 맞아요?', '정품 인증해 주세요'를 거의 반드시 묻습니다. 영어 화자의 함정은 genuine을 막연히 '진짜'로만 옮겨 '진짜예요?'라고 묻는 것인데, 상거래에서는 '정품이에요?'가 의도를 더 정확히 전달해요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 정품 (authentic product) with 정가 (the fixed retail price) — they sound alike but one is about realness, the other about price.
Using 진품 for retail goods — 진품 fits art/antiques being real; for brand-name market items the natural word is 정품.
Asking only 진짜예요? when you mean 'is it authentic?' — in a buying context 정품이에요? is the precise question.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 중고 means "used / secondhand (goods)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "used / secondhand (goods)" is 중고 (junggo). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 중고로 사다 ("to buy secondhand"). Watch the particle attached to 중고 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: -로 marks the condition/route the item comes in
거래 = transaction; the whole used-market activity
중고 attaches directly in front of a noun (중고차, 중고폰)

usagePhrases.en: for a used item / considering it's used
usagePhrases.note: -치고 = 'for a ...', sets a lenient standard

examples.en: This is secondhand.
examples.note: beginner: 중고 + 이다, plainly stating the condition

examples.en: New ones are expensive so I bought it secondhand.
examples.note: everyday: 중고로 사다 vs 새것; the core reason people go used

examples.en: For a used item, the condition is really clean.
examples.note: real-situation: 중고치고는 = considering it's used, it exceeds expectations

extendedVocab.nuance: '중고' 中古 는 한자로 '가운데쯤(中) 오래된(古)', 곧 한 번 이상 쓰인 물건을 말해요. 명확한 반대말은 '새것/새 상품'이고, 거의 안 쓴 물건은 'S급'이나 '미개봉'(unopened)으로 따로 표시합니다. 핵심 문법 함정은 품사: '중고'는 명사라서 형용사처럼 활용하지 않아요 — '중고하다'(X)는 없고, '중고로 사다'·'중고 물건'·'중고폰'처럼 명사 앞이나 조사 -로와 함께 씁니다. 또 발음·표기가 비슷한 '중간'(中間, middle)과 헷갈리지 마세요. 한국은 당근마켓·중고나라 등 중고 거래 문화가 매우 활발해 '중고 거래'라는 말이 일상적이며, 영어의 'second hand'를 직역해 두 단어로 떼어 쓰거나 '두 번째 손'식으로 풀어 말하면 어색합니다 — 그냥 명사 '중고' 한 단어예요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Treating 중고 as a verb/adjective that conjugates — it's a noun; say 중고로 사다 or 중고 물건, never 중고하다.
Confusing 중고 (secondhand) with 중간 (middle) — different words despite both starting with 中(중).
Splitting or literalizing 'second hand' — Korean uses the single noun 중고, not a two-word or 'second hand' calque.

발음·표기가 비슷한 '중간'(中間, middle)과 헷갈리지 마세요.
'중고' 中古 는 한자로 '가운데쯤(中) 오래된(古)'이에요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 쿠폰 means "coupon (discount voucher)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 쿠폰 (kupon) = "coupon (discount voucher)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 쿠폰을 쓰다 ("to use a coupon") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 쿠폰, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 쓰다 = apply/use it at the buying moment
적용 = application; the actual checkout step that activates it
the separate first step of getting it to your account
할인 = discount; the most common type of coupon

examples.en: I have a coupon.
examples.note: beginner: 쿠폰 + 있다, the simplest way to say you've got one

examples.en: After applying the coupon it got 5,000 won cheaper.
examples.note: everyday: 쿠폰 적용하다 → 싸지다; -았더니 = once I did X, then Y happened

examples.ko: 쿠폰 다운받는 거 깜빡해서 그냥 결제했어요.
examples.romanization: kupon daunbanneun geo kkamppakaeseo geunyang gyeoljehaesseoyo.
examples.en: I forgot to download the coupon and just checked out.
examples.note: real-situation: a common regret; claiming and applying are separate

extendedVocab.nuance: '쿠폰'은 영어 coupon에서 온 외래어로, 가격을 그 자리에서 깎아 주는 할인권이에요. 반드시 구별할 짝은 '적립'(포인트 쌓기): 쿠폰은 지금 결제에서 즉시 값을 깎지만, 적립은 나중에 쓸 포인트를 모아 두는 거라 효과 시점이 정반대입니다. 또 '쿠폰'은 깎아 주는 '권리/수단'이고, 그렇게 실제로 깎인 액수는 '할인'이라 층위가 달라요. 한국 앱의 핵심 함정은 절차가 두 단계라는 점 — 먼저 '쿠폰 다운받기/받기'(claim)로 내 계정에 담고, 결제 화면에서 '쿠폰 적용'(apply)을 눌러야 비로소 깎입니다. 받기만 하고 적용을 깜빡하면 할인이 안 돼요. 영어 화자는 'I have a coupon'처럼 받은 것만으로 끝났다고 생각하기 쉬운데, 적용 버튼까지 눌러야 실제 할인이 들어갑니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Forgetting that claiming (받다/다운받다) and applying (적용) a coupon are two separate steps — having it isn't using it.
Mixing up 쿠폰 (instant discount voucher) with 적립금/포인트 (saved-up points for later) — opposite timing of the benefit.
Saying 쿠폰을 적립하다 — you 쿠폰을 받다/적용하다; 적립 is for points, not coupons.

반드시 구별할 짝은 '적립'(포인트 쌓기): 쿠폰은 지금 결제에서 즉시 값을 깎지만, 적립은 나중에 쓸 포인트를 모아 두는 거라 효과 시점이 정반대입니다. 또 '쿠폰'은 깎아 주는 '권리/수단'이고, 그렇게 실제로 깎인 액수는 '할인'이라 층위가 달라요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 내성적이다 means "introverted" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 내성적이다 (naeseongjeogida) means "introverted". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 내성적인 성격 ("an introverted personality"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 내성적이다 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 성격 (personality) is the noun it pairs with most
-(이)라서 gives a reason off a 이다-adjective

usagePhrases.en: I'd say I'm on the introverted side
usagePhrases.note: -(으)ㄴ 편이다 hedges instead of stating it flatly
Habitually chained with 조용하다 in self-descriptions

examples.en: I'm a bit introverted.
examples.note: Add 좀 to soften a self-label; note the form is 내성적이에요, not 내성적해요

examples.ko: 저는 내성적이라서 처음 보는 사람이랑 말하는 게 어려워요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun naeseongjeogiraseo cheoeum boneun saramirang malhaneun ge eoryeowoyo.
examples.en: I'm introverted, so talking to people I'm meeting for the first time is hard.
examples.note: -(이)라서 links the trait to its everyday consequence

examples.ko: 걔는 내성적이지만 친해지면 말이 엄청 많아.
examples.romanization: gyaeneun naeseongjeogijiman chinhaejimyeon mari eomcheong mana.
examples.en: He's introverted, but once you get close he talks a ton.
examples.note: 걔 + banmal among friends; -지만 sets up the contrast

extendedVocab.nuance: 내성적이다 is the neutral, textbook word for 'introverted' and is completely safe to say about yourself in interviews or first meetings — Koreans read it as a temperament, not a flaw. It is Sino-Korean: 內省的 (內 inner + 省 to reflect/introspect), literally 'inward-reflecting type', so it points to drawing energy inward rather than to being unfriendly. The key contrast is with 소심하다 (timid), which adds a negative 'holds back out of fear' edge, and with 조용하다 (quiet), which is only about low volume; an introvert can be talkative once comfortable. It collocates with 성격, 사람, and the hedge -(으)ㄴ 편이다. The pitfall for English speakers is the conjugation: because the stem already ends in 이다, you say 내성적이에요 / 내성적인, never the 하다-style 내성적해요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 내성적해요 — there is no 하다 here; the stem is 내성적이다, so it conjugates as 내성적이에요 / 내성적인
Treating it as a synonym of 소심하다 — 내성적 is just inward-facing and value-neutral, while 소심하다 implies timid, fearful holding-back
Using it to mean merely 'quiet' (조용하다) — composure and volume are separate; 내성적 is about where you get your energy

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 외향적이다 means "extroverted, outgoing" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "extroverted, outgoing" is 외향적이다 (oehyangjeogida). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 외향적인 성격 ("an outgoing personality"). Watch the particle attached to 외향적이다 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Direct opposite of 내성적인 성격
-(이)라서 gives the reason off 이다
외향적으로 + 변하다 = change in that direction
-(으)ㄴ 편이다 to hedge rather than declare

examples.en: I'm outgoing.
examples.note: Basic self-intro; the form is 외향적이에요, never 외향적해요

examples.ko: 저는 외향적이라서 새 친구 사귀는 게 좋아요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun oehyangjeogiraseo sae chingu sagwineun ge joayo.
examples.en: I'm outgoing, so I enjoy making new friends.
examples.note: 친구를 사귀다 = make friends; -(이)라서 ties trait to behavior

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 진짜 외향적이라서 회식 때 분위기를 다 살려요.
examples.romanization: uri timjangnimeun jinjja oehyangjeogiraseo hoesik ttae bunwigireul da sallyeoyo.
examples.en: Our team lead is super outgoing, so they liven up the whole mood at company dinners.
examples.note: 분위기를 살리다 = liven up the mood; a 회식 staple scene

extendedVocab.nuance: 외향적이다 is the standard, positive-leaning term for 'extroverted' and is woven into MBTI chat, which is hugely popular in Korea — you will constantly hear 'E야 I야?' (Are you an E or an I?). It is Sino-Korean: 外向的 (外 outside + 向 to face/turn toward), literally 'outward-facing type', describing where someone aims their energy. The sharp contrast is with 활발하다: 외향적이다 names the inner trait, while 활발하다 describes the visible liveliness you can see in a room — an extrovert who happens to be tired won't look 활발한 at that moment. It pairs with 성격, the verb 변하다 (외향적으로 변하다), and the hedge -(으)ㄴ 편이다. The English-speaker trap is twofold: don't add 하다 (it's 외향적이에요 / 외향적인), and don't swap in the noun 외향성 (extroversion) where the adjective belongs — say 외향적이에요, not 외향성이에요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing 외향적해요 — correct forms are 외향적이에요 / 외향적인, because the stem ends in 이다
Using the noun 외향성 (extroversion) as if it were the adjective — to describe a person, use 외향적이다
Equating it with 활발하다 — 외향적 is the trait, 활발 is the observable energy, and they don't always coincide

Using it for 'neat/clean' — that is 깔끔하다; 꼼꼼하다 is about thoroughness, not tidiness
Adding a particle to the adverb: it's 꼼꼼하게 / 꼼꼼히, never 꼼꼼하게로

Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

Neutral-to-slightly-negative about a person
Also used for skin, allergies, stomach, sleep
예민하게 굴다 = act oversensitive

examples.en: I'm a bit on edge lately.
examples.note: A quick, very natural heads-up to a friend; banmal

examples.ko: 시험 기간이라 요즘 예민하니까 이해해 줘.
examples.romanization: siheom giganira yojeum yeminhanikka ihaehae jwo.
examples.en: It's exam season so I'm on edge — please bear with me.
examples.note: -(으)니까 gives the reason for asking forbearance

examples.ko: 저는 잠귀가 예민해서 작은 소리에도 깨요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun jamgwiga yeminhaeseo jageun soriedo kkaeyo.

examples.note: 잠귀가 예민하다 = sensitive ears while sleeping; the physical sense

extendedVocab.nuance: 예민하다 covers two strands: a person being emotionally on-edge, touchy, or easily set off (usually from stress), and physical sensitivity — 피부 (skin), 잠귀 (sleep), 속/위 (stomach). It is Sino-Korean: 銳敏 (銳 sharp + 敏 quick/keen), literally 'sharply keen', which is why it reaches into both perception and temper. About someone's mood it can sound mildly critical, so people most often apply it to themselves as a pre-emptive warning. The English trap is assuming 'sensitive = caring/tender'; for a gently sensitive, easily-moved heart, Koreans say 섬세하다, not 예민하다.

Reaching for 예민하다 to praise a kind, tender person — that warmer 'sensitive' is 섬세하다; 예민하다 leans toward irritable/on-edge
Swapping it freely with 민감하다 — for sensitive topics/data/markets use 민감하다; for a person's frayed mood use 예민하다
Confusing it with 예리하다 (sharp-minded/incisive); a 예민한 person is touchy, a 예리한 person is perceptive

extendedVocab.explanation: "blunt, curt, gruff (cold-seeming manner)" is 무뚝뚝하다 (muttukttukada). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 무뚝뚝하게 말하다 ("speak curtly"). usagePhrases.note: Describes a flat, short-spoken delivery
Often softened with 그래도 (but still…)
겉으로는 = on the outside, sets up a 'but inside…' turn
-아/어 보이다 = looks/seems

examples.en: My dad is kind of gruff.
examples.note: A stock, affectionate description of Korean fathers; banmal

examples.ko: 사장님이 무뚝뚝하게 대답해서 화난 줄 알았어요.
examples.romanization: sajangnimi muttukttukage daedapaeseo hwanan jul arasseoyo.
examples.en: The boss answered so curtly that I thought he was angry.
examples.note: -(으)ㄴ 줄 알았다 = mistakenly thought that…

examples.ko: 우리 아빠는 무뚝뚝하지만 속은 정말 따뜻해요.
examples.romanization: uri appaneun muttukttukajiman sogeun jeongmal ttatteutaeyo.

examples.note: 속은 따뜻하다 = warm inside; the classic redeeming-turn collocation

extendedVocab.nuance: 무뚝뚝하다 is native Korean describing a curt, unexpressive manner — short answers, no small talk, a flat face — without necessarily meaning the person is unkind. It is so reliably paired with 속은 따뜻하다 ('warm inside') that the 'gruff exterior, warm interior' arc is almost a cultural template for dads, older men, and Gyeongsang-do speakers. The crucial contrast is with 차갑다 (cold-hearted): 차갑다 implies the person actually is cold toward you, while 무뚝뚝하다 is only about an undemonstrative style — the feeling underneath may be perfectly warm. It also differs from 무례하다 (rude), which is a breach of manners; a 무뚝뚝한 person follows etiquette, they just don't decorate it with warmth. The English-speaker pitfalls are two: spelling (the syllable doubles — 무뚝뚝하다, not 무뚝하다), and resisting the instinct to read curtness as hostility, since Koreans hear it as personality, not an insult.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Dropping a syllable as 무뚝하다 — the word reduplicates: 무뚝뚝하다
Using it to mean 'rude' — that is 무례하다; 무뚝뚝하다 is about flat affect, not bad manners
Equating it with 차갑다 (cold-hearted) — 무뚝뚝하다 is just an unexpressive style and often coexists with real warmth

usagePhrases.en: have a warm way of speaking
usagePhrases.note: 말투 = tone/manner of speech

examples.en: You're so sweet.
examples.note: A warm, direct compliment to a friend; banmal

examples.ko: 선생님이 다정하게 말해 줘서 긴장이 풀렸어요.
examples.romanization: seonsaengnimi dajeonghage malhae jwoseo ginjangi pullyeosseoyo.
examples.en: The teacher spoke to me so warmly that my nerves eased.
examples.note: 긴장이 풀리다 = tension eases; 다정하게 modifies how they spoke

examples.ko: 남자친구가 너무 다정해서 친구들이 다 부러워해요.

examples.note: 부러워하다 = be envious; a real-life relationship boast

extendedVocab.nuance: 다정하다 means warm, tender, and affectionate toward others — it is about emotional closeness and sweet treatment, which makes it the go-to compliment for partners, dear friends, and beloved teachers. It is Sino-Korean at the root: 多情 (多 many + 情 affection/feeling), literally 'much feeling', i.e. full of warmth. The dividing line that matters is with 친절하다 (kind/polite): 친절하다 is the right word for staff being helpful to a customer or a stranger giving directions — courteous service — whereas 다정하다 implies real, personal warmth, so it sounds slightly off for a one-time formal exchange. The expanded 다정다감하다 is a touch more literary but common in praise. The English trap is mapping 'nice/friendly' onto 다정하다 across the board: a cashier being pleasant is 친절한, not 다정한, and reserving 다정하다 for genuine warmth is what keeps it from sounding strange.

Using 다정하다 for polite service — staff being helpful to customers is 친절하다, not 다정하다
Applying it to a one-time formal stranger — it implies real intimacy, so it rings false there; use 친절하다
Confusing the adverb target: 다정하게 modifies how you treat/speak to someone (다정하게 대하다), so anchor it to a verb

usagePhrases.note: 오늘따라 = unusually today
까칠하게 굴다 = behave in a prickly way
The original literal sense: rough to the touch

examples.en: Why are you so snippy?
examples.note: Casual concern between friends; banmal

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님 평소엔 괜찮은데 마감 때만 까칠해져요.
examples.romanization: uri timjangnim pyeongsoen gwaenchaneunde magam ttaeman kkachilhaejyeoyo.

examples.ko: 그 사람 까칠해 보여도 알고 보면 착해요.

extendedVocab.nuance: 까칠하다 literally means 'rough to the touch' (you'll still hear 피부가 까칠하다 for dry, stubbly skin) and figuratively describes someone snippy, easily irritated, or hard to please. Crucially it is fairly light and even playful — friends tease each other with it — so it is nowhere near a serious insult; for genuinely mean or nasty, Koreans say 못됐다. The contrast learners most need is with 까다롭다: 까다롭다 is about high, demanding standards (a 까다로운 손님 sends the dish back because it doesn't meet their bar), while 까칠하다 is about mood and attitude (a 까칠한 사람 is touchy and short with you regardless of standards). usagePhrases.note: Mildly self-deprecating self-intro
Carries a slightly negative nuance
Encouraging a friend to speak up
Beloved set phrase for small, harmless payback

examples.en: I'm a bit timid.

examples.en: Don't be timid, just ask!
examples.note: A friendly push to be bolder; 굴다 = behave/act

examples.ko: 지각한 동료 자리에 몰래 포스트잇 붙였어. 소심한 복수지.

extendedVocab.nuance: 소심하다 means timid, fainthearted, or easily intimidated — and unlike the neutral 내성적이다 ('introverted'), it leans negative, implying you hold back when you really shouldn't (can't send back a wrong dish, can't speak up in a meeting). It is Sino-Korean: 小心 (小 small + 心 heart), literally 'small-hearted'. Beware a false-friend trap here: the Chinese 小心 means 'be careful', but in Korean 소심하다 does NOT mean careful — it means timid; the 'careful/prudent' meaning belongs to 신중하다. The sharp contrast with 내성적이다 is the whole point: an introvert simply recharges alone, while a 소심한 person shrinks back out of fear, so the two are not interchangeable. The much-loved set phrase 소심한 복수 ('petty revenge') is everywhere. The English-speaker pitfall, beyond the false friend, is using it as an interview 'strength' — it sounds self-critical, so pick 신중하다 (prudent) instead.

usagePhrases.en: take it easy, relax one's mind
usagePhrases.note: Set phrase: 마음을 ~게 먹다

examples.en: There's no rush, so take your time.
examples.note: 급하다 = be in a hurry; a reassuring, soothing tone

examples.ko: 저는 성격이 느긋해서 웬만한 일에는 스트레스를 안 받아요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun seonggyeogi neugeutaeseo wenmanhan ireneun seuteureseureul an badayo.
examples.en: I'm laid-back, so most things don't stress me out.
examples.note: 웬만한 = most ordinary; 스트레스 받다 = get stressed

examples.ko: 휴가 때는 느긋하게 늦잠도 자고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: hyuga ttaeneun neugeutage neutjamdo jago sipeoyo.
examples.en: On vacation I want to sleep in and just take it easy.
examples.note: 늦잠 자다 = sleep in; 느긋하게 colors the whole leisure scene

extendedVocab.nuance: 느긋하다 is native Korean for the positive flavor of 'laid-back' — calm, unbothered, and not easily rushed — and it works both for a person's temperament (성격이 느긋하다) and for relaxed stretches of time (느긋한 아침, 느긋한 주말). Its natural antonym is 급하다 (impatient/hasty), and the two are often set against each other. Two contrasts keep it precise. With 여유롭다 (which overlaps), 느긋하다 is about an unhurried temperament, while 여유롭다 leans toward having actual leeway — of time, space, or means (마음의 여유, 시간 여유); you can feel 느긋한 even when you're not objectively 여유로운. With 게으르다 (lazy), the difference is intent: 느긋하다 is unhurried by choice and still gets things done, whereas 게으르다 is an unwillingness to work — calling a relaxed person 게으른 is an insult, not a description. The English-speaker pitfall is exactly that lazy/laid-back slip, plus the conjugation: it's a regular 하다-stem, so 느긋해요 / 느긋한, never 느긋어요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing it with 게으르다 (lazy) — 느긋하다 is unhurried by choice and still productive, not unwilling to work
Using it interchangeably with 여유롭다 — 여유롭다 stresses having leeway (time/means); 느긋하다 stresses an unhurried temperament
Mis-conjugating as 느긋어요 — it's a 하다-adjective: 느긋해요 / 느긋한

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 활발하다 means "lively, energetic, sociable" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 활발하다 (hwalbalhada) means "lively, energetic, sociable". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 성격이 활발하다 ("have a lively personality"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 활발하다 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Common positive description
활발하게 + 활동하다 in clubs, work
Frequent for children
Also describes a room, class, or chat

examples.en: That kid is really lively.
examples.note: A warm remark watching an energetic child; 활발하다 about visible energy

examples.ko: 새로 온 인턴이 성격이 활발해서 금방 다 친해졌어요.
examples.romanization: saero on inteoni seonggyeogi hwalbalhaeseo geumbang da chinhaejyeosseoyo.
examples.en: The new intern is so lively that everyone got close fast.
examples.note: 금방 = quickly; 친해지다 = get close

examples.ko: 동아리에서 활발하게 활동하면 친구를 많이 사귈 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: dongarieseo hwalbalhage hwaldonghamyeon chingureul mani sagwil su isseoyo.
examples.en: If you're active in a club, you can make lots of friends.
examples.note: 동아리 = club; 활발하게 활동하다 is a fixed pairing

extendedVocab.nuance: 활발하다 describes lively, energetic, sociable behavior — it's how you praise someone bright and engaged in groups, and it stretches naturally to atmospheres and activities (활발한 토론 = a lively debate, 분위기가 활발하다 = the vibe is lively). It is Sino-Korean: 活潑 (活 alive + 潑 to splash/be spirited), literally 'alive and splashing', a vivid image of bubbling energy. The contrast that matters is with 외향적이다: 외향적이다 names the inner MBTI-style trait (where you draw energy), while 활발하다 names the observable liveliness in the moment — a true extrovert who's exhausted simply won't look 활발한 right then, and a normally reserved person can be 활발한 at a party they love. It's almost always a compliment about people. The English-speaker pitfall is using it as a flat synonym for 'outgoing/extroverted'; reserve 활발하다 for visible energy and motion, and don't attach it to calm, inanimate things, where it sounds wrong.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using it as a pure synonym for 외향적이다 — 활발하다 is observable energy, not the underlying personality trait
Applying it to calm, inanimate things — it implies motion and liveliness, so it sounds off there
Forgetting it covers atmospheres too — 분위기가 활발하다 / 활발한 토론 are natural, not just people

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 차분하다 means "calm, composed, level-headed" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "calm, composed, level-headed" is 차분하다 (chabunhada). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 성격이 차분하다 ("have a calm temperament"). Watch the particle attached to 차분하다 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Positive, mature impression
차분하게 = composedly
-아/어지다 = become
Often praised in high-pressure jobs

examples.en: You have such a calm voice.
examples.note: A polite compliment using honorific -(으)시-; about composure, not volume

examples.ko: 차 한 잔 마시니까 마음이 좀 차분해졌어요.
examples.romanization: cha han jan masinikka maeumi jom chabunhaejyeosseoyo.
examples.en: After a cup of tea my mind calmed down a bit.
examples.note: -(으)니까 marks the natural cause; 차분해지다 = grow calm

examples.ko: 급한 상황에서도 차분하게 대처해서 다들 놀랐어요.
examples.romanization: geupan sanghwangeseodo chabunhage daecheohaeseo dadeul nollasseoyo.
examples.en: Even in an urgent situation they handled it calmly, so everyone was impressed.
examples.note: 대처하다 = handle/respond to; a strong interview-worthy trait

extendedVocab.nuance: 차분하다 is native Korean for calm, composed, and steady — a person who doesn't get rattled, or a quiet, settled mood. It is a strong compliment, especially for keeping your head under pressure (차분하게 대처하다), which makes it an excellent trait to claim in interviews. It commonly takes -아/어지다 to mark a shift into calm (마음이 차분해지다). The contrast learners need most is with 조용하다 (quiet): 조용하다 is about low sound/volume — a quiet room or a person who simply doesn't talk much — while 차분하다 is about inner composure and temperament; someone can speak up plenty and still be 차분한. It also sits opposite 예민하다 (on-edge) and 급하다 (hasty). The English-speaker pitfalls are mapping 'calm = quiet' onto it (they diverge — composure vs. volume) and the conjugation: it's a regular 하다-adjective, so 차분해요 / 차분한, never the doubled 차분하해요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing it with 조용하다 (quiet) — 차분하다 is composure/temperament, not just low volume; a talkative person can still be 차분한
Writing 차분하해요 — the stem is 차분하다, so it's 차분해요 / 차분한
Limiting it to mood — it also describes a steady manner under pressure (차분하게 대처하다), a prime interview strength

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 무심하다 means "indifferent, aloof, inattentive" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 무심하다 (musimhada) = "indifferent, aloof, inattentive". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 무심한 성격 ("an aloof, inattentive nature") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 무심하다, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Not noticing details or others' moods
무심하게 = without thinking much of it

usagePhrases.en: look after someone in a low-key way
usagePhrases.note: Trendy phrase: aloof on the surface, caring underneath
남한테 = toward other people

examples.en: My husband is kind of inattentive.
examples.note: An extremely common, half-joking relationship complaint

examples.en: I got hurt by something my friend said offhandedly.
examples.note: 무심하게 던진 말 = a careless, throwaway remark

examples.ko: 그 선배는 무심한 듯 챙겨 줘서 인기가 많아요.
examples.romanization: geu seonbaeneun musimhan deut chaenggyeo jwoseo ingiga manayo.
examples.en: That senior looks aloof but quietly looks out for people, so they're popular.
examples.note: 무심한 듯 챙기다 = the beloved 'cold but caring' type

extendedVocab.nuance: 무심하다 means indifferent, aloof, or simply not paying attention to others' feelings and small changes — it's the stock (half-joking) complaint about a partner who never notices a new haircut. It is Sino-Korean: 無心 (無 without + 心 heart/mind), literally 'without mind/heart', i.e. not having one's attention on something. Importantly it is gentler than 차갑다 (cold-hearted): a 무심한 person may genuinely care but just fails to show it or notice, whereas 차갑다 implies real emotional coldness toward you — which is exactly why the trendy praise 무심한 듯 챙기다 ('caring in a seemingly indifferent way') works. The other contrast is 무관심하다 (無關心, 'no interest'), which is stronger and usually aimed at topics or matters (정치에 무관심하다 = uninterested in politics), while 무심하다 is about a person's inattentive disposition toward people. The English-speaker pitfall is sliding to 'cold' or 'doesn't care at all'; 무심하다 is closer to 'doesn't notice / doesn't show it' than to genuine coldness or total disinterest.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 무심하다 (inattentive/aloof) with 무관심하다 — 무관심하다 is stronger 'totally uninterested', usually about a topic
Equating it with 차갑다 (cold-hearted) — 무심하다 is about not noticing/showing, not about being emotionally cold
Reading it as 'doesn't care at all' — a 무심한 person often does care; they just don't express or register it (hence 무심한 듯 챙기다)

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 진통제 means "painkiller" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 진통제 (jintongje) means "painkiller". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 진통제 주세요 ("Please give me a painkiller"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 진통제 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: The standard pharmacy request; add 한 통 for a whole box or 한 알 for a single tablet
Oral meds always pair with 먹다, never 마시다 even though English says 'take'
센 is the natural everyday adjective for potency here; 강한 sounds stiff and technical
효과가 있다 = it works; 효과가 빠르다 = it kicks in fast

examples.en: Please give me one painkiller.
examples.note: Simplest counter form: 한 알 = one tablet, with 알 the counter for pills

examples.en: My head hurts so much, do you have any painkillers?
examples.note: Everyday opener at a 약국; -은데 softly sets up the request

examples.ko: 생리통이 심해서 진통제 두 알 먹었는데도 안 나아요.
examples.romanization: saengnitongi simhaeseo jintongje du al meogeonneundedo an naayo.
examples.en: My cramps are bad so I took two painkillers but it's still not better.
examples.note: Real-situation: -는데도 = 'even though'; 안 나아요 = doesn't get better

extendedVocab.nuance: 진통제 is the everyday word for any pain-relief pill — headache, cramps, muscle ache — and a pharmacist understands it instantly. The hanja is 鎭痛劑 'suppress-pain-agent': 鎭 calm/suppress, 痛 pain, 劑 a prepared dose, the same 劑 that marks 해열제 and 소화제. The dividing line you must learn is 진통제 (relieves the pain itself) versus 해열제 (lowers a fever); many products do both, but the words name different jobs, so don't treat them as synonyms. Register is fully neutral — kids, grandparents and pharmacists all use it — though in casual speech people often just say the brand 타이레놀. The classic English-speaker pitfall is the verb: English 'take a pill' tempts learners into 마시다 or even 가지다, but a pill is always 먹다 (literally 'eat'), and you count it with 알, not 개.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 진통제 마셔요 — a pill is 먹다 (eat/take), not 마시다 (drink), regardless of the English 'take'
Treating 진통제 and 해열제 as the same word — 진통제 targets pain, 해열제 lowers fever; some products combine both but the terms are not interchangeable
Counting with 개: it should be 진통제 한 알, because 알 is the counter for tablets

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 소화제 means "digestive medicine (for indigestion)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "digestive medicine (for indigestion)" is 소화제 (sohwaje). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 소화제 주세요 ("Please give me some digestive medicine"). Watch the particle attached to 소화제 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.en: Please give me some digestive medicine
usagePhrases.note: The go-to request after a heavy meal
먹다 covers both the chewable tablets and the liquid bottles colloquially

usagePhrases.en: I bought digestive medicine because I couldn't digest
usagePhrases.note: 소화가 안 되다 = to have indigestion, the most natural framing

usagePhrases.en: a digestive medicine like Gas Hwalmyeongsu
usagePhrases.note: Names the famous liquid 소화제 brand pharmacists will recognize

examples.en: Please give me one digestive medicine.
examples.note: Simple counter: 하나 / 한 개 works for a bottle or sachet

examples.en: I overate so I took digestive medicine and lay down.
examples.note: Everyday cause-result: 과식하다 = to overeat

examples.ko: 체했는데 소화제 먹어도 속이 계속 더부룩해요.
examples.romanization: chehaenneunde sohwaje meogeodo sogi gyesok deoburukaeyo.
examples.en: I have an upset stomach and even after digestive medicine my belly still feels bloated.
examples.note: Real-situation: 체하다 = stomach 'blocked'; 더부룩하다 = bloated, the signature 소화제 symptom

extendedVocab.nuance: 소화제 is what you ask for after eating too much or when you feel 체했어요 (food 'stuck'), and it covers both chewable tablets and the popular liquid bottles like 까스활명수. The hanja is 消化劑 'dissolve-transform-agent': 消 to dissolve/dispel, 化 to change, 劑 a prepared dose — literally an 'agent that makes food break down'. The sharp contrast to memorize is 소화제 versus 위장약: 소화제 is narrowly for digestion after overeating, while 위장약 is the broader stomach medicine for acid, burning (속쓰림) and gastritis. The register is neutral and all-ages. The English-speaker pitfall is twofold: first, learners invent 소화약 by analogy with 감기약, but the correct, fixed form is 소화제 with the Sino-Korean -제 suffix; second, don't reach for 마시다 just because the liquid type is a drink — Koreans still say 소화제 먹다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 소화약 — the established word is 소화제 with the -제 (劑) suffix; only some medicines (감기약, 위장약) take native -약
Using 소화제 and 위장약 interchangeably — 소화제 is for digestion after overeating, 위장약 treats acid, burning and gastritis
Using 마시다 for the liquid bottle — even drinkable 소화제 pairs with 먹다 in normal speech

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 해열제 means "fever reducer" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 해열제 (haeyeolje) = "fever reducer". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 해열제 주세요 ("Please give me a fever reducer") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 해열제, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.en: Please give me a fever reducer
usagePhrases.note: The standard pharmacy request when running a fever

usagePhrases.en: to give a fever reducer (to someone)
usagePhrases.note: 먹이다 is the causative 'to feed/administer', used for a child or patient

usagePhrases.en: I had a fever so I took a fever reducer
usagePhrases.note: 열이 나다 = to run a fever, the set phrase
-용 (用) = 'for the use of'; ask this way for kids' doses

examples.en: Please give me a fever reducer.
examples.note: Simplest request; 좀 softens it politely

examples.en: My fever was over 38 degrees so I took a fever reducer.
examples.note: Everyday: Koreans cite 도 (Celsius degrees) for fever

examples.ko: 아이한테 해열제 먹였는데도 열이 안 떨어져요.
examples.romanization: aihante haeyeolje meogyeonneundedo yeori an tteoreojyeoyo.
examples.en: Even after I gave my child a fever reducer the fever won't come down.
examples.note: Real-situation: -한테 먹이다 = give meds to someone; 열이 떨어지다 = the fever drops

extendedVocab.nuance: 해열제 is the go-to word when 열이 나요 (you have a fever), and pharmacists grasp it at once. The hanja is 解熱劑 'release-heat-agent': 解 to loosen/release, 熱 heat/fever, 劑 a dose — so literally 'an agent that releases the body's heat'. The contrast to fix in your mind is 해열제 versus 감기약: 해열제 does one job, dropping a fever, while 감기약 is the umbrella cold remedy that bundles fever, runny nose and cough together; they overlap but are not the same word. Register is neutral, used at home and in clinics alike. A key pitfall is the verb shift when you dose someone else: you 먹다 medicine yourself, but you 먹이다 (causative) it to a child — English uses 'give' for both, so learners wrongly say 해열제 줬어요 when they mean they administered it. Also resist inventing 열약; the fixed term is 해열제.

Saying 열약 — the correct, fixed term is 해열제 (解熱劑)
Confusing 해열제 with 감기약 — 해열제 only lowers fever, while 감기약 is the broad cold remedy covering several symptoms
Using 해열제 줬어요 to mean you dosed a child — administering meds to someone is 먹이다 (먹였어요), not just 주다

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 감기약 means "cold medicine" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.

In Korean the particle or ending next to 감기약 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.en: Please give me some cold medicine
usagePhrases.note: The single most common pharmacy request for newcomers
먹다 covers both pills and the liquid sachets
Name your main symptom: 콧물 (runny nose) / 기침 (cough) / 목 (throat)
Pharmacists ask 졸린 거 vs 안 졸린 거 — drowsy vs non-drowsy

examples.en: Please give me cold medicine.
examples.note: Simplest form; just name the product so the pharmacist knows what you need

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있어서 감기약 사러 왔어요.
examples.romanization: gamgi giuni isseoseo gamgiyak sareo wasseoyo.
examples.en: I'm coming down with a cold so I came to buy cold medicine.
examples.note: Everyday: 감기 기운 = the onset/feeling of a cold, a very natural phrase

examples.ko: 일해야 해서 안 졸린 감기약으로 주세요.
examples.romanization: ilhaeya haeseo an jollin gamgiyageuro juseyo.
examples.en: I have to work, so please give me the non-drowsy cold medicine.
examples.note: Real-situation: -(으)로 주세요 = 'give me the one that is...', specifying a variant

extendedVocab.nuance: 감기약 is the umbrella term for cold remedies and the single most common thing a newcomer buys at a 약국. Note the formation: 감기 is Sino-Korean 感氣 'catch-air/energy' (the Korean concept of a cold as bad air entering the body), but the medicine takes the native suffix -약 ('medicine'), not the Sino-Korean -제 you see in 진통제·해열제·소화제 — so it is 감기약, never 감기제. The contrast worth knowing is 감기약 versus 해열제: 감기약 bundles several cold symptoms (fever, runny nose, cough) into one product, while 해열제 targets fever alone. Register is completely neutral and essential daily vocabulary. The pitfall: English speakers walk in and ask only for 약 ('medicine'), which tells the pharmacist nothing — always say 감기약 — and they forget that 감기약 varies a lot by symptom, so be ready to name 콧물, 기침 or 목.

Saying 감기제 by over-applying the -제 suffix — cold medicine takes native -약: 감기약
Asking only for 약 — the pharmacist needs 감기약 plus your symptom (콧물/기침/목) to choose correctly
Forgetting the drowsy/non-drowsy distinction — say 안 졸린 감기약 if you must drive or work

extendedVocab.explanation: "ointment / topical cream" is 연고 (yeongo). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 연고 주세요 ("Please give me some ointment"). Watch the particle attached to 연고 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: For cuts, burns, rashes and bites
바르다 'to spread/smear' is the fixed verb for creams and ointments

usagePhrases.en: I put ointment on the wound
usagePhrases.note: The spot takes the particle 에: 상처에 바르다
Name the target: 무좀 (athlete's foot), 안연고 (eye ointment)

examples.en: Please put some ointment on here.
examples.note: Simple request; 발라 주세요 = please apply it (for me)

examples.ko: 이 연고는 하루에 세 번 바르세요.
examples.romanization: i yeongoneun harue se beon bareuseyo.
examples.en: Apply this ointment three times a day.
examples.note: Everyday dosage phrasing: 하루에 세 번 = three times a day

examples.ko: 넘어져서 무릎 까졌는데 바르는 연고 있어요?
examples.romanization: neomeojyeoseo mureup kkajyeonneunde bareuneun yeongo isseoyo?
examples.en: I fell and scraped my knee — do you have an ointment to put on it?
examples.note: Real-situation: 까지다 = to get scraped; 바르는 연고 = the kind you apply

extendedVocab.nuance: 연고 covers any medicated cream or salve for the skin — cuts, burns, bug bites, rashes — and is Sino-Korean 軟膏 'soft-paste': 軟 soft, 膏 ointment/grease, so literally 'a soft paste'. The verb is always 바르다 ('spread/smear onto'), which is the same verb you use for sunscreen, lotion and lip balm, and it is what cleanly separates 연고 from 파스 (a patch you 붙이다, stick on) and from oral medicine you 먹다. For a specific area, name it up front: 무좀 연고 (athlete's foot), 안연고 (eye ointment), 화상 연고 (burns). Register is neutral and everyday. The big English-speaker pitfall is treating ointment like a pill — 연고 먹다 is wrong because it is external only — and reaching for 칠하다 ('to paint/coat', used for walls and nails) instead of the correct 바르다 for putting medicine on skin.

Saying 연고 먹다 — ointment is applied to the skin with 바르다, never eaten
Using 칠하다 (paint a surface) instead of 바르다 — medicine and cosmetics on skin always take 바르다
Marking the spot with the wrong particle — it's 상처에 연고를 바르다 (에 for the location), not 상처를

extendedVocab.explanation: 파스 (paseu) = "medicated patch / pain-relief patch". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 파스 주세요 ("Please give me a pain patch") shows how it actually behaves. usagePhrases.en: Please give me a pain patch
usagePhrases.note: For sore muscles and stiff shoulders

usagePhrases.en: to stick on a pain patch
usagePhrases.note: 붙이다 'to stick/attach' is the verb for patches

usagePhrases.en: I put a patch on my shoulder
usagePhrases.note: The body part takes 에: 어깨에 붙이다
뿌리다 = to spray; the aerosol type of 파스

examples.en: Please stick a patch on here.
examples.note: Simple request; 하나 = one, 붙여 주세요 = please attach it

examples.en: After working out I put a patch on my calf.
examples.note: Everyday: -고 나서 = after doing; 종아리 = calf

examples.ko: 어깨가 결려서 파스 붙였더니 한결 시원해요.
examples.romanization: eokkaega gyeollyeoseo paseu butyeotdeoni hangyeol siwonhaeyo.
examples.en: My shoulder was stiff so I put on a patch and it feels much better.
examples.note: Real-situation: 결리다 = to feel stiff/cramped; 시원하다 here = a soothing, cooling relief

extendedVocab.nuance: 파스 is the everyday word for the medicated patches Koreans slap on sore muscles, stiff necks and tired legs. Unlike the -제 and -약 medicines around it, 파스 is a loanword (from German/Dutch 'pasta'/pleister, via Japanese パス), so it has no hanja and no suffix — just the bare borrowed noun. The verb is 붙이다 ('stick on'), which is exactly what separates it from 연고 (a cream you 바르다, spread) and from any pill you 먹다. People habitually mention the strong menthol 냄새 (smell) and the 시원한 (cooling) feel. Register is casual and extremely common in daily life. The English-speaker pitfall is verb choice driven by the English word 'apply': learners say 파스 바르다, but a patch is stuck on with 붙이다 — only the cream or spray variants use 바르다 / 뿌리다 — and some try to swallow it like a pill, when 파스 is strictly external.

Saying 파스 바르다 — a patch is stuck on with 붙이다; only the cream/spray types use 바르다 or 뿌리다
Treating 파스 as something you swallow — it is external-only, applied to the skin
Expecting a hanja or -제/-약 suffix — 파스 is a bare loanword with neither
