천을 빠는 동작은 '씻다'가 아니라 '빨다'를 쓴다는 점을 영어 화자가 자주 놓칩니다(그릇은 씻다, 천·옷은 빨다).

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 밀폐용기 means "airtight (food-storage) container" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "airtight (food-storage) container" is 밀폐용기 (milpyeyonggi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 밀폐용기 ("airtight container"). Watch the particle attached to 밀폐용기 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Sealable container for storing food in the fridge; 밀폐 (密閉) = sealed airtight.
The casual everyday word for the same thing, especially used for 반찬 (side dishes).
담다 = to put/store food into a vessel; mark the container with 에.

usagePhrases.en: to store away in a container
usagePhrases.note: 넣어 두다 = to put inside and leave/keep it there.

examples.en: Put this in a side-dish container, please.
examples.note: 반찬통 is the casual spoken word; 밀폐용기 is the precise term.

examples.ko: 남은 반찬은 밀폐용기에 담아서 냉장고에 넣어 두세요.
examples.romanization: nameun banchaneun milpyeyonggie damaseo naengjanggoe neoeo duseyo.
examples.en: Put the leftover side dishes in an airtight container and keep them in the fridge.
examples.note: 담아서 = put in and then...; 넣어 두다 = store away. Note food goes 통에 담다 (에, not 으로).

examples.ko: 국물 있는 건 밀폐 잘 되는 통에 담아야 안 새요.
examples.romanization: gungmul inneun geon milpye jal doeneun tonge damaya an saeyo.
examples.en: Soupy food should go in a well-sealing container so it doesn't leak.
examples.note: 밀폐가 되다 = to seal tight; 새다 = to leak.

extendedVocab.nuance: 밀폐용기는 뚜껑이 꽉 닫혀 공기가 새지 않게 음식을 보관하는 통입니다. 한자어 '밀폐(密閉)'는 '빽빽할 밀 + 닫을 폐', 곧 '빈틈없이 닫는다'는 뜻이라 국물이 새지 않고 냄새가 배지 않는 것이 핵심입니다('용기 容器'는 '담는 그릇'). 일상 대화에서는 같은 물건을 '반찬통'이라고 훨씬 자주 부르는데, 밀폐용기가 격식 있고 정확한 말이라면 반찬통은 친근한 생활어입니다(특히 반찬을 담을 때). 그냥 '통'이나 '박스'와 달리 '밀폐'라는 말에 '공기가 안 통하게 잘 닫힌다'는 기능이 들어 있는 점을 살려 쓰면 좋습니다. 영어 화자가 자주 틀리는 조사는, 음식을 통 '안에' 넣더라도 '밀폐용기에 담다/넣다'처럼 장소 조사 에를 쓴다는 점입니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling it just 박스 or 통 — for food storage the precise term is 밀폐용기, or casually 반찬통; 박스 suggests a cardboard box.
Marking the container with 으로 — food goes INTO it, so use 에: '밀폐용기에 담다/넣다', not '밀폐용기로'.
Pairing it with 넣다 alone for fixed storage — to put away and keep, the natural form is 넣어 두다 or 담아 두다.

structuredNuance.t: 밀폐용기는 뚜껑이 꽉 닫혀 공기가 새지 않게 음식을 보관하는 통입니다. 그냥 '통'이나 '박스'와 달리 '밀폐'라는 말에 '공기가 안 통하게 잘 닫힌다'는 기능이 들어 있는 점을 살려 쓰면 좋습니다.
일상 대화에서는 같은 물건을 '반찬통'이라고 훨씬 자주 부르는데, 밀폐용기가 격식 있고 정확한 말이라면 반찬통은 친근한 생활어입니다(특히 반찬을 담을 때).
한자어 '밀폐(密閉)'는 '빽빽할 밀 + 닫을 폐', 곧 '빈틈없이 닫는다'는 뜻이라 국물이 새지 않고 냄새가 배지 않는 것이 핵심입니다('용기 容器'는 '담는 그릇').
영어 화자가 자주 틀리는 조사는, 음식을 통 '안에' 넣더라도 '밀폐용기에 담다/넣다'처럼 장소 조사 에를 쓴다는 점입니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 앞치마 means "apron" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 앞치마 (apchima) = "apron". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 앞치마 ("apron") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 앞치마, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Worn over the front of your clothes to protect them while cooking or cleaning.
두르다 = to wrap around; the most idiomatic verb for an apron (르 irregular: 둘러요/둘렀어요).
입다 is also widely heard in everyday speech, though 두르다 is more precise.
벗다 for removing it, the same verb as for taking off clothes.

examples.en: Lend me an apron, please.
examples.note: Simple request; 앞치마 literally = 'front (앞) skirt-cloth (치마)'.

examples.en: Before cooking, I put on an apron first.
examples.note: 두르다 conjugates to 둘렀어요 (르 irregular); -부터 = 'starting with'.

examples.ko: 김치 담글 때 옷에 안 묻게 앞치마 꼭 하세요.
examples.romanization: gimchi damgeul ttae ose an mutge apchima kko kaseyo.
examples.en: When making kimchi, be sure to wear an apron so it doesn't get on your clothes.
examples.note: 묻다 = to get smeared on; colloquially '앞치마(를) 하다' also works for 'put on'.

extendedVocab.nuance: 앞치마는 요리하거나 설거지·청소할 때 옷이 더러워지지 않게 몸 앞에 두르는 천으로, 이름 자체가 '앞(front) + 치마(skirt-cloth)'라 글자만 봐도 뜻이 보입니다. 가장 자연스러운 동사는 '두르다'인데, 이는 허리에 끈을 '둘러' 묶기 때문입니다('두르다'는 르 불규칙이라 둘러요/둘렀어요로 바뀌니 주의). 일상에서는 '앞치마를 입다'나 '앞치마(를) 하다'도 흔히 쓰여 셋 다 통합니다. 영어 화자가 헷갈리기 쉬운 점은, 같은 부엌 천이라도 행주·수건은 무언가를 '닦는' 천이고 앞치마는 몸에 '걸쳐 입는' 옷이라는 것입니다(앞치마로 식탁을 닦지는 않습니다). 김치를 담그거나 기름이 튀는 요리를 할 때 옷을 보호하려고 특히 자주 두릅니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using only 입다 for it — the most idiomatic verb for an apron is 두르다 (you tie/wrap it around).
Mis-conjugating 두르다 as a regular verb — it's 르-irregular: past is 둘렀어요, not '두르었어요'.
Confusing 앞치마 with 행주/수건 — the apron is worn on the body, while those are cloths for wiping or drying.

structuredNuance.t: 앞치마는 요리하거나 설거지·청소할 때 옷이 더러워지지 않게 몸 앞에 두르는 천입니다. 김치를 담그거나 기름이 튀는 요리를 할 때 옷을 보호하려고 특히 자주 두릅니다.
이름 자체가 '앞(front) + 치마(skirt-cloth)'라 글자만 봐도 뜻이 보입니다.
가장 자연스러운 동사는 '두르다'인데, 이는 허리에 끈을 '둘러' 묶기 때문입니다('두르다'는 르 불규칙이라 둘러요/둘렀어요로 바뀌니 주의). 일상에서는 '앞치마를 입다'나 '앞치마(를) 하다'도 흔히 쓰여 셋 다 통합니다.
영어 화자가 헷갈리기 쉬운 점은, 같은 부엌 천이라도 행주·수건은 무언가를 '닦는' 천이고 앞치마는 몸에 '걸쳐 입는' 옷이라는 것입니다(앞치마로 식탁을 닦지는 않습니다).

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 숙박 means "lodging, overnight stay" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 숙박 (sukbak) means "lodging, overnight stay". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 숙박 시설 ("lodging facilities"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 숙박 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Set phrase on official signs and laws; 시설 = facility, so it means any registered place to stay.
비 (費) = fee/cost; the money paid for the night, e.g. 숙박비가 비싸다.
하다-verb form; sounds formal, used on forms and by staff, not in casual chat.
Standard way to count a trip; read 일박 이일. The 박 here is the same 泊 as in 숙박.

examples.en: Where are you staying?
examples.note: Simple travel small talk; 어디서 = where (at), the location particle 에서 shortened to 서.

examples.en: The lodging is pricier than I expected.
examples.note: -네요 adds a soft 'oh, I notice' reaction; very natural when reacting to a price.

examples.ko: 성수기라 시내 숙박 시설이 거의 다 찼어요.
examples.romanization: seongsugira sinae sukbak siseori geoui da chasseoyo.
examples.en: It's peak season so almost every place to stay downtown is booked.
examples.note: 다 찼어요 = all filled up; 숙박 시설 is the formal noun a receptionist or news report would use.

extendedVocab.nuance: 숙박 (宿泊: 宿 'to lodge' + 泊 'to stay overnight', originally a boat lying at anchor) is the umbrella, paperwork-flavored word for spending the night somewhere — any hotel, motel, guesthouse or 펜션. The dividing line you must feel: 숙박 is the ACT/concept of staying, while 숙소 (宿所) is the PLACE you stay; Koreans say 숙소를 예약했어요 (booked a place) but 숙박을 했어요 sounds stiff, so prefer the more conversational 잤어요/묵었어요 in speech. It collocates with 시설, 비, 업소 and 예약, and shows up on booking apps, receipts and signs. The English-speaker pitfall is treating 숙박 like the casual English 'stay' and saying things like 호텔에서 숙박했어요 — natural Korean is 호텔에서 잤어요 or 묵었어요; save 숙박 for the noun (숙박 시설, 숙박비), not as your everyday verb.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 친구 집에서 숙박했어요 for 'I stayed at my friend's place' — 숙박하다 is too formal/commercial; a real speaker says 친구 집에서 잤어요 (slept over) or 묵었어요.
Mixing up 숙박 (the act of staying) with 숙소 (the lodging itself); you book a 숙소, you don't book a 숙박.
Writing 1박을 길게 늘여 '일 박' with a space — it's 1박 2일 as a fixed count, and the 박 is a counter, not a free noun here.

structuredNuance.t: 숙박은 어딘가에서 하룻밤을 보낸다는 뜻의, 격식 있고 서류 느낌이 나는 포괄적 단어다 — 호텔, 모텔, 게스트하우스, 펜션 등 어디든 가리킨다. 예약 앱, 영수증, 간판에 자주 나오며 시설, 비, 업소, 예약과 잘 어울린다.
느껴야 할 경계: 숙박은 머무는 행위·개념이고, 숙소(宿所)는 머무는 장소다. 한국 사람은 숙소를 예약했어요라고 하지만 숙박을 했어요는 딱딱하게 들린다. 말할 때는 더 구어적인 잤어요/묵었어요를 쓰는 게 낫다.
宿泊: 宿 '머물다' + 泊 '하룻밤 지내다'. 본래 배가 닻을 내리고 정박해 있는 모습에서 왔다.
숙박을 영어 캐주얼한 'stay'처럼 다뤄 호텔에서 숙박했어요라고 말하는 것. 자연스러운 한국어는 호텔에서 잤어요나 묵었어요다. 숙박은 명사(숙박 시설, 숙박비)로 아껴 쓰고 일상 동사로 쓰지 말 것.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 게스트하우스 means "guesthouse" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "guesthouse" is 게스트하우스 (geseuteuhauseu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 게스트하우스에 묵다 ("to stay at a guesthouse"). Watch the particle attached to 게스트하우스 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 묵다 is the go-to verb for lodging; slightly more travel-flavored than 자다 (sleep).
Clipped form among 20-30s; 게스트하우스 → 게하, used constantly in speech and texts.
A bunk-bed room shared with strangers — the cheapest bed; often clipped to 도미.
Read 일인실, 이인실; the private-room options if you don't want a dorm.

examples.ko: 저는 여행할 때 보통 게스트하우스에 묵어요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun yeohaenghal ttae botong geseuteuhauseue mugeoyo.
examples.en: When I travel I usually stay at a guesthouse.
examples.note: 묵다 = to lodge; pairs with 에 (location of staying), not 에서, when it means 'lodge at'.

examples.en: I made a lot of friends at the guesthouse.
examples.note: 사귀다 = to make/befriend; here 에서 marks where the action happened. Note the casual short form 게하.

examples.ko: 조식 포함이고 사장님이 직접 파티도 열어 줘서 분위기가 좋았어요.
examples.romanization: josik pohamigo sajangnimi jikjeop patido yeoreo jwoseo bunwigiga joasseoyo.
examples.en: Breakfast was included and the owner even threw a party, so the vibe was great.
examples.note: 조식 포함 = breakfast included; 파티를 열다 = to throw a party — guesthouses are known for social nights.

extendedVocab.nuance: 게스트하우스 is a direct English loanword (guest + house) written as ONE word, and in Korea it specifically means cheap, sociable backpacker-style lodging — think shared dorms, a common kitchen, and famous 게하 파티 nights, hugely popular in Jeju and Busan with 20-30s. The contrast you need: a 게스트하우스 sells you a BED in a shared social space, a 호텔 sells a serviced private room, a 펜션 rents you a whole independent unit, and a 민박 puts you in a local family's spare room — so don't use them interchangeably just because all are 'places to sleep'. The native verb that pairs with it is 묵다 (to lodge), and crucially young people almost always shorten it to 게하 in conversation, so you must recognize the slang. The English-speaker pitfall is twofold: never split it as 게스트 하우스 in writing, and don't assume every room is a dorm — most also offer 1인실/2인실, so ask 도미토리예요, 1인실이에요? when booking.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing it as two words 게스트 하우스 — Korean treats it as a single loanword noun, 게스트하우스.
Assuming it always means a shared dorm and being surprised by private rooms; many offer 1인실/2인실, so confirm the room type first.
Saying 게스트하우스에서 잤어요 only — fine, but to sound like a traveler use 게스트하우스에 묵었어요, where 묵다 is the lodging verb.

structuredNuance.t: 한국에서 게스트하우스는 싸고 사교적인 배낭여행자 스타일 숙소를 콕 집어 가리킨다 — 공용 도미토리, 공용 주방, 그리고 유명한 게하 파티 밤이 떠오른다. 제주와 부산에서 20-30대에게 아주 인기다. 함께 쓰는 동사는 묵다(to lodge)다.
필요한 대비: 게스트하우스는 공용 사교 공간의 침대를 팔고, 호텔은 서비스되는 개인 객실을, 펜션은 독립된 한 채 전체를, 민박은 현지 가정의 남는 방을 내준다. 모두 '잘 곳'이라고 해서 마구 바꿔 쓰지 말 것. 또한 젊은 사람들은 대화에서 거의 항상 게하로 줄이므로 이 슬랭을 알아들어야 한다.
영어 외래어(guest + house)를 한 단어로 붙여 쓴 말이다.
두 가지다: 글로 쓸 때 절대 게스트 하우스로 띄어 쓰지 말 것, 그리고 모든 방이 도미토리라고 가정하지 말 것 — 대부분 1인실/2인실도 있으니 예약할 때 도미토리예요, 1인실이에요?라고 물어볼 것.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 펜션 means "pension (vacation rental house)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 펜션 (pensyeon) = "pension (vacation rental house)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 펜션을 빌리다 / 잡다 ("to rent / book a pension") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 펜션, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 빌리다 = rent; 잡다 (lit. grab) is casual for 'secure a booking', e.g. 펜션 하나 잡았어.
An upmarket 펜션 with a private pool; trendy for group getaways and couples.
Almost every 펜션 has a 바비큐 area — a top reason groups book one over a hotel.
로 marks manner; 펜션 are ideal 단체로 since you rent the whole space.

examples.ko: 친구들이랑 펜션 빌려서 놀러 가기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: chingudeurirang pensyeon billyeoseo nolleo gagiro haesseoyo.
examples.en: We decided to rent a pension with friends and go hang out.
examples.note: 빌리다 = to rent; -기로 했어요 = 'we decided to', the standard way to announce a group plan.

examples.ko: 이 펜션은 바다 바로 앞이라 전망이 좋아요.
examples.romanization: i pensyeoneun bada baro apira jeonmangi joayo.
examples.en: This pension is right by the sea so the view is great.
examples.note: 바로 앞 = right in front; -이라 = 'being (that)', a casual reason connector from 이다.

examples.ko: 펜션에서 다 같이 바비큐 해 먹는 게 제일 좋았어요.
examples.romanization: pensyeoneseo da gachi babikyu hae meongneun ge jeil joasseoyo.
examples.en: Cooking and eating barbecue all together at the pension was the best part.
examples.note: 해 먹다 = cook-and-eat (do-it-yourself meal); -는 게 = nominalizes 'the act of', a key pattern for 'the … part'.

extendedVocab.nuance: A 펜션 is a notorious false friend: it has nothing to do with a retirement pension (that's 연금, 年金 'yearly money') — in Korea it means a privately run vacation house or unit you rent whole, usually in the countryside or by the coast. The loanword came via European 'pension/pensione' (guesthouse) but the Korean usage has drifted to mean a self-catering rental for a 가족 or 친구들 group, which is exactly why it differs from a 호텔 (serviced rooms), a 게스트하우스 (a bed in a shared space) and a 리조트 (a big facility complex). It collocates with 빌리다/잡다, 바비큐, 풀빌라 and 단체로, and the whole appeal is getting a kitchen, your own space, and a BBQ deck. The English-speaker pitfall, beyond the 연금 mix-up, is expecting hotel service: a 펜션 is typically self-service with no daily housekeeping, so don't ask the 주인 for room cleaning or daily towels.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Hearing 펜션 and thinking 'retirement pension' — that meaning is 연금; 펜션 is only a vacation rental.
Expecting hotel-style service like daily cleaning or room service — a 펜션 is self-catering, so you cook and tidy yourself.
Saying 펜션 방을 예약했어요 (booked a pension room) as if it were a hotel — you usually rent the whole 펜션/동, so 펜션을 잡았어요/빌렸어요 fits better.

structuredNuance.t: 한국에서 펜션은 통째로 빌리는 개인 운영 휴양용 집이나 한 채를 뜻하며, 보통 시골이나 해안가에 있다. 빌리다/잡다, 바비큐, 풀빌라, 단체로와 잘 어울리고, 핵심 매력은 주방과 나만의 공간, BBQ 데크를 얻는 것이다.
한국어 용법이 가족이나 친구들 그룹을 위한 셀프 케이터링 렌탈로 굳었고, 바로 그 점에서 호텔(서비스되는 객실), 게스트하우스(공용 공간의 침대), 리조트(큰 시설 복합단지)와 다르다.
악명 높은 가짜 친구다: 노후 연금과는 전혀 무관하다(그건 연금, 年金 '해마다 받는 돈'). 외래어는 유럽의 'pension/pensione'(게스트하우스)에서 왔지만 한국 용법은 의미가 옮겨갔다.
연금 혼동 외에 또 하나는 호텔식 서비스를 기대하는 것이다: 펜션은 보통 셀프서비스라 매일 청소가 없으니, 주인에게 객실 청소나 매일 수건을 요청하지 말 것.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 리조트 means "resort" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 리조트 (rijoteu) means "resort". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 리조트에 묵다 ("to stay at a resort"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 리조트 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 묵다 for lodging; you 'stay at' a 리조트 the way you would a hotel.
The headline facility of a summer 리조트; a big draw for families.
장 (場) = grounds/field; what you book a winter 리조트 for.
부대 (附帶) = attached; the extra facilities (pool, spa, gym) a 리조트 advertises.

examples.en: I went to a resort to ski in winter.
examples.note: 스키(를) 타다 = to ski (lit. ride skis); -러 가다 = 'go in order to', for a purpose of movement.

examples.ko: 리조트 안에 워터파크가 있어서 애들이 정말 좋아해요.
examples.romanization: rijoteu ane woteopakeuga isseoseo aedeuri jeongmal joahaeyo.
examples.en: There's a water park inside the resort so the kids really love it.
examples.note: 안에 = inside; -아서 chains 'there is X, so Y', cause-then-result.

examples.ko: 리조트는 좀 비싸지만 부대시설이 워낙 잘 돼 있어서 안 나가도 돼요.
examples.romanization: rijoteuneun jom bissajiman budaesiseori wonak jal dwae isseoseo an nagado dwaeyo.
examples.en: A resort is a bit pricey but the amenities are so well set up you don't even need to leave.
examples.note: 잘 돼 있다 = to be well-equipped; -지만 = 'but'; 워낙 = 'by nature/so very', emphasizing degree.

extendedVocab.nuance: 리조트 is the English loanword 'resort', but in Korea it specifically means a large self-contained vacation COMPLEX — lodging bundled with pools, spas, restaurants, and a 워터파크 or 스키장 — a clear step up from a plain 호텔. The sharp contrast: a 호텔 sells you a room and you go out for fun, whereas a 리조트's facilities ARE the trip, so you book it precisely when you intend to stay inside the whole time (Gangwon ski 리조트, Jeju beach 리조트). Watch the nested term 콘도/콘도미니엄 — that's a membership-based, kitchen-equipped unit you book INSIDE many resorts, not a synonym for the resort itself. It collocates with 묵다, 부대시설, 워터파크 and 스키장. The English-speaker pitfall is using 리조트 and 호텔 interchangeably the way casual English blurs 'resort/hotel'; in Korean the word signals scale and on-site amenities, so calling a single downtown business hotel a 리조트 sounds wrong.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 리조트 and 호텔 as the same word — a 리조트 implies a big amenity-packed complex, while a 호텔 is just serviced rooms; pick by scale.
Confusing 리조트 (the whole complex) with 콘도/콘도미니엄 (a membership unit booked inside it).
Spelling it 리조트 vs 리조튼/리조트호텔 carelessly — the standard loanword is just 리조트.

structuredNuance.t: 한국에서 리조트는 크고 자체 완결적인 휴양 복합단지를 콕 집어 뜻한다 — 숙소에 수영장, 스파, 식당, 워터파크나 스키장이 묶인 형태로, 평범한 호텔보다 확실히 한 단계 위다. 묵다, 부대시설, 워터파크, 스키장과 잘 어울린다.
날카로운 대비: 호텔은 객실을 팔고 재미는 밖에 나가서 찾지만, 리조트는 시설 자체가 여행이라 안에서 내내 머물 작정일 때 예약한다(강원 스키 리조트, 제주 해변 리조트). 또 안에 든 용어 콘도/콘도미니엄을 조심할 것 — 그건 많은 리조트 안에서 예약하는 회원제·주방 딸린 유닛이지 리조트 자체의 동의어가 아니다.
영어 외래어 'resort'다.
캐주얼한 영어가 'resort/hotel'을 뭉뚱그리듯 리조트와 호텔을 바꿔 쓰는 것. 한국어에서 이 단어는 규모와 현장 부대시설을 신호하므로, 도심의 단일 비즈니스호텔을 리조트라 부르면 어색하게 들린다.

extendedVocab.english: homestay, B&B in a private home
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 민박 means "homestay, B&B in a private home" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "homestay, B&B in a private home" is 민박 (minbak). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 민박을 하다 / 민박을 잡다 ("to do / book a homestay"). Watch the particle attached to 민박 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 하다 = to do (a stay); 잡다 casual for securing one, e.g. 바닷가에 민박 잡았어요.
집 = house; the physical place where you do a 민박, the 'host's house'.
주인 (主人) = owner; often addressed as 주인 아주머니/아저씨, who cooks and chats.
민박 are most common 시골에서 and in seaside 어촌 (漁村) villages.

examples.en: We slept one night at a homestay near the beach.
examples.note: 하룻밤 = one night (irregular: 하루 + 밤 → 하룻밤); 근처 = nearby.

examples.ko: 민박집 주인 아주머니가 아침을 직접 차려 주셨어요.
examples.romanization: minbakjip juin ajumeoniga achimeul jikjeop charyeo jusyeosseoyo.
examples.en: The homestay host (auntie) personally made us breakfast.
examples.note: 차려 주다 = to set out a meal for someone; the honorific 주셨어요 respects the older host.

examples.ko: 호텔보다 민박이 훨씬 정겹고 사람 사는 냄새가 나서 좋았어요.
examples.romanization: hotelboda minbagi hwolssin jeonggyeopgo saram saneun naemsaega naseo joasseoyo.
examples.en: A homestay felt far homier than a hotel, with a real lived-in warmth I loved.
examples.note: 정겹다 = warm-hearted/homey; 사람 사는 냄새가 나다 = idiom 'has a lived-in human warmth'.

extendedVocab.nuance: 민박 (民泊: 民 'civilian/the people' + 泊 'to stay overnight') literally means 'staying in an ordinary person's home', and that is exactly what it is — you rent a spare room in a local family's house, the most old-school, personal and budget lodging type, common in 시골 and fishing villages. The dividing line among the cheap options: a 민박 means SHARING space with the host family (the 주인 often cooks you breakfast), a 펜션 gives you a whole independent unit to yourselves, and a 게스트하우스 is a commercial bunk-bed operation; many learners blur all three. It pairs with 민박집, 주인, 시골 and 하룻밤, and its charm is the human warmth (정 / 정겹다). Two pitfalls: spelling — the final consonant is ㄱ (민박 'stay'), NOT ㅇ (민방), so don't write 민방; and don't equate it with the English 'Airbnb' — that whole-place short-term rental is closer to 펜션 or just 에어비앤비, while 민박 keeps the nuance of a host actually living there with you.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Spelling it 민방 — the 박 is 泊 (overnight stay) ending in ㄱ; 민방 is a different, wrong word.
Treating 민박, 펜션, and 게스트하우스 as synonyms — a 민박 shares the host family's home, a 펜션 is a private rental unit, a 게스트하우스 is a shared-dorm business.
Calling any Airbnb a 민박 — the host living on-site is the point of 민박; a whole-unit rental is closer to 펜션/에어비앤비.

structuredNuance.t: 민박은 글자 그대로 '평범한 사람의 집에서 묵기'를 뜻하며, 바로 그것이다 — 현지 가정 집의 남는 방을 빌리는, 가장 옛날식이고 정겹고 저렴한 숙소 유형으로 시골과 어촌에 흔하다. 민박집, 주인, 시골, 하룻밤과 어울리며 매력은 사람의 정(정 / 정겹다)이다.
저렴한 선택지들 사이의 경계: 민박은 주인 가족과 공간을 공유한다는 뜻이고(주인이 아침을 차려 주는 경우가 많다), 펜션은 독립된 한 채 전체를 우리끼리 쓰게 해 주며, 게스트하우스는 상업적인 이층침대 영업이다. 많은 학습자가 셋을 뭉뚱그린다.
民泊: 民 '백성/일반인' + 泊 '하룻밤 묵다'.
두 가지다: 철자 — 받침이 ㄱ(민박 '묵다')이지 ㅇ(민방)이 아니므로 민방으로 쓰지 말 것. 그리고 영어 'Airbnb'와 같다고 보지 말 것 — 집 전체 단기 렌탈은 펜션이나 그냥 에어비앤비에 더 가깝고, 민박은 주인이 실제로 함께 거기 산다는 뉘앙스를 유지한다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 체크아웃 means "check-out" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 체크아웃 (chekeuaut) = "check-out". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 체크아웃 시간 ("check-out time") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 체크아웃, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: The single most useful phrase: 체크아웃 시간이 몇 시예요? (What time is check-out?)
The arrival counterpart; the two loanwords always travel as a pair.
하다-verb used at the front desk: 지금 체크아웃할게요 (I'll check out now).
맡기다 = entrust; the standard follow-up request after checkout, 짐 좀 맡길 수 있어요?

examples.en: What time is check-out?
examples.note: The essential front-desk question; 몇 시 = what time, with the topic particle dropping the 시간 in fast speech.

examples.en: Can I leave my luggage after checking out?
examples.note: -고 = 'and then' linking the two actions; 맡기다 + -ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can entrust', a very common polite request.

examples.ko: 늦게 체크아웃하면 추가 요금이 붙을 수 있으니까 미리 말씀해 주세요.
examples.romanization: neutge chekeuautamyeon chuga yogeumi buteul su isseunikka miri malsseumhae juseyo.
examples.en: If you check out late an extra fee can apply, so please tell us in advance.
examples.note: 추가 요금이 붙다 = a surcharge 'sticks on'; -니까 gives the reason; 말씀해 주세요 = honorific 'please tell'.

extendedVocab.nuance: 체크아웃 is the universal English loanword (check out) used at every hotel, 게스트하우스 and 펜션 in Korea, and it lives glued to its partner 체크인 — you will essentially never meet one without the other. The reason to learn the loanword rather than a native equivalent: the native 나가다 just means 'to leave/go out' physically and does NOT carry the hotel meaning of settling the bill and ending the booking, so saying 호텔에서 나가요 sounds like you stepped outside, not that you checked out. It collocates with 시간, 하다, and the very practical 짐 맡기다 (store luggage). The key real-world phrase is 체크아웃이 몇 시예요?, because late departure usually triggers an 추가 요금, and afterward you can typically ask for 짐 보관. The English-speaker pitfall: 'late checkout' is 레이트 체크아웃 or 늦은 체크아웃 and is rarely free — confirm the fee first rather than assuming.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 나가다 (to leave/go out) for the hotel process — that only means physically exiting; the front-desk action is 체크아웃하다.
Assuming late checkout is free — it's 레이트/늦은 체크아웃 and usually costs an 추가 요금, so ask before staying past time.
Forgetting that 체크인/체크아웃 are a fixed pair; learn and use them together rather than coining a native phrase.

structuredNuance.t: 체크아웃은 한국의 모든 호텔, 게스트하우스, 펜션에서 쓰이는 보편적 영어 외래어(check out)로, 짝꿍 체크인과 딱 붙어 산다 — 사실상 하나만 따로 만날 일은 없다. 시간, 하다, 그리고 아주 실용적인 짐 맡기다(짐 보관)와 어울린다. 핵심 실전 표현은 체크아웃이 몇 시예요?인데, 늦은 출발은 대개 추가 요금을 부르기 때문이다.
고유어 대신 외래어를 배우는 이유: 고유어 나가다는 그저 물리적으로 '떠나다/나가다'를 뜻하고 계산을 하고 예약을 끝낸다는 호텔 의미를 담지 않는다. 그래서 호텔에서 나가요라고 하면 체크아웃했다는 게 아니라 잠깐 밖에 나갔다는 말처럼 들린다.
'late checkout'은 레이트 체크아웃이나 늦은 체크아웃이고 무료인 경우가 드물다 — 당연하게 여기지 말고 요금을 먼저 확인할 것.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 성수기 means "peak season" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 성수기 (seongsugi) means "peak season". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 극성수기 ("absolute peak season"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 성수기 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 극 (極) = extreme; the very busiest stretch, e.g. late July to mid-August.
The inflated price tier; lodging sites list 성수기 vs 비수기 요금 separately.
피하다 = to avoid; the classic money-saving move locals talk about.
꽉 = tightly; 꽉 차다 = packed full, what happens to rooms in 성수기.

examples.ko: 성수기에는 펜션 값이 거의 두 배예요.
examples.romanization: seongsugieneun pensyeon gapsi geoui du baeyeyo.
examples.en: In peak season pension prices are almost double.
examples.note: 두 배 = double; 값 = price; 에는 marks the time-frame as the topic ('as for peak season').

examples.en: It's peak season so plane tickets are really hard to get.
examples.note: 구하다 = to obtain/get hold of; -기가 힘들다 = 'is hard to (do)', nominalizing the action.

examples.ko: 성수기를 살짝 피해서 가니까 가격도 싸고 사람도 없어서 훨씬 좋더라고요.
examples.romanization: seongsugireul saljjak pihaeseo ganikka gagyeokdo ssago saramdo eopseoseo hwolssin joteoragoyo.
examples.en: Going just slightly off-peak made it cheaper and less crowded, so much better.
examples.note: 피해서 = avoiding-and-then; -더라고요 = reporting a personal realization, 'I found that…'.

extendedVocab.nuance: 성수기 (盛需期: 盛 'flourishing/abundant' + 需 'demand' + 期 'period') literally means 'period of booming demand' — the high travel seasons (여름휴가 summer, 추석 Chuseok, 설날 Seollal, ski season) when lodging and flights cost far more and sell out fast. Its exact antonym is 비수기 (非需期, 'non-demand period'), and you should drill them as a pair; do NOT confuse it with 우기 (雨期, 'rainy season') — the 수 here is 需 'demand', not 水 'water'. It collocates with 요금/값이 오르다, 예약이 꽉 차다, 극성수기 and especially 성수기를 피하다, the phrase residents use constantly to save money. The English-speaker pitfall: 성수기 is about DEMAND, not weather, so a single sunny day is not 성수기, and conversely a rainy August week is still 성수기 because people are traveling — keep the meaning anchored to crowds and prices, not to the sky.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Mixing up 성수기 (peak) and 비수기 (off-season) — they are direct antonyms; memorize them together.
Reading the 수 as 水 'water' and thinking it relates to rainy/water season — it's 需 'demand'; rainy season is 우기/장마.
Treating it as a weather word ('it's sunny, so it's 성수기') — 성수기 is defined by travel demand and prices, not by the day's weather.

structuredNuance.t: 성수기는 글자 그대로 '수요가 폭발하는 시기'를 뜻한다 — 여름휴가, 추석, 설날, 스키 시즌 같은 여행 성수기로, 숙소와 항공편이 훨씬 비싸지고 빨리 매진된다. 요금/값이 오르다, 예약이 꽉 차다, 극성수기, 특히 주민들이 돈 아끼려고 늘 쓰는 성수기를 피하다와 어울린다.
정확한 반의어는 비수기(非需期, '수요 없는 시기')이고 둘을 한 쌍으로 익혀야 한다. 우기(雨期, '장마철')와 헷갈리지 말 것 — 여기 수는 需 '수요'이지 水 '물'이 아니다.
盛需期: 盛 '번성/풍성함' + 需 '수요' + 期 '기간'.
성수기는 날씨가 아니라 수요에 관한 것이다. 그래서 맑은 하루는 성수기가 아니고, 반대로 비 오는 8월 한 주도 사람들이 여행 중이므로 여전히 성수기다 — 의미를 하늘이 아니라 인파와 가격에 묶어 둘 것.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 비수기 means "off-season, low season" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "off-season, low season" is 비수기 (bisugi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 비수기 요금 ("off-season rate"). Watch the particle attached to 비수기 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: The cheaper price tier; the flip side of 성수기 요금 on booking sites.
할인 (割引) = discount; 비수기 is when lodging offers the deepest 할인.
Describes how a tourist spot feels in 비수기, opposite of 붐비다 (crowded).
가성비 = 가격 대비 성능 (price-to-performance); 비수기 travel has top 가성비.

examples.en: If you go in the off-season it's much cheaper.
examples.note: 훨씬 = much/by far (with comparatives); 싸다 = cheap; -면 = 'if/when'.

examples.ko: 비수기라 사람이 별로 없어서 조용하고 좋았어요.
examples.romanization: bisugira sarami byeollo eopseoseo joyonghago joasseoyo.
examples.en: It was off-season so there weren't many people, nice and quiet.
examples.note: 별로 + 없다 = 'not many/not really'; -아서 chains 'so', giving the result.

examples.ko: 같은 펜션인데 비수기라 가성비가 진짜 좋더라고요.
examples.romanization: gateun pensyeoninde bisugira gaseongbiga jinjja joteoragoyo.
examples.en: Same pension, but being off-season the value was really great.
examples.note: -인데 = 'it's X, and (contrast)'; 가성비 is everyday slang; -더라고요 reports what you noticed firsthand.

extendedVocab.nuance: 비수기 (非需期: 非 'non-' + 需 'demand' + 期 'period') is the off-season — weekdays, late autumn, deep winter outside ski areas — when demand drops, lodging slashes prices, and spots feel 한산하다 (calm and empty). It is the exact mirror of 성수기 (盛需期), so the only structural difference is 非 'not' replacing 盛 'flourishing'; learn the two as one pair. A frequent learner trap is the syllable 비: here it is 非 'not', NOT 비 (雨) 'rain' and NOT 비 (費) 'fee', so 비수기 has nothing to do with rainy weather or a 'cheap fee' despite the coincidental sound. It collocates with 할인, 한산하다, and the buzzword 가성비, which is why budget-minded 20-30s love it: the same room for far less, minus the crowds. The English-speaker pitfall is assuming 'off-season' means everything is closed — in Korea many 비수기 deals are precisely the draw, so frame it as a money-and-quiet upside, not a downside.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Pairing it wrong — 비수기 is the antonym of 성수기, not a separate unrelated word; always learn them together.
Reading 비 as 'rain' (雨) and thinking 비수기 is a rainy season — the 비 is 非 'non/not'.
Assuming off-season means places are shut/dead — in Korea 비수기 is valued for cheap 할인 and a 한산한 (uncrowded) feel.

structuredNuance.t: 비수기는 비성수기다 — 평일, 늦가을, 스키장 외 지역의 한겨울 — 수요가 떨어지고 숙소가 값을 확 깎고 명소가 한산하다(조용하고 텅 빈) 느낌이 드는 때다. 할인, 한산하다, 그리고 유행어 가성비와 어울리며, 그래서 예산을 따지는 20-30대가 좋아한다: 같은 방을 훨씬 싸게, 인파 없이.
성수기(盛需期)의 정확한 거울이라, 구조적 차이는 非 '아니다'가 盛 '번성함'을 대체한 것뿐이다. 둘을 한 쌍으로 익힐 것.
非需期: 非 '아니다' + 需 '수요' + 期 '기간'. 학습자가 자주 빠지는 함정은 음절 비다: 여기서는 非 '아니다'이지 비(雨) '비'도 아니고 비(費) '비용'도 아니다. 우연히 소리가 같을 뿐 비수기는 비 오는 날씨나 '싼 비용'과 아무 상관이 없다.
'off-season'이 모든 게 문 닫혔다는 뜻이라고 가정하는 것. 한국에서는 많은 비수기 할인이 바로 그 매력이므로, 단점이 아니라 돈과 한적함의 장점으로 받아들일 것.

extendedVocab.english: day trip (there and back same day)
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 당일치기 means "day trip (there and back same day)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 당일치기 (dangilchigi) = "day trip (there and back same day)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 당일치기로 ("as a day trip") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 당일치기, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 로 marks manner: 당일치기로 다녀오다 = 'go and come back as a day trip'.
The verb that naturally pairs with 당일치기, stressing the round trip.
무박 (無泊) = no overnight; an extreme day trip that runs overnight without sleeping at lodging.
The contrast term: if you DO sleep over, it becomes 1박 2일, not 당일치기.

examples.ko: 부산은 서울에서 당일치기로 다녀올 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: busaneun seoureseo dangilchigiro danyeool su isseoyo.
examples.en: You can do Busan as a day trip from Seoul.
examples.note: 다녀오다 = go-and-return; -ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can/be able to', here 다녀올 수 있어요.

examples.en: It's a day trip so I packed really light.
examples.note: 가볍게 = lightly (adverb from 가볍다); 짐을 싸다 = to pack one's bags.

examples.ko: 새벽에 출발해서 밤늦게 돌아오는 당일치기라 좀 빡빡하긴 했어요.
examples.romanization: saebyeoge chulbalhaeseo bamneutge doraoneun dangilchigira jom ppakppakagin haesseoyo.
examples.en: It was a day trip leaving at dawn and getting back late, so it was a bit tight.
examples.note: 빡빡하다 = packed/tight (very common colloquial); -긴 했어요 = 'it was … (admittedly)', softening the complaint.

extendedVocab.nuance: 당일치기 means a same-day round trip with NO overnight stay, built from 당일 (當日, 'that very day') plus the native suffix -치기 ('doing it in/within'), so it literally frames the whole trip as 'done within the day'. It is enormously practical in Korea because of the KTX, letting a Seoul resident pop down to 부산 or 강릉 당일치기. The sharp contrast learners need: 당일치기 vs 1박 2일 — the moment you sleep over even once, it is no longer 당일치기 but 1박 2일; and beyond that lies 무박 2일 (無泊, travelling across two days but never checking into lodging). It strongly collocates with 다녀오다 and tends to be described as 빡빡하다 (tight) because you cram everything into one day. The English-speaker pitfall is using plain 가다 ('go') — since the entire concept is the there-AND-back, Korean wants 다녀오다 (go and come back); 당일치기로 갔어요 alone can sound unfinished, so 당일치기로 다녀왔어요 is the natural frame.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using it when you actually stay the night — one overnight makes it 1박 2일, not 당일치기.
Saying 당일치기로 갔어요 with just 가다 — the round trip is the whole point, so use 다녀오다: 당일치기로 다녀왔어요.
Confusing 당일치기 (same-day return) with 무박 2일 (spans two days, no lodging) — they are different trip shapes.

structuredNuance.t: 당일치기는 하룻밤도 묵지 않는 당일 왕복 여행을 뜻한다. KTX 덕분에 한국에서 엄청나게 실용적이라, 서울 사람이 부산이나 강릉을 당일치기로 다녀올 수 있다. 다녀오다와 강하게 어울리고, 하루에 모든 걸 욱여넣기 때문에 빡빡하다(빡빡한)로 묘사되곤 한다.
학습자에게 필요한 날카로운 대비: 당일치기 vs 1박 2일 — 단 한 번이라도 묵는 순간 더 이상 당일치기가 아니라 1박 2일이 된다. 그 너머에는 무박 2일(無泊, 이틀에 걸쳐 다니지만 숙소에 체크인은 하지 않음)이 있다.
당일(當日, '바로 그날')에 고유어 접미사 -치기('그 안에 해내기')가 붙어, 여행 전체를 글자 그대로 '하루 안에 해냄'으로 틀 짓는다.
그냥 가다('go')를 쓰는 것 — 개념 전체가 갔다가 돌아오는 것이라 한국어는 다녀오다(가서 돌아오다)를 원한다. 당일치기로 갔어요만 쓰면 끝나지 않은 느낌이라, 당일치기로 다녀왔어요가 자연스러운 틀이다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 야경 means "night view, night scenery" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 야경 (yagyeong) means "night view, night scenery". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 야경이 예쁘다 ("the night view is pretty"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 야경 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: The single most common compliment about a place after dark; also 야경이 좋다.
명소 (名所) = noted place; e.g. 남산타워, 한강, where people go for the view.
전망대 (展望臺) = lookout; the spot you climb for the best 야경.
Playful slang borrowing 맛집 (food hotspot) → any spot with a killer 야경.

examples.ko: 남산에서 보는 서울 야경이 진짜 예뻐요.
examples.romanization: namsaneseo boneun seoul yagyeongi jinjja yeppeoyo.
examples.en: The Seoul night view from Namsan is really pretty.
examples.note: 에서 보는 = 'seen from' (location of the action modifying 야경); 진짜 = really.

examples.en: Want to go to the Han River to see the night view?
examples.note: -러 가다 = 'go in order to (see)'; -ㄹ래요? = a casual, friendly invitation/offer.

examples.ko: 여기 옥상 카페는 야경 맛집이라 데이트하기 딱 좋아요.
examples.romanization: yeogi oksang kapeneun yagyeong matjibira deiteuhagi ttak joayo.
examples.en: This rooftop cafe is a night-view gem, perfect for a date.
examples.note: 야경 맛집 = slang for a great-view spot; 딱 좋다 = 'just right/perfect', 딱 emphasizing the fit.

extendedVocab.nuance: 야경 (夜景: 夜 'night' + 景 'scenery/view') is specifically the VIEW SEEN AT NIGHT — glittering city lights from a 전망대, bridge, or rooftop — and enjoying it is a core way Koreans experience cities after dark. The crucial near-miss is 야간 (夜間: 夜 'night' + 間 'interval'), which means 'nighttime' as a TIME PERIOD (야간 근무 = night shift, 야간 운전 = night driving); 야경 is the scenery, 야간 is the clock window, and they are not interchangeable despite sharing 夜. Daytime scenery, by contrast, is just 경치 or 전망, so reserve 야경 for after dark. It collocates with 예쁘다/좋다, 명소, 전망대, and the social-media slang 야경 맛집 (literally 'night-view tasty-spot'), which young people coin by analogy to the foodie word 맛집. The English-speaker pitfall is saying 밤 경치 word-for-word for 'night scenery' — it's understandable but the idiomatic single word Koreans actually use is 야경.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 야경 (the night SCENERY) with 야간 (night TIME, as in 야간 근무 night shift) — same 夜 but different second character.
Using 야경 for daytime views — daytime scenery is 경치/전망; 야경 is strictly after dark.
Translating 'night scenery' literally as 밤 경치 — the natural single word is 야경.

structuredNuance.t: 야경은 콕 집어 '밤에 보는 풍경'을 뜻한다 — 전망대, 다리, 옥상에서 보는 반짝이는 도시 불빛 — 이를 즐기는 것은 한국 사람이 밤에 도시를 경험하는 핵심 방식이다. 예쁘다/좋다, 명소, 전망대, 그리고 젊은 사람들이 맛집을 본떠 만든 SNS 슬랭 야경 맛집('밤 풍경 맛집')과 어울린다.
결정적인 헷갈림은 야간(夜間: 夜 '밤' + 間 '사이')인데, 이건 시간대로서의 '밤 시간'을 뜻한다(야간 근무 = 야간 교대, 야간 운전 = 밤 운전). 야경은 풍경, 야간은 시간 창이라, 夜를 공유해도 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 반대로 낮 풍경은 그냥 경치나 전망이니, 야경은 해 진 뒤로 아껴 둘 것.
夜景: 夜 '밤' + 景 '풍경/경치'.
'night scenery'를 글자 그대로 밤 경치라고 하는 것 — 알아듣기는 하지만 한국 사람이 실제로 쓰는 관용적 한 단어는 야경이다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 일출 means "sunrise" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "sunrise" is 일출 (ilchul). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 해돋이 ("sunrise (native word)"). Watch the particle attached to 일출 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Pure-Korean synonym for 일출; 해돋이 보러 가다 is extremely common and sounds warmer.
Watching the first sunrise of the year is a major tradition; 첫 = first.
명소 (名所) = noted place; east-coast 정동진, 호미곶 are classic 일출 명소.
What you check the night before; catching it means setting a 새벽 alarm.

examples.ko: 새해 첫날 일출 보러 동해에 갔어요.
examples.romanization: saehae cheonnal ilchul boreo donghaee gasseoyo.
examples.en: On New Year's Day we went to the East Sea to see the sunrise.
examples.note: 첫날 = first day; 동해 = East Sea; -러 가다 = 'go in order to (see)'.

examples.ko: 일출을 보려고 새벽 다섯 시에 일어났어요.
examples.romanization: ilchureul boryeogo saebyeok daseot sie ireonasseoyo.
examples.en: I got up at 5 a.m. to watch the sunrise.
examples.note: -려고 = 'intending to / in order to'; 새벽 = pre-dawn; pairs with the effort of early rising.

examples.ko: 구름이 잔뜩 껴서 결국 일출을 못 봤지만 그래도 분위기는 좋았어요.
examples.romanization: gureumi jantteuk kkyeoseo gyeolguk ilchureul mot bwatjiman geuraedo bunwigineun joasseoyo.
examples.en: It clouded over completely so we missed the sunrise, but the mood was still nice.
examples.note: 구름이 끼다 = to cloud over; 못 봤다 = couldn't see; -지만 = 'but', conceding the letdown.

extendedVocab.nuance: 일출 (日出: 日 'sun' + 出 'to come out/exit') is sunrise, the exact antonym of 일몰 (日沒, 'sun sinks'), and in Korea watching it carries real cultural weight — crowds stream to the east coast (동해) for the 새해 일출, the first sunrise of the year, to make wishes. There is a true everyday synonym, the native 해돋이 (해 'sun' + 돋이 from 돋다 'to rise/come up'); 일출 is the Sino-Korean, slightly more formal term you see on signs and forecasts, while 해돋이 sounds warmer and is just as common in speech — they mean the same event, so 일출 보러 가요 and 해돋이 보러 가요 are interchangeable. It collocates with 명소, 시간, 보다, and the early-morning effort words 새벽 and 일어나다, since catching it means rising before dawn. The English-speaker pitfall is two-fold: don't swap 일출 (sunrise, 出 'out') with its lookalike 일몰 (sunset, 沒 'sink'), and don't over-formalize — in casual talk a native speaker is just as likely to say 해돋이, so recognizing both words matters.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Swapping 일출 (sunrise, 出 'come out') with 일몰 (sunset, 沒 'sink') — they share 日 but the second character flips the meaning; learn them as a pair.
Thinking 일출 and 해돋이 are different things — they are the same event; 해돋이 is just the native, warmer-sounding synonym.
Saying 일출에 갔어요 ('went at sunrise') when you mean 'went to SEE the sunrise' — use 일출(을) 보러 갔어요, since 보러 carries the purpose.

structuredNuance.t: 일출은 해돋이이고, 한국에서 이를 보는 것은 실제 문화적 무게를 지닌다 — 사람들이 새해 첫 해돋이인 새해 일출을 보며 소원을 빌러 동해 동쪽 해안으로 몰려간다. 명소, 시간, 보다, 그리고 새벽에 일어나야 하므로 이른 아침의 수고 단어 새벽, 일어나다와 어울린다.
진짜 일상 동의어가 있는데 고유어 해돋이(해 + 돋이, 돋다 '솟아오르다'에서)다. 일출은 한자어로 간판과 일기예보에 보이는 약간 더 격식 있는 말이고, 해돋이는 더 따뜻하게 들리며 말에서도 똑같이 흔하다 — 같은 현상이라 일출 보러 가요와 해돋이 보러 가요는 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
日出: 日 '해' + 出 '나오다/나가다'. 일몰(日沒, '해가 가라앉다')의 정확한 반의어다.
두 가지다: 일출(sunrise, 出 '나오다')을 닮은꼴 일몰(sunset, 沒 '가라앉다')과 바꿔 쓰지 말 것, 그리고 지나치게 격식 차리지 말 것 — 일상 대화에서 원어민은 해돋이라고 할 확률이 똑같이 높으니 두 단어를 다 알아듣는 게 중요하다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 일몰 means "sunset" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 일몰 (ilmol) = "sunset". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 일몰 시간 ("sunset time") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 일몰, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: What you check before heading to a viewpoint; e.g. 일몰 시간 맞춰서 가다.
노을 = the colored afterglow; 노을이 지다 = the evening glow forms — the everyday word in speech.
석양 (夕陽) = a more literary synonym you'll see in captions and signs.
명소 (名所) = noted place; west-coast 서해 beaches are classic 일몰 명소.

examples.en: The West Sea is famous for beautiful sunsets.
examples.note: -기로 유명하다 = 'famous for (doing/being)'; 서해 = West Sea, the classic sunset coast.

examples.ko: 일몰 시간에 딱 맞춰서 바닷가에 도착했어요.
examples.romanization: ilmol sigane ttang matchwoseo badatgae dochakaesseoyo.
examples.en: We arrived at the beach right on sunset time.
examples.note: 에 맞춰서 = 'timed to/in sync with'; 딱 = exactly/right on; 도착하다 = to arrive.

examples.ko: 바다 위로 해가 넘어가는데 노을이 너무 예뻐서 한참 동안 사진만 찍었어요.
examples.romanization: bada wiro haega neomeoganeunde noeuri neomu yeppeoseo hancham dongan sajinman jjigeosseoyo.
examples.en: As the sun went down over the sea the glow was so pretty I just took photos for ages.
examples.note: 해가 넘어가다 = the sun 'goes over'/sets; -는데 sets the scene; 한참 동안 = for a good while.

extendedVocab.nuance: 일몰 (日沒: 日 'sun' + 沒 'to sink/submerge') is sunset, the precise mirror of 일출 (日出, 'sun comes out'), and Korea's west coast (서해) is the textbook place to watch the sun sink into the sea. The register split matters: 일몰 is the slightly technical/written term for the EVENT (weather apps, signs, news give 일몰 시간), while in everyday speech people more often talk about the 노을 — the colorful afterglow in the sky — especially when sharing photos; 일몰 names the sinking sun, 노을 names the painted sky. A third synonym, 석양 (夕陽 'evening sun'), is more poetic/literary. It collocates with 시간, 명소, 보다 and the scene-setting verb 해가 넘어가다 (the sun goes down). The English-speaker pitfall is two-fold: don't swap 일몰 (sunset) with its lookalike pair-word 일출 (sunrise), and when you mean the pretty glow rather than the astronomical moment, reach for 노을, not 일몰 — saying 일몰이 예뻐요 is fine but Koreans more naturally say 노을이 예뻐요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Swapping 일몰 (sunset, 沒 'sink') with 일출 (sunrise, 出 'come out') — they are a fixed antonym pair; keep the second character straight.
Using 일몰 when you mean the pretty colored sky — that glow is 노을 (노을이 예뻐요), while 일몰 is the technical event.
Forgetting 노을이 지다 — note 지다 here means the glow 'forms/appears', it does NOT mean it 'fades away'.

structuredNuance.t: 일몰은 해넘이로, 한국 서해는 해가 바다로 가라앉는 것을 보기에 교과서적인 곳이다. 시간, 명소, 보다, 그리고 장면을 설정하는 동사 해가 넘어가다(해가 진다)와 어울린다.
어감 차이가 중요하다: 일몰은 현상을 가리키는 약간 기술적·문어적 용어다(날씨 앱, 간판, 뉴스가 일몰 시간을 알려 준다). 반면 일상 대화에서는, 특히 사진을 공유할 때, 사람들이 노을 — 하늘의 알록달록한 잔광 — 을 더 자주 말한다. 일몰은 가라앉는 해를, 노을은 물든 하늘을 가리킨다. 세 번째 동의어 석양(夕陽 '저녁 해')은 더 시적·문학적이다.
日沒: 日 '해' + 沒 '가라앉다/잠기다'. 일출(日出, '해가 나오다')의 정확한 거울이다.
두 가지다: 일몰(sunset)을 닮은꼴 짝 단어 일출(sunrise)과 바꿔 쓰지 말 것, 그리고 천문학적 순간이 아니라 예쁜 잔광을 뜻할 때는 일몰이 아니라 노을을 쓸 것 — 일몰이 예뻐요도 괜찮지만 한국 사람은 노을이 예뻐요라고 더 자연스럽게 말한다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 계곡 means "valley, mountain stream" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 계곡 (gyegok) means "valley, mountain stream". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 계곡 ("valley / mountain stream"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 계곡 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Plain noun covering both the rocky ravine and the cold stream inside it
물 attached; the icy water you actually dip your feet in
에서 marks where the activity happens, not 에
시원하다 is the habitual summer adjective for 계곡

examples.en: In summer the valley is the coolest.
examples.note: Simple opinion; 제일 = most, an easy superlative

examples.en: Dipping my feet in the stream feels so refreshing.
examples.note: 발(을) 담그다 = dip feet in, the set collocation; 담그니까 = 'now that I dip'

examples.ko: 주말에 가족이랑 계곡으로 물놀이 가기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: jumare gajogirang gyegogeuro mulnori gagiro haesseoyo.
examples.en: We decided to go play in the water at a valley with family this weekend.
examples.note: 으로 marks the destination you head toward; 물놀이 = water play

extendedVocab.nuance: 계곡 (溪谷, 'mountain-stream + valley') names both the V-shaped rocky ravine and, in everyday talk, the cold stream running through it — so 'I'm at the 계곡' usually means standing in the water. The dividing line vs 강 is size and feel: a 강 is a wide, slow river you cross by bridge, while a 계곡 is the narrow, boulder-strewn mountain version with fast cold water. Register is fully neutral and casual; everyone from kids to grandparents says it, and from June to August it's THE budget getaway word, glued to 시원하다 (refreshing) and 물놀이 (water play). The English-speaker pitfall is twofold: don't picture a soft green 'valley' (that scenic basin is closer to 골짜기 in literary use), and don't say 계곡에서 수영하다 expecting a pool — you 물놀이 or 발 담그다, since real 계곡 water is shallow, rocky and freezing.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 강 when you mean the mountain stream: 강 is a broad river (한강), but the cold rocky ravine you wade in is 계곡 — using 강 makes Koreans picture a totally different, bigger place.
Spelling it 게곡: the vowel is ㅖ (예), so it must be 계곡, never 게곡.
Treating 계곡 like a swimming pool with 수영하다 — Koreans say 물놀이 하다 or 발 담그다, because 계곡 water is shallow and rocky, not for laps.

structuredNuance.t: 계곡 names both the V-shaped rocky ravine and, in everyday talk, the cold stream running through it — so 'I'm at the 계곡' usually means standing in the water. Register is fully neutral and casual; everyone from kids to grandparents says it, and from June to August it's THE budget getaway word, glued to 시원하다 (refreshing) and 물놀이 (water play).
The dividing line vs 강 is size and feel: a 강 is a wide, slow river you cross by bridge, while a 계곡 is the narrow, boulder-strewn mountain version with fast cold water.
From 溪谷, 'mountain-stream + valley.'

The pitfall is twofold: don't picture a soft green 'valley' (that scenic basin is closer to 골짜기 in literary use), and don't say 계곡에서 수영하다 expecting a pool — you 물놀이 or 발 담그다, since real 계곡 water is shallow, rocky and freezing.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 폭포 means "waterfall" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "waterfall" is 폭포 (pokpo). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 폭포 ("waterfall"). Watch the particle attached to 폭포 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Neutral noun for any falls, tiny drop to famous tourist one
수(水) added; stresses the falling water, not the cliff
떨어지다 (to fall) is the natural verb for the water dropping
소리 = sound; the most-mentioned appeal of a falls

examples.en: Can you hear the waterfall over there?
examples.note: 들리다 = to be audible; simple yes/no question

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 폭포 물줄기가 엄청 세요.
examples.romanization: biga mani waseo pokpo muljulgiga eomcheong seyo.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the waterfall's flow is really strong.
examples.note: 물줄기 = jet/stream of water; 세다 = to be powerful

examples.ko: 폭포 앞에서 사진 찍으면 진짜 시원해 보여요.
examples.romanization: pokpo apeseo sajin jjigeumyeon jinjja siwonhae boyeoyo.
examples.en: Photos taken in front of a waterfall really look refreshing.
examples.note: 찍으면 = if/when you take (a photo); 보이다 = to look/appear

extendedVocab.nuance: 폭포 (瀑布, 'gushing-spread water') is the plain, neutral word for a waterfall of any size — a small drop tucked in a 계곡 or a famous tourist landmark alike — and it habitually travels with 소리 (sound) and 시원하다 (refreshing) when people explain why they like it. Unlike 계곡 (the ravine/stream you walk into) a 폭포 is the vertical fall itself, so the two often appear together: 계곡 따라 올라가면 폭포가 나와요. The near-synonym to know is 폭포수: 폭포 is the structure/place, while 폭포수 isolates the cascading water (the 수 is hanja 水, water). The English-speaker pitfall is the verb — in English a waterfall 'falls' but learners reach for 내리다; Korean specifically uses 떨어지다 (폭포가 떨어지다), and the water is 세다 (strong), never 빠르다 (fast).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Misspelling it 포포 or 폭보: the word is 폭포 — first syllable ends in ㄱ batchim, second begins with ㅍ.
Using 내리다 for the falling water (an English 'comes down' transfer) — the natural verb is 폭포가 떨어지다.
Forcing 폭포수 in casual speech: for everyday 'let's go see a waterfall,' plain 폭포 is right; 폭포수 narrowly means the falling water itself.

extendedVocab.explanation: 동굴 (donggul) = "cave". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 동굴 ("cave") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 동굴, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Natural rock cave; also figurative for a dark cozy hideout
탐험(探險) = adventurous exploring; standard for tourist caves
안 = the interior; 동굴 안은 시원해요
에 + 들어가다 for entering an enclosed space

examples.en: Inside the cave it's cool even in summer.
examples.note: 안은 = inside (as topic); caves stay cold year-round

examples.en: I checked out a lava cave in Jeju.
examples.note: 용암 = lava; 구경하다 is the go-to verb for sightseeing a place

examples.ko: 동굴이 너무 어두워서 손전등이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.romanization: dongguri neomu eoduwoseo sonjeondeungi kkok piryohaeyo.
examples.en: The cave is so dark that a flashlight is essential.
examples.note: 어둡다 → 어두워서 (ㅂ-irregular); 손전등 = flashlight

extendedVocab.nuance: 동굴 (洞窟, 'hollow-cavern') is the standard word for a natural cave, including Korea's famous limestone caverns and Jeju's UNESCO lava tubes that headline day trips, and it pairs almost reflexively with 구경하다 (to look around) or 탐험 (exploration). The synonym to separate it from is bare 굴: 굴 can mean 'cave/hole' but in food contexts means 'oyster,' so 굴 구경 is ambiguous while 동굴 구경 is unmistakably the cave. Register is neutral, and there's a warm figurative use — 동굴 같은 방 (a cave-like room) for a dark, snug space, or 동굴에 들어가다 jokingly for hiding away. The English-speaker pitfall is the particle: 'enter the cave' tempts 동굴로 들어가다, but for going INTO an enclosed space you want 동굴에 들어가다; 로 would imply the route/direction you took, not the entering itself.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Shortening to bare 굴 in travel talk: 굴 also means 'oyster,' so 굴 보러 가자 is confusing — use 동굴 to mean cave clearly.
Saying 동굴로 들어가다 for simply entering: use 동굴에 들어가다 (에), since 로 signals the direction/path rather than the act of going in.
Forgetting the ㅂ-irregular in 어둡다: 'because it's dark' is 어두워서, not 어둡어서.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 절벽 means "cliff" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 절벽 (jeolbyeok) means "cliff". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 절벽 ("cliff"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 절벽 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Sheer vertical rock face; also figurative for a dead end / crisis
끝 = edge/end; 절벽 끝에 서다 = stand at the edge
위 = top; sea views are described from 절벽 위
에서 marks the source point of the fall

examples.en: This cliff here is really tall.
examples.note: 높다 = tall/high; the basic adjective for a cliff

examples.ko: 위험하니까 절벽 끝에 너무 가까이 가지 마세요.
examples.romanization: wiheomhanikka jeolbyeok kkeute neomu gakkai gaji maseyo.
examples.en: It's dangerous, so don't go too close to the cliff edge.
examples.note: 가까이 = closely (adverb); -지 마세요 = polite 'please don't'

examples.ko: 저 해안 절벽이 사진 명소라서 사람이 많아요.
examples.romanization: jeo haean jeolbyeogi sajin myeongsoraseo sarami manayo.
examples.en: Those coastal cliffs are a famous photo spot, so it's crowded.
examples.note: 해안 = coast; 명소(名所) = famous/scenic spot

extendedVocab.nuance: 절벽 (絶壁, literally 'cut-off wall') is a sheer, vertical cliff or rock face — the 絶 ('to sever') captures how the ground just drops away, common along Korea's coastlines and hiking ridges where signs warn you to stay back. The contrast learners blur is 절벽 vs 언덕: an 언덕 is a gentle, walkable hill, whereas a 절벽 is a vertical drop you could fall off, so they are opposites in steepness, not synonyms. Register is neutral, but 절벽 carries a vivid figurative life — 절벽 끝에 몰리다 (driven to the cliff's edge) means pushed to the brink, and 재정 절벽 is the 'fiscal cliff.' The English-speaker pitfall is the particle of falling: you fall 절벽에서 떨어지다 (에서, the source) — using 에 there would wrongly point to a destination, and don't confuse the scenic 해안 절벽 with a soft 'bluff,' which Korean would not call 절벽.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling a gentle slope a 절벽: an 언덕 is a small hill you walk up, while 절벽 is a vertical drop — mixing them misstates how dangerous the place is.
Spelling it 절뼉 or 절벅: the correct form is 절벽 with ㄹ batchim on the first syllable.
Saying 절벽에 떨어지다 for falling off: use 절벽에서 떨어지다 (에서 = from the cliff), since 에 would suggest landing onto it.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 갯벌 means "tidal flat, mudflat" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "tidal flat, mudflat" is 갯벌 (gaetbeol). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 갯벌 ("tidal flat / mudflat"). Watch the particle attached to 갯벌 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Coastal mud exposed at low tide; a west-coast specialty
체험(體驗) = hands-on experience; a popular family activity

usagePhrases.en: dig for clams in the mudflat
usagePhrases.note: 캐다 = to dig up; the classic mudflat activity
드러나다 = to be revealed, as the tide goes out

examples.en: This is that famous mudflat.
examples.note: Simple identification; 이에요 = polite 'it is'

examples.en: At low tide the mudflat gets fully exposed.
examples.note: 썰물 = ebb/low tide; 쫙 = mimetic for spreading wide open

examples.ko: 갯벌은 미끄러우니까 꼭 장화 신고 가세요.
examples.romanization: gaetbeoreun mikkeureounikka kkok janghwa singo gaseyo.
examples.en: Mudflats are slippery, so be sure to wear rubber boots.
examples.note: 미끄럽다 → 미끄러우니까 (ㅂ-irregular); 장화 = rubber boots

extendedVocab.nuance: 갯벌 is the soft, muddy tidal flat that emerges at low tide — a defining feature of Korea's West and South coasts and a beloved hands-on 체험 where families go 조개 캐기 (clam digging). It's a pure native-Korean compound, 개 ('seaside/inlet') + 벌 ('open flat'), joined with a 사이시옷 that adds the ㅅ batchim → 갯벌, which is why the spelling matters. The contrast to nail is 갯벌 vs 해변/모래사장: a 해변 is a firm sandy beach you sunbathe on, while a 갯벌 is wet mud that only exists when the tide is OUT and is tied to 썰물 (low tide) and 밀물 (high tide). The English-speaker pitfall is treating any shoreline as 갯벌 — it specifically means the mud-at-low-tide zone, so don't use it for a regular sandy 해변; also note Korea's 갯벌 are UNESCO-listed, so locals say it with pride, not as 'just mud.'
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing 개벌 or 갯펄: standard spelling keeps the 사이시옷 ㅅ batchim → 갯벌.
Calling a sandy beach 갯벌: 갯벌 is mud exposed at low tide, while a firm sandy shore is 해변 / 모래사장 — they are different terrains.
Forgetting the ㅂ-irregular in 미끄럽다: 'because it's slippery' is 미끄러우니까, not 미끄럽으니까.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 등대 means "lighthouse" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 등대 (deungdae) = "lighthouse". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 등대 ("lighthouse") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 등대, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Coastal light tower; a very common seaside photo landmark
Ports pair a red and a white one to mark the channel
불빛 = emitted light; what guides ships at night
구경 = casual sightseeing; everyday trip phrasing

examples.en: Can you see the red lighthouse over there?
examples.note: 보이다 = to be visible; simple pointing-out question

examples.en: At night the lighthouse beam is visible from far away.
examples.note: 멀리까지 = all the way far; 까지 = up to/as far as

examples.ko: 빨간 등대 쪽으로 산책하면 노을이 진짜 예뻐요.
examples.romanization: ppalgan deungdae jjogeuro sanchaekamyeon noeuri jinjja yeppeoyo.
examples.en: If you stroll toward the red lighthouse, the sunset is really pretty.
examples.note: 쪽으로 = in the direction of; 노을 = sunset glow

extendedVocab.nuance: 등대 (燈臺, 'lamp-platform/tower') is a lighthouse, and on Korean harbor breakwaters you'll famously see a 빨간 등대 (red) and a 하얀/하얀색 등대 (white) marking which side of the channel is which — a beloved backdrop for seaside walks, sunset photos and dates. The hanja 燈 ('lamp') links it to a family of light words, which is exactly the trap: don't confuse 등대 with 등 (a lamp/light) or with the unrelated 등산 (hiking) just because they share 등 sounds. Register is fully neutral and casual, and 등대 also carries a warm figurative sense of a guiding beacon (희망의 등대). The English-speaker pitfall is location particles: for 'meet at the lighthouse' Koreans say 등대 앞에서 / 등대 쪽에서 만나자, because 등대에서 만나자 sounds like meeting literally at its base; and the light it casts is 불빛, not just 빛.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Mixing up 등대 (lighthouse) with 등 (lamp) or 등산 (hiking): they share the 등 sound but are entirely different words.
Saying 등대에서 만나자 for a meetup point: more natural is 등대 앞에서 / 등대 쪽에서 만나자, since people gather near it, not at its base.
Using 빛 alone for the beam: the lighthouse's glow is 등대 불빛, the standard collocation.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 항구 means "harbor, port" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 항구 (hanggu) means "harbor, port". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 항구 ("harbor / port"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 항구 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: The whole working waterfront where boats dock
도시 = city; a proud set phrase (Busan is the classic)

usagePhrases.en: a ship comes into the harbor
usagePhrases.note: 에 + 들어오다 = to come in toward you

usagePhrases.en: a sashimi place near the harbor
usagePhrases.note: 횟집 = raw-fish restaurant; ports mean fresh seafood

examples.en: Busan is a big harbor.
examples.note: Simple statement; 항구예요 = polite 'is a harbor'

examples.ko: 저녁이 되면 항구에 배들이 하나둘 들어와요.
examples.romanization: jeonyeogi doemyeon hanggue baedeuri hanadul deureowayo.
examples.en: Come evening, ships come into the harbor one by one.
examples.note: 하나둘 = one by one; 들어오다 = come in

examples.ko: 항구 앞에서 갓 잡은 생선을 바로 팔아요.
examples.romanization: hanggu apeseo gat jabeun saengseoneul baro parayo.
examples.en: Right by the harbor they sell freshly caught fish on the spot.
examples.note: 갓 잡은 = freshly caught; 바로 = right away/right there

extendedVocab.nuance: 항구 (港口, 'port-mouth') is the harbor as a whole — the entire working waterfront of docks, boats and fish markets — strongly tied to Korea's seafood cities like 부산, 속초 and 통영, so it surfaces constantly in 회 (sashimi) trip talk, and 항구 도시 (port city) is a set phrase locals use with pride. The key synonym contrast is 항구 vs 부두: 항구 is the broad harbor area, while 부두 is the specific built pier/wharf where a ship actually ties up — 항구에 도착해서 부두에서 내렸다 shows both. The shared hanja 港 also links it to 공항(空港, airport), the second trap: same character, but 공항 is 'empty-port' = airport, totally different place. Register is neutral. The English-speaker pitfall is scope: don't use 항구 for the single pier you board from (that's 부두), and remember a ship 항구에 들어오다/들어가다 (에), since the harbor is the enclosed destination.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 항구 for a single pier: 항구 is the whole harbor, while the specific docking structure is 부두 — keep the two distinct.
Confusing 항구 (harbor) with 공항 (airport): both contain 港, but 공항 means airport — context and the 공(空, sky) make the difference.
Forgetting the verb pairing: a ship 항구에 들어오다 (에 marks the harbor it enters), not 항구를 들어오다.

extendedVocab.explanation: "pier, wharf, dock" is 부두 (budu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 부두 ("pier / wharf"). Watch the particle attached to 부두 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: The built structure where ships tie up and load
정박하다(碇泊) = to dock/anchor (slightly formal)
따라 = along; common stroll/date phrasing
여객선 = passenger ship; where island ferries leave

examples.en: You catch the boat at that pier.
examples.note: 타다 = to board; 에서 marks where you get on

examples.en: We looked at the sea while walking along the pier.
examples.note: 걸으면서 = while walking (ㄷ-irregular 걷다 → 걸으면서)

examples.ko: 섬에 가는 배는 저쪽 여객선 부두에서 출발해요.
examples.romanization: seome ganeun baeneun jeojjok yeogaekseon budueseo chulbalhaeyo.
examples.en: The boat to the island leaves from that passenger pier over there.
examples.note: 여객선 부두 = ferry terminal; 출발하다 = to depart

extendedVocab.nuance: 부두 (埠頭, 'wharf-head') is the concrete pier or wharf where boats physically tie up, load and unload — the built edge of the water, as opposed to 항구 (the whole harbor that surrounds it). You'll reach for it most when catching island ferries (여객선 부두) or strolling a photogenic waterfront, and it collocates with 정박하다 (to moor) and 따라 걷다 (walk along). The synonym line to hold is precisely 부두 vs 항구: 부두 is one specific structure, 항구 is the entire harbor district — slightly more concrete/technical, but still everyday. Register is neutral. The English-speaker pitfalls: don't swap 부두 and 항구 freely (English 'dock' blurs them, Korean doesn't), and watch the spelling — 부두, not 부뚜, because 부뚜막 is the ledge of a traditional stove, a completely unrelated word; and to board, you say 부두에서 타다 (에서, the place you board from).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 부두 and 항구 interchangeably: 부두 is the pier structure, 항구 is the whole harbor — English 'dock' collapses them, Korean keeps them apart.
Spelling it 부뚜: the word is 부두; 부뚜(막) is a stove ledge, an entirely different thing.
Saying 부두에 타다 for boarding: the natural form is 부두에서 (배를) 타다, since 에서 marks the place the action departs from.

structuredNuance.t: 부두 is the concrete pier or wharf where boats physically tie up, load and unload — the built edge of the water, as opposed to 항구 (the whole harbor that surrounds it). You'll reach for it most when catching island ferries (여객선 부두) or strolling a photogenic waterfront, and it collocates with 정박하다 (to moor) and 따라 걷다 (walk along). Register is neutral.
The synonym line to hold is precisely 부두 vs 항구: 부두 is one specific structure, 항구 is the entire harbor district — slightly more concrete/technical, but still everyday.

Don't swap 부두 and 항구 freely (English 'dock' blurs them, Korean doesn't), and watch the spelling — 부두, not 부뚜, because 부뚜막 is the ledge of a traditional stove, a completely unrelated word; and to board, you say 부두에서 타다 (에서, the place you board from).

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 들판 means "field, open plain" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 들판 (deulpan) = "field, open plain". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 들판 ("field / open plain") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 들판, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Wide open grassy or farm land in the countryside
넓다 → 넓은; the most natural pairing
펼쳐지다 = to spread open, used of scenery
가로지르다 = to cross/traverse

examples.en: I can see a wide open field outside the window.
examples.note: 창밖 = outside the window; 보이다 = to be seen

examples.en: When autumn comes, the fields turn yellow.
examples.note: 노랗게 = yellowly (ㅎ-irregular 노랗다); ripening rice

examples.ko: 탁 트인 들판에서 자전거 타니까 진짜 시원했어요.
examples.romanization: tak teuin deulpaneseo jajeongeo tanikka jinjja siwonhaesseoyo.
examples.en: Riding a bike across the wide-open field felt so refreshing.
examples.note: 탁 트이다 = to be wide open; 시원하다 here = liberating

extendedVocab.nuance: 들판 is a wide open field or plain — farmland, grassland, the scenery rolling past a countryside train window — and it carries a calm, spacious, rural mood, surfacing especially in 가을 (autumn) when the rice fields turn gold. It's a native compound, 들 ('open country/wild field') + 판 ('flat expanse'). The synonym to separate is 들판 vs 밭: a 밭 is a specific cultivated crop plot (a vegetable field you tend), whereas 들판 is the broad, scenic open expanse — so 밭에서 일하다 (work the field) but 들판이 펼쳐지다 (fields spread out before you). Register is neutral, slightly literary/scenic. The English-speaker pitfall is that English 'field' is too broad: a sports field is 운동장, a single crop field is 밭, an academic 'field' is 분야 — reach for 들판 only for the open rural plain, and pair it with 펼쳐지다 or 넓다 rather than translating 'a field of...' literally.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 들판 for a cultivated plot: a tended crop field is 밭, while 들판 is the broad open plain — 밭 is for working, 들판 is for the scenic sweep.
Translating every English 'field' as 들판: a sports field is 운동장 and an area of study is 분야 — 들판 is only the rural open expanse.
Spelling it 들빤 or 들반: the correct form is 들판 (ㄹ batchim + 판).

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 언덕 means "hill, slope" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 언덕 (eondeok) means "hill, slope". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 언덕 ("hill / gentle slope"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 언덕 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: A small rise, far smaller than a 산 (mountain)
위 = top; 언덕 위 카페 = a hilltop cafe
오르다 = to go up; also 언덕을 올라가다
가파르다 = steep; common for tiring uphill streets

examples.en: There's a house up on that hill.
examples.note: 위에 = on top of; 있다 = there is

examples.ko: 집까지 가는 길이 언덕이라서 좀 힘들어요.
examples.romanization: jipkkaji ganeun giri eondeogiraseo jom himdeureoyo.
examples.en: The way home is uphill, so it's a bit tiring.
examples.note: 언덕이라서 = because it's a slope; 힘들다 = to be tough

examples.en: In spring the hill blooms with tons of flowers.
examples.note: 잔뜩 = a whole lot; 피다 → 펴요 (to bloom)

extendedVocab.nuance: 언덕 is a hill or gentle slope — a small rise, far smaller than a 산 (mountain), but enough to make you huff on the walk home — and in Korean cities the hillside neighborhood and the 언덕 위 카페 (hilltop cafe with a view) are a real cultural thing. It's native Korean, and beyond a literal hill it doubles for the tiring incline of a street: 우리 집은 언덕에 있어요 means 'my place is up a slope.' The synonym/scale contrast is the heart of it — don't call a real mountain an 언덕; use 산 for anything you'd actually hike, 언덕 for the small walkable rise (and a steep paved one is 가파른 언덕 or 비탈/비탈길). Register is neutral, often a touch nostalgic. The English-speaker pitfall is that English 'hill' and 'mountain' overlap loosely, but Korean draws a firmer line: misusing 언덕 for 설악산 sounds comically small, while calling a neighborhood slope a 산 sounds overdramatic.

Calling a real mountain an 언덕: anything you hike is 산; 언덕 is reserved for small hills and slopes, so the scale would sound wrong.
Spelling it 언떡 or 언덬: the correct form is 언덕 (ㄴ batchim + 덕).
Reaching for 산 to describe a steep street: a tiring paved incline is an 언덕 (or 비탈길), not a 산.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 봉우리 means "peak, summit (of a mountain)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "peak, summit (of a mountain)" is 봉우리 (bonguri). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 봉우리 ("peak / summit"). Watch the particle attached to 봉우리 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: An individual mountain peak; a range has several
산 prefixed; a very common combined form
오르다 = to ascend; 정상까지 오르다 is similar
뾰족하다 = pointy; describes sharp summits

examples.en: That peak over there is the highest.
examples.note: 제일 높다 = the highest; simple comparison

examples.ko: 저 멀리 눈 덮인 봉우리가 보여요.
examples.romanization: jeo meolli nun deopin bonguriga boyeoyo.
examples.en: Off in the distance you can see a snow-covered peak.
examples.note: 눈 덮인 = snow-covered; 보이다 = to be visible

examples.ko: 가장 높은 봉우리까지 두 시간쯤 걸려요.
examples.romanization: gajang nopeun bongurikkaji du siganjjeum geollyeoyo.
examples.en: It takes about two hours to reach the highest peak.
examples.note: 가장 높은 = the highest; 걸리다 = to take (time)

extendedVocab.nuance: 봉우리 (the 봉 from hanja 峰, 'mountain peak,' plus a native ending) is a single peak or summit, and a ridge or range is understood as several 봉우리 strung together — hikers use it constantly for mountains like 설악산 and 지리산, and the combined 산봉우리 is equally common. The synonym contrast that trips people up is 봉우리 vs 정상: 봉우리 is any one peak among several, while 정상(頂上) is THE very top/highest point you're aiming for — so a mountain can have many 봉우리 but one 정상, and trail talk pairs them (이 봉우리 지나면 정상이에요). Register is neutral, common in hiking and scenery description. The two English-speaker pitfalls: don't equate 봉우리 with 정상 (peak-as-one-of-many vs the single summit), and crucially don't spell it 봉오리 — that's a flower bud, a completely different word, so 산 봉오리 would absurdly mean 'mountain flower-bud.'

Treating 봉우리 and 정상 as identical: 봉우리 is one peak among several, while 정상 is the single highest top — a range has many 봉우리 but one 정상.
Spelling it 봉오리: 봉오리 means a flower bud, so the mountain peak must be 봉우리 — a one-vowel slip changes the meaning entirely.
Dropping 산 when context is unclear: in mixed talk 산봉우리 makes 'mountain peak' explicit and avoids ambiguity.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 해변 means "beach, seashore" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 해변 (haebyeon) = "beach, seashore". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 해변 ("beach / seashore") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 해변, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about getting around, reservations, directions, photos, and emergency help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: The sandy shore zone; more 'beach' than the open 바다
산책 = stroll; a very common seaside activity
에서 marks where the activity happens
가 (edge) added; 해변가 카페 = a beachfront cafe

examples.en: In summer I went to Gangneung beach.
examples.note: 강릉 = Gangneung; 에 가다 = go to (a place)

examples.ko: 해변을 따라 걸으니까 노을이 너무 예뻤어요.
examples.romanization: haebyeoneul ttara georeunikka noeuri neomu yeppeosseoyo.
examples.en: Walking along the beach, the sunset was so pretty.
examples.note: 따라 = along; 노을 = sunset glow

examples.en: There weren't many people on the beach, so it was quiet.
examples.note: 별로 + 없다 = not many; 조용하다 = to be quiet

extendedVocab.nuance: 해변 (海邊, 'sea-edge') is specifically the sandy beach/shore strip, while 바다 is the sea itself — the distinction is concrete: you lay your towel and stroll on the 해변, but you swim in the 바다, so 해변에서 수영하다 sounds slightly off (you're on the sand, not in the water). East-coast spots like 강릉 and 속초 are the go-to 해변, and it collocates with 산책 (stroll) and 노을 (sunset). The other near-synonym is 해수욕장(海水浴場, 'sea-water-bathing place'): 해변 is the natural shore generally, whereas 해수욕장 is a designated, facility-equipped swimming beach (lifeguards, showers, the official summer-open kind) — overlapping but not identical. Register is neutral. The English-speaker pitfall is exactly that 바다/해변 split: English 'go to the beach' covers both lying out and swimming, but in Korean you 해변에 가다 to be on the shore and 바다에 들어가다 to get in the water.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Swapping 해변 (the shore) for 바다 (the sea): 해변에서 수영하다 sounds off because you swim in the water — say 바다에서 수영하다.
Treating 해변 and 해수욕장 as the same: 해수욕장 specifically means a designated swimming beach with facilities, while 해변 is the shore in general.
Carrying over English 'go to the beach' wholesale: Korean splits it into 해변에 가다 (be on the shore) vs 바다에 들어가다 (enter the water).
