extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 플라스틱 means "plastic" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "plastic" is 플라스틱 (peullaseutik). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 플라스틱 용기 ("plastic container"). Watch the particle attached to 플라스틱 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 용기 = container; the everyday word for tupperware-type food boxes.
플라스틱 + item to state what it is made of.
전자레인지 + 용(用, for-use); the spec to check before microwaving a container.
쓰레기 = trash; relevant because Korea's recycling sorting is strict.

examples.en: Is this plastic?
examples.note: Fast material check; 이거 + 명사 + 이에요? works for any 'what's this made of?' moment.

examples.en: Can I microwave this container?
examples.note: 돌리다 (to run/spin) is the casual verb for 'microwave it'; -아도 돼요? asks permission.

examples.ko: 저렴한 건 플라스틱이고 비싼 건 유리예요.
examples.romanization: jeoryeomhan geon peullaseutigigo bissan geon yuriyeyo.
examples.en: The cheap ones are plastic and the expensive ones are glass.
examples.note: -는 ... -고 ... contrasts two product tiers by price, a common in-store comparison.

extendedVocab.nuance: 플라스틱 is the all-purpose loanword for plastic, covering containers, chairs, and packaging — there is no everyday native synonym, so this borrowed word does all the work. Two contrasts matter when shopping: against 유리 (glass), where 플라스틱 is light and unbreakable but seen as less hygienic and not always microwave-safe; and against 비닐, which English lumps in as 'plastic' too but Korean keeps separate — 비닐 is thin film/sheeting (the 비닐봉지 plastic bag, plastic wrap), while 플라스틱 is rigid molded plastic (the box, the chair). Because Korea enforces 분리수거 (waste sorting) strictly, this word matters beyond the store. The English-speaker pitfall is pronunciation: it is not the two-beat English 'plastic' but a clean four-syllable 플·라·스·틱, and calling a 비닐봉지 a 플라스틱 봉지 will get a puzzled look.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling a plastic bag a 플라스틱 봉지. Thin film bags and wrap are 비닐 (비닐봉지, 비닐); 플라스틱 is rigid molded plastic like a box or chair.
Microwaving any 플라스틱 without checking. Only 전자레인지용 (microwave-safe) plastic is rated for heat — ask 전자레인지에 돌려도 돼요? first.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 유리 means "glass (material)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 유리 (yuri) = "glass (material)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 유리컵 ("glass cup") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 유리, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 컵 = cup; the standard drinking glass, written as one word.
Marketed as heat-safe and more hygienic than plastic ones.
강화(强化, strengthened) + 유리; what you buy as a phone screen protector or tough cookware.
(으)로 되다 = 'be made of'; a natural way to state material — 유리로 된 컵.

examples.en: Is this cup glass?
examples.note: Plain material check; 명사 + 이에요? is the all-purpose 'is this ___?' question.

examples.en: Since it's glass, I'm worried it might break.
examples.note: 깨지다 + V-(으)ㄹ까 봐 = worry that something might happen; -라서 supplies the reason.

examples.en: I'm planning to put a tempered glass on my phone.
examples.note: 붙이다 = to stick on; -(으)려고요 states your shopping intention politely.

extendedVocab.nuance: 유리 is glass as a material (Sino-Korean 琉璃, originally a word for colored glass/lapis), used for cups, containers, windows, and 강화유리 (tempered glass) screen protectors. Shoppers constantly weigh it against 플라스틱: 유리 is heavier and breakable but prized as cleaner and microwave/oven-safe. The synonym confusions for English speakers are two: 거울 (mirror) is a separate word — a mirror is made from 유리 but you call it a 거울, not 유리; and 잔, which is the counter/word for a glass-as-a-serving (a 와인 잔, '한 잔 더' = one more glass to drink) rather than the substance. Common collocations are 유리컵, 유리병, 유리 용기, 강화유리, and 유리가 깨지다 (the glass breaks). One more trap: 유리 is also a very common woman's given name, so in a sentence about a person it may be a name, not the material.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 유리 when you mean a mirror — a mirror is 거울. It is made of 유리, but you ask for a 거울 in the store.
Using 유리 for 'a glass' you drink from. The serving/counter word is 잔 (한 잔 더 주세요); 유리 is the raw material, 유리컵 is the physical cup.
Forgetting 유리 doubles as a girl's name. '유리가 예뻐요' could praise the glass or the person named Yuri — context decides.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 금속 means "metal" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 금속 (geumsok) means "metal". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 금속 알레르기 ("metal allergy"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 금속 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: The single most practical phrase — say it before buying earrings, watches, or belts.
재질(材質) = material/composition; staff use it when describing what a product is made of.
프레임 (frame) for glasses, beds, or furniture.
(으)로 되다 = 'be made of'; 금속으로 된 부분 = the metal part.

examples.en: Is this metal?
examples.note: Quick material check; useful for jewelry where you may react to certain metals.

examples.ko: 저 금속 알레르기 있어서 다른 거 없어요?
examples.romanization: jeo geumsok allereugi isseoseo dareun geo eopseoyo?
examples.en: I have a metal allergy, so don't you have something else?
examples.note: 있어서 (-아서, 'because I have') chains the reason to a polite request for an alternative.

examples.ko: 금속 부분이 녹스니까 물기를 닦아 주세요.
examples.romanization: geumsok bubuni nokseunikka mulgireul dakka juseyo.
examples.en: The metal part rusts, so please wipe off the moisture.
examples.note: 녹슬다 = to rust; -니까 gives the reason for the -아 주세요 request to wipe it dry.

extendedVocab.nuance: 금속 is the general category word for metal (Sino-Korean 金屬, 金 'gold/metal' + 屬 'belong to,' i.e. 'things in the metal family'). It is the umbrella; for a specific metal Koreans name it directly — 금 (gold, 金), 은 (silver, 銀), 철 (iron/steel, 鐵), 스테인리스 (stainless), 알루미늄 (aluminum) — so the key contrast to internalize is 금속 ≠ 금: 금속 is metal-in-general, while 금 is specifically gold (and a single character of the very same compound). The most useful real-life collocation is 금속 알레르기 (metal allergy), exactly what you say when earrings or a watch make your skin react. Other natural partners: 금속 재질, 금속 프레임, 금속이 녹슬다 (metal rusts). The English-speaker pitfall is reaching for 금 ('metal' sounds gold-ish) when you mean any metal, or using 철 (iron specifically) as if it meant metal generally.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 금 when you mean metal in general. 금 is gold specifically; the category is 금속. '금 알레르기' would mean a gold allergy, not a general metal allergy.
Using 철 (iron/steel) as a catch-all for metal. 철 is one specific metal; if you don't know which one, say 금속.
Treating 금속 like a brand of metal. It is just the category — to specify, name it: 스테인리스, 알루미늄, 은, etc.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 고무 means "rubber" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "rubber" is 고무 (gomu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 고무장갑 ("rubber gloves"). Watch the particle attached to 고무 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 고무 + 장갑; the dishwashing/cleaning gloves in every Korean kitchen.
고무 + 줄(string); also the stretchy elastic in a waistband.
밑창 = sole of a shoe; non-slip rubber soles are a selling point.
재질 = material; how staff describe what something is made of.

examples.ko: 설거지할 때 고무장갑 끼는 게 좋아요.
examples.romanization: seolgeojihal ttae gomujanggap kkineun ge joayo.
examples.en: It's good to wear rubber gloves when washing dishes.
examples.note: 끼다 = to put on (gloves); V-는 게 좋다 = 'it's good to,' the most common use of 고무.

examples.ko: 이 신발 밑창이 고무라서 안 미끄러워요.
examples.romanization: i sinbal mitchangi gomuraseo an mikkeureowoyo.
examples.en: This shoe's sole is rubber, so it isn't slippery.
examples.note: 미끄럽다 = slippery; -라서 ties the rubber sole to the non-slip result.

examples.en: The waist of these pants is elastic, so it's really comfy.
examples.note: 고무줄 here = the waistband elastic; -(이)라 gives the casual reason, 편하다 = comfortable.

extendedVocab.nuance: 고무 means rubber and feels fully native even though it entered Korean as a loanword (via Dutch/Japanese 'gom'). It shows up most in 고무장갑 (rubber gloves), an absolute staple you'll grab at any 마트 or 다이소, and in 고무줄, which usefully covers both a 'rubber band' and the stretchy 'elastic' in clothing waistbands — context decides which. The synonym/pitfall to watch is footwear: rubber rain boots are 장화, not 고무 신발, even though they're literally rubber, because Korean names them by function, not material. Likewise the bouncy 'rubber' of a tire is just 타이어, and a rubber eraser is 지우개 — you rarely say 고무 for these finished objects. Natural collocations: 고무장갑 끼다, 고무 밑창, 고무줄로 묶다 (tie with a rubber band), 고무가 늘어나다 (the rubber stretches).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling rain boots 고무 신발. Rubber rain boots are 장화 — Korean names them by use, not by the rubber they're made of.
Forgetting 고무줄 has two senses. It is both a 'rubber band' (고무줄로 묶다) and clothing 'elastic' (고무줄 바지); only context tells them apart.
Using 고무 for an eraser. A pencil eraser is 지우개, not 고무, even though older Korean and Japanese link the two.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 도자기 means "ceramic / pottery" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 도자기 (dojagi) = "ceramic / pottery". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 도자기 그릇 ("ceramic dish/bowl") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 도자기, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 그릇 = bowl/dish; the typical ceramic tableware.
컵 + 도자기 to pin down the material.
전통(傳統) = traditional; sold as Korean craft and souvenir pieces.
제품 = product; a category sign you'll see at homeware shops.

examples.en: Is this dish ceramic?
examples.note: Quick material check; matters because it affects price, weight, and microwave-safety.

examples.en: Ceramic breaks right away if you drop it.
examples.note: 떨어뜨리다 = to drop; -면 ... 바로 = 'as soon as / right away,' the fragility warning.

examples.ko: 인사동에서 예쁜 도자기 컵을 하나 샀어요.
examples.romanization: insadongeseo yeppeun dojagi keobeul hana sasseoyo.
examples.en: I bought a pretty ceramic cup in Insadong.
examples.note: Insadong is the go-to spot for traditional 도자기; 하나 = 'one (of them)' counts the item.

extendedVocab.nuance: 도자기 is the word for ceramics/pottery, a Sino-Korean compound (陶瓷器: 陶 'earthenware' + 瓷 'porcelain' + 器 'vessel') that literally bundles the two fired-clay families into 'fired-clay ware.' It runs from everyday dishes to prized craft pieces sold in places like Insadong, often labeled 전통 도자기. The synonym map is worth knowing: 도자기 is the umbrella, while 도기 (陶器) is coarser earthenware and 자기 (瓷器) is fine porcelain/china; for traditional Korean wares you'll also hear 백자 (white porcelain) and 청자 (celadon) as named subtypes. The English-speaker pitfall is two-fold: don't confuse glossy 도자기 with 유리 (glass) just because both shine — they're different materials and break differently; and don't microwave 도자기 that has gold or silver trim, because the metallic paint can spark. extendedVocab.explanation: 스테인리스 (seuteilliseu) means "stainless steel". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 스테인리스 텀블러 ("stainless steel tumbler"). usagePhrases.note: 텀블러 = tumbler; the insulated bottle everyone carries.
냄비 = pot; a common upgrade from coated pans because nothing peels.
Very common spoken contraction of 스테인리스 — you'll hear it shouted at markets.
식기(食器) = tableware; the metal bowls and spoons used in many homes.

examples.en: Is this tumbler stainless?
examples.note: Material check; matters for heat retention and whether it'll rust.

examples.en: Since it's stainless, it keeps heat well.
examples.note: 보온(保溫) = heat retention; -라서 links the material to its main selling point.

examples.en: Ma'am, is this stainless?
examples.note: 스뎅 is the natural spoken form you'd actually use at a market stall; 아주머니 addresses the vendor.

extendedVocab.nuance: 스테인리스 is the loanword for stainless steel, everywhere in Korean kitchens — 텀블러, 냄비, bowls, spoons. Two register notes are essential. Natural collocations: 스테인리스 냄비/텀블러/식기, 보온이 잘 되다, 코팅이 안 벗겨지다 (the coating doesn't peel), 녹이 안 슬다 (it doesn't rust). The pitfall for English speakers is over-spelling it as 스테인리스 스틸 and not recognizing the slang 스뎅.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 천 means "fabric / cloth" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "fabric / cloth" is 천 (cheon). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 천 가방 ("cloth / tote bag"). Watch the particle attached to 천 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: The fabric tote you use instead of plastic; very common in Korea.
소파 = sofa; the in-store either/or against a 가죽 (leather) sofa.
(으)로 되다 = 'be made of'; 천으로 된 가방 = a fabric bag.
부드럽다 = soft; describing texture while you shop.

examples.en: Is this sofa fabric or leather?
examples.note: A standard either/or question when furniture shopping; 천 vs 가죽 is the core split.

examples.ko: 천 가방은 가벼워서 장 볼 때 좋아요.
examples.romanization: cheon gabangeun gabyeowoseo jang bol ttae joayo.
examples.en: A cloth bag is light, so it's good for grocery shopping.
examples.note: 장(을) 보다 = to do grocery shopping; -아서 gives the reason it's handy.

examples.ko: 천이 얇아서 비치는데 다른 색 없어요?
examples.romanization: cheoni yalbaseo bichineunde dareun saek eopseoyo?
examples.en: The fabric is thin and see-through; don't you have another color?
examples.note: 얇다 = thin; 비치다 = to show through, a real clothing complaint, -는데 softens the request.

extendedVocab.nuance: 천 is the native general word for cloth/fabric — any soft woven textile, as opposed to 가죽 (leather), 플라스틱, or 금속. It's the everyday way to ask what something is made of: 천이에요, 가죽이에요? The synonym layer to sort out: 천 is the broadest term, 옷감 specifically means dressmaking fabric/'material for clothes,' and 원단 is the trade/industry word for bolt fabric you'd hear at a fabric market like Dongdaemun — so 천 is what you say in normal life, 원단 is shoptalk. Crucially, 천 is the umbrella, while 면 (cotton), 울 (wool), and 실크 (silk) are specific kinds of 천, so don't say 천 when you actually mean cotton. The headline English-speaker pitfall is the homophone: 천 is also the number 1,000 (千), spelled and pronounced identically — '천 원' is a thousand won, '천으로 된 가방' is a cloth bag, and only context separates them. Collocations: 천 가방, 천 소파, 천이 얇다/두껍다, 천을 자르다 (cut fabric).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 천 (cloth) with 천 (1,000). Same sound and spelling; '천 원' = a thousand won, '천 가방' = a cloth bag — context is your only guide.
Saying 천 when you specifically mean cotton. Cotton is 면; 천 is fabric in general, and 면/울/실크 are particular kinds of 천.
Using 원단 in casual talk. 원단 is the trade word for bolt fabric at a fabric market; in everyday speech just say 천.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 합성섬유 means "synthetic fiber" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 합성섬유 (hapseongseomyu) = "synthetic fiber". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 합성섬유 100% ("100% synthetic fiber") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 합성섬유, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: On the tags of cheaper clothing and sportswear; spoken '합성섬유 백 퍼센트'.
The most common specific 합성섬유 actually named on labels.
천연(天然) = natural; the opposite category — cotton, wool, silk.
소재 = material; how the fabric type is described on a spec line.

examples.en: Is this garment synthetic fiber?
examples.note: Material check; tells you how it'll wash, breathe, and wrinkle.

examples.en: Since it's synthetic, it doesn't wrinkle easily.
examples.note: 구겨지다 = to get wrinkled; -라서 ties wrinkle-resistance to the synthetic material.

examples.en: Do you prefer natural fibers or synthetic ones?
examples.note: The basic fabric either/or when shopping; parallel A가 좋아요, B가 좋아요? offers a choice.

extendedVocab.nuance: 합성섬유 is the umbrella term for man-made fabrics — a Sino-Korean compound (合成纖維: 合成 'synthesized/combined' + 纖維 'fiber'), literally 'synthesized fiber.' On labels its named members are things like 폴리에스터 (polyester), 나일론 (nylon), and 아크릴 (acrylic), so 폴리에스터 is a specific kind of 합성섬유, not a different category. The sharp contrast to lock in is 합성섬유 ↔ 천연섬유 (天然纖維, 'natural fiber'): they sit on opposite sides of the care label, with 면/울/실크 in the 천연 column. The practical trade-off — and the reason this word is worth knowing in humid Korea — is that 합성섬유 resists wrinkles and dries fast but breathes poorly, so summer wear in it can feel sticky while sportswear uses it on purpose for stretch and quick-dry. The English-speaker pitfall is treating 합성섬유 as automatically 'bad/cheap'; it's a neutral category, and registering it as the opposite of 천연섬유 (rather than as an insult) keeps your tag-reading accurate.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Mixing up 합성섬유 (synthetic) and 천연섬유 (natural). They're opposite columns on the care label — 면/울/실크 are 천연섬유, polyester/nylon are 합성섬유.
Thinking 폴리에스터 is separate from 합성섬유. Polyester is a kind of 합성섬유; the tag may name the specific fiber instead of the category.
Assuming 합성섬유 is always bad. It's neutral — sportswear is deliberately synthetic for stretch and quick-dry; the downside is mainly breathability in heat.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 사물함 means "locker" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 사물함 (samulham) means "locker". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 사물함 비밀번호 ("locker combination/PIN"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 사물함 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 비밀번호(秘密番號) = secret number; 다이얼식이면 '자물쇠 번호'라고도 함
조사 -에 = the destination you put something INTO, not -에서
안 열리다 = won't open (자동사 부정); 고장 났을 때 단골 표현
정리(整理) = sorting/clearing; 학기 말에 꼭 하는 일

examples.en: Where are the lockers?
examples.note: 위치를 묻는 가장 기본 문장; 장소 명사 + 이/가 어디예요?

examples.en: Textbooks are heavy, so I keep them in my locker.
examples.note: 두고 다니다 = leave it (there) and go about — 두다 'place' + -고 다니다 'habitually'

examples.ko: 사물함 번호가 기억이 안 나서 한참 헤맸어요.
examples.romanization: samulham beonhoga gieogi an naseo hancham hemaesseoyo.
examples.en: I couldn't recall my locker number, so I fumbled for a while.
examples.note: 기억이 안 나다 = (a memory) doesn't come — 나다는 저절로 떠오를 때, '안 기억하다'는 비문

extendedVocab.nuance: 사물함은 한자 私物函(사물·함)으로 '개인 물건을 넣는 상자', 즉 학교·헬스장·수영장·지하철역에 있는 개인 보관함을 두루 가리킵니다. 영어 locker를 옮긴 외래어 '라커/락커'는 헬스장·스키장에선 들리지만 학교 맥락에서는 거의 안 쓰고 사물함이 표준이에요. 비슷한 말로 '보관함'은 짐을 잠시 맡기는 코인 라커(물품보관함) 느낌이 강하고, 사물함은 한 사람이 학기 내내 전용으로 쓰는 칸이라는 점이 갈림선입니다. 자주 어울리는 말은 '사물함에 넣다/두다, 사물함을 열다, 사물함 비밀번호, 사물함 정리'. 영어식 함정은 두 가지인데, locker를 '연다'고 할 때 전원 켜는 켜다를 쓰면 안 되고(자물쇠는 열다/잠그다), 또 '사물함에서 넣다'처럼 -에서를 쓰면 틀립니다 — 넣는 방향은 -에, 꺼내는 출발점만 -에서예요.

'사물함에서 책을 넣었어요'는 조사 오류예요. 넣는 방향은 도착점 -에(사물함에 넣다)이고, -에서는 꺼낼 때(사물함에서 꺼내다) 씁니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 교무실 means "teachers' office, faculty room" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "teachers' office, faculty room" is 교무실 (gyomusil). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 교무실에 가다 ("go to the teachers' office"). Watch the particle attached to 교무실 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. usagePhrases.note: 선생님을 찾아갈 때; 도착지 -에

usagePhrases.en: please come to the teachers' office
usagePhrases.note: -로 = direction the listener should head toward

usagePhrases.en: wait in front of the faculty room
usagePhrases.note: 위치 명사 + 앞에서; 자주 만나는 장소 표현

usagePhrases.en: get called (in) to the teachers' office
usagePhrases.note: 불려가다 = be summoned (피동); 혼나는 뉘앙스

examples.en: Which floor is the faculty room on?
examples.note: 층 = floor counter; 길 찾을 때 기본 문장

examples.en: I went to the teachers' office during break and asked a question.
examples.note: 쉬는 시간 = the break between classes (쉬다 'rest' + -는 + 시간)

examples.ko: 담임 선생님이 교무실에 안 계셔서 메모를 남겼어요.

examples.en: My homeroom teacher wasn't in the faculty room, so I left a note.
examples.note: 계시다 = honorific 있다 — 선생님이 주어라 반드시 높임

extendedVocab.nuance: 교무실은 한자 敎務室(교무·실), 글자 그대로 '가르치는 업무(敎務)를 보는 방'으로, 선생님들이 함께 쓰는 사무 공간이에요. 가장 헷갈리는 이웃 단어가 '사무실'인데, 사무실(事務室)은 일반 회사·관공서의 업무 공간을 뜻하고 학교 선생님들의 방은 콕 집어 교무실이라 부릅니다(학교 행정·돈 처리는 따로 '행정실'). 학생에게는 칭찬보다 지적받으러 가는 약간 긴장되는 장소라 '교무실에 불려가다, 교무실로 따라와'처럼 혼나는 상황과 자주 묶입니다. 자연스러운 짝은 '교무실에 가다/들르다, 교무실 앞, 교무실로 오세요'. 영어식 함정은 office를 무조건 '사무실'로 직역하는 것 — teachers' office는 교무실이라야 자연스럽고, 또 그 안의 선생님은 주체 높임이라 '있어요'가 아니라 '계세요'를 써야 합니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'사무실'과 혼동하지 마세요. 학교 선생님들의 방은 교무실, 일반 회사·관공서의 방은 사무실입니다.
선생님이 주어일 땐 높임을 쓰세요. '선생님이 교무실에 있어요'는 어색하고 '계세요'가 맞습니다.
학교의 돈·서류 처리하는 곳까지 교무실이라 하면 부정확해요. 그쪽은 보통 '행정실'이라고 부릅니다.

영어식 함정은 office를 무조건 '사무실'로 직역하는 것 — teachers' office는 교무실이라야 자연스럽고, 또 그 안의 선생님은 주체 높임이라 '있어요'가 아니라 '계세요'를 써야 합니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 담임 means "homeroom teacher" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 담임 (damim) = "homeroom teacher". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 담임 선생님 ("homeroom teacher") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 담임, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 부를 때는 반드시 뒤에 '선생님'을 붙임
친구끼리 3인칭으로 가리킬 때 줄여 부름

usagePhrases.en: take charge of a homeroom class
usagePhrases.note: 맡다 = take on (a duty); 선생님 입장의 표현

usagePhrases.en: a meeting with the homeroom teacher
usagePhrases.note: 면담(面談) = face-to-face talk; 상담 신청할 때

examples.en: Who is our homeroom teacher?
examples.note: 사람을 묻는 기본 문장; 담임 뒤에 선생님을 붙인 정중형

examples.ko: 우리 담임 선생님은 진짜 잘 챙겨 주세요.
examples.romanization: uri damim seonsaengnimeun jinjja jal chaenggyeo juseyo.
examples.en: Our homeroom teacher really looks out for us.
examples.note: 챙겨 주다 = look after — 챙기다 'see to' + -아 주다 '(do) for someone'

examples.en: I requested a career counseling session with my homeroom teacher.
examples.note: 께 = honorific of -에게 (to a respected person)

extendedVocab.nuance: 담임은 한자 擔任(담·임), '맡아서(擔) 책임진다(任)'는 뜻으로, 한 반을 1년간 전담해 출결·생활지도·상담까지 책임지는 선생님이에요. 영어엔 딱 떨어지는 말이 없어 homeroom teacher로 옮기지만, 한국의 담임은 단순히 조회시간만 맡는 게 아니라 학생 생활 전반을 챙긴다는 점이 더 강합니다. 비슷해 보이는 '교과 선생님(과목만 가르치는 분)'과 달리 담임은 '우리 반을 책임지는 한 분'이라는 게 갈림선이고, 회사의 '팀장'에 비유되기도 하지만 그 말과 섞어 쓰진 않아요. 핵심 주의점: 담임은 직책 이름이자 사람을 가리키므로 친구끼리 '우리 담임 바뀌었어'처럼 3인칭으로는 줄여 써도, 선생님을 직접 부르거나 그분 앞에서는 반드시 '담임 선생님'이라고 해야 예의에 맞습니다. '담임!'이라고만 부르면 무례하게 들려요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
선생님을 직접 부를 때 '담임!'이라고만 하면 무례합니다. 호칭은 꼭 '담임 선생님'이라고 하세요.
담임은 사람·직책을 가리키므로 '담임 수업, 담임 과목'처럼 과목 뜻으로 쓰면 안 됩니다. 그건 '교과/과목 선생님'입니다.
'우리 담임 선생님이 가르쳐요'에서 선생님이 주어면 높임을 챙기세요 — '가르쳐 주세요/가르치세요'가 자연스럽습니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 반장 means "class president, class leader" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 반장 (banjang) means "class president, class leader". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 반장 선거 ("class president election"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 반장 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 선거(選擧) = election; 학기 초에 반에서 뽑음
뽑다 = pick/elect (by vote)
되다 takes -이/가 for the resulting role
부-(副) = vice/deputy; 반장을 돕는 자리

examples.en: Are you the class president?
examples.note: 이다 의문형; 가장 단순한 확인 문장

examples.en: Minsu became class president this semester.
examples.note: 되다 앞 주어는 -이/가(민수가 되다), 결과 신분은 보어

examples.en: Since I'm the class president, the responsibility feels heavy.
examples.note: -라서 = because (이다 + -아서, 명사 뒤 이유)

extendedVocab.nuance: 반장은 한자 班長(반·장), '반(班)의 우두머리(長)'로, 반을 대표하고 선생님과 학생 사이를 잇는 학생 리더예요(보좌역은 부반장, 副班長). 끝 글자 -長은 회장(會長)·팀장·반장처럼 '~의 장(長), 우두머리'를 만드는 한자라, 회사의 팀장이나 군대의 분대장과 같은 계열이지만 학급 대표는 학교 맥락의 반장으로 못박아 씁니다. 비슷한 '회장(會長)'은 전교를 대표하는 전교회장처럼 더 큰 조직을 이끌 때 쓰니 한 반의 대표는 반장이 맞아요. 보통 학기 초 투표(반장 선거)로 뽑고 책임감 있는 역할로 여겨집니다. 영어식 함정은 조사 생략 — '반장 되다'처럼 -이를 빼면 어색하고 '반장이 되다'라야 하며, become을 옮길 때 결과 신분에 -이/가가 붙는 한국어 특유의 구조('의사가 되다, 반장이 되다')를 기억하세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'반장 되다'처럼 조사를 빼면 어색합니다. 결과 신분에는 -이/가를 붙여 '반장이 되다'라고 하세요.
회사 직책 '팀장'이나 군대 '분대장'과 섞어 쓰지 마세요. 학급 대표는 학교 맥락의 반장입니다.
한 반의 대표를 '회장'이라 하면 과해요. 회장은 전교회장처럼 더 큰 조직의 대표에게 씁니다.

structuredNuance.t: 한자 班長(반·장), '반(班)의 우두머리(長)'로, 반을 대표하고 선생님과 학생 사이를 잇는 학생 리더예요(보좌역은 부반장, 副班長). 보통 학기 초 투표(반장 선거)로 뽑고 책임감 있는 역할로 여겨집니다.

끝 글자 -長은 회장(會長)·팀장·반장처럼 '~의 장(長), 우두머리'를 만드는 한자라, 회사의 팀장이나 군대의 분대장과 같은 계열이지만 학급 대표는 학교 맥락의 반장으로 못박아 씁니다.
영어식 함정은 조사 생략 — '반장 되다'처럼 -이를 빼면 어색하고 '반장이 되다'라야 하며, become을 옮길 때 결과 신분에 -이/가가 붙는 한국어 특유의 구조('의사가 되다, 반장이 되다')를 기억하세요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 조퇴 means "leaving school (or work) early" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "leaving school (or work) early" is 조퇴 (jotoe). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 조퇴하다 ("leave early (before the day ends)"). Watch the particle attached to 조퇴 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 명사 + 하다 동사화
신청(申請) = application; 담임·보건실에 함
가장 흔한 사유; -아서 = reason

usagePhrases.en: logging it as an early dismissal
usagePhrases.note: 처리(處理) = handling; 출결에 기록될 때

examples.en: I'm leaving early today.
examples.note: 가장 짧은 통보형; 명사 + 하다 현재형

examples.en: I had a fever, so I left early during third period.
examples.note: 교시(校時) = the period counter (1교시, 2교시…)

examples.ko: 조퇴하려면 담임 선생님 허락을 받아야 해요.
examples.romanization: jotoeharyeomyeon damim seonsaengnim heorageul badaya haeyo.
examples.en: To leave early, you need the homeroom teacher's permission.
examples.note: -(으)려면 = if you intend to (do); 의도+조건

extendedVocab.nuance: 조퇴는 한자 早退(조·퇴), '이를 조(早) + 물러날 퇴(退)' = 정해진 시간보다 일찍 자리를 뜨는 것으로, 학교든 회사든 다 씁니다. 단순한 '일찍 가다/먼저 가다'와의 결정적 차이는, 조퇴는 정당한 사유(아픔·일정)와 허락이 있어야 하고 출결에 기록되는 공식 행위라는 점이에요 — 그래서 결석·지각·조퇴가 한 묶음으로 다닙니다. 반대 방향(늦게 옴)은 지각(遲刻)이고, 아예 안 옴은 결석(缺席)이니 세트로 외우면 좋아요. 자연스러운 짝은 '조퇴하다, 조퇴(를) 신청하다, 조퇴 처리, 몸이 안 좋아서 조퇴'. 영어식 함정 둘: leave early를 직역해 '조퇴를 가다'라고 하면 비문이라 '조퇴하다/조퇴 신청을 하다'로 써야 하고, 친구랑 그냥 일찍 놀러 나갈 땐 조퇴가 아니라 '먼저 갈게/일찍 나갈게'라고 합니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'조퇴를 가다'는 틀려요. 동사화는 '조퇴하다', 절차를 말하면 '조퇴 신청을 하다'입니다.
그냥 '일찍 가다'와 다릅니다. 조퇴는 허락·기록이 따르는 공식 표현이라, 친구와 일찍 놀러 갈 땐 안 씁니다.
늦게 오는 것까지 조퇴라 하면 틀려요. 늦게 오는 건 '지각', 안 오는 건 '결석'으로 구분하세요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 결석 means "absence (from school)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 결석 (gyeolseok) = "absence (from school)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 결석하다 ("be absent") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 결석, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 명사 + 하다; 주어가 빠지는 행위
무단(無斷) = without permission; 허락 없이 빠짐
병결(病缺) = 병으로 인한 결석의 줄임말
사유(事由) = grounds/reason; 출결 처리 때 묻는 말

examples.en: One person is absent today.
examples.note: 명 = counter for people; 출석 확인 기본 문장

examples.en: My cold was bad, so I was absent yesterday.
examples.note: 심하다 = be severe; -아서로 이유 연결

examples.ko: 개근상을 받으려면 결석이 한 번도 없어야 해요.
examples.romanization: gaegeunsangeul badeuryeomyeon gyeolseogi han beondo eopseoya haeyo.
examples.en: To get the perfect-attendance award, you must have zero absences.
examples.note: 개근상(皆勤賞) = the award for never missing a day

extendedVocab.nuance: 결석은 한자 缺席(결·석), '빌 결(缺) + 자리 석(席)' = '자리가 비다', 즉 수업에 나오지 않는 것으로 출석(出席)의 정반대예요. 같은 缺을 회사에 쓰면 결근(缺勤)이 되는데, 이게 가장 중요한 갈림선입니다 — 결석은 학교 수업, 결근은 직장 근무에 빠질 때라 섞으면 안 돼요. 사유에 따라 병결(아파서)·무단결석(허락 없이)으로 나뉘고, 특히 무단결석은 부정적으로 여겨져 생활기록부나 성적에 영향을 줄 수 있는 무거운 말입니다. 같은 출결 식구로 지각(늦게 옴)·조퇴(일찍 감)가 함께 다녀요. 영어식 함정: be absent를 옮길 때 '결석을 가다/결석을 하러 가다'처럼 쓰면 비문이고 '결석하다'가 맞으며, 직장에 안 나간 걸 결석이라 하면 어색하니 그땐 결근을 쓰세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'결석을 가다'는 틀려요. '결석하다'로 동사화하거나 '결석을 하다'로 씁니다.
직장에 안 나가는 것을 결석이라 하면 어색합니다. 회사 결근, 학교 결석으로 구분하세요.
무단결석을 가벼운 말로 여기지 마세요. 생활기록부에 남는 부정적 표현이라 단순 '안 갔다'와 무게가 다릅니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 소풍 means "school outing, picnic, field trip" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 소풍 (sopung) means "school outing, picnic, field trip". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 소풍을 가다 ("go on an outing"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 소풍 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 동사는 '하다'가 아니라 '가다'와 어울림
기다려지는 날; 날 = day
보통 봄·가을에 감

usagePhrases.en: the packed lunch for the outing
usagePhrases.note: 도시락 = boxed lunch; 소풍의 핵심

examples.en: We're going on an outing tomorrow.
examples.note: 가장 단순한 예고; 소풍 + 가다

examples.en: We went on the outing and ate gimbap with friends.
examples.note: -이랑 = casual 와/과 (and/with), 받침 뒤

examples.en: The outing got postponed to next week due to rain.
examples.note: 미뤄지다 = get postponed (미루다의 피동); 우천(雨天)=rainy weather

extendedVocab.nuance: 소풍은 학생들이 학교 밖 공원·산으로 나가 도시락을 먹고 노는 가벼운 하루 나들이로, 한자는 보통 逍風/消風(거닐며 바람을 쐬다)로 풀이됩니다(다만 일상에선 한자 없이 순우리말처럼 씁니다). 같은 학교 행사라도 갈림선이 분명한데, 박물관·유적지처럼 학습 목적이 강하면 '현장학습', 며칠 묵으며 멀리 가면 '수학여행', 그냥 즐겁게 노는 당일치기가 소풍이에요. 일반 어른의 주말 나들이는 소풍 대신 '나들이/피크닉'을 더 쓰고, 소풍은 학창 시절의 설레는 행사라는 색이 짙습니다. 자연스러운 짝은 '소풍을 가다, 소풍 날, 소풍 도시락, 봄/가을 소풍'. 영어식 함정 둘: picnic이 동사로 쓰인다고 '소풍하다'라고 하면 어색하고 반드시 '소풍(을) 가다'이며, day trip이라도 며칠짜리 여행을 소풍이라 부르면 안 됩니다 — 그건 수학여행이에요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'소풍하다'는 어색해요. 동사는 '소풍(을) 가다/다녀오다'와 어울립니다.
여러 날 멀리 가는 여행은 소풍이 아니라 '수학여행'입니다. 소풍은 보통 하루짜리예요.
교육 목적이 뚜렷한 견학은 '현장학습'이라 부르는 게 더 정확합니다. 노는 데 초점이면 소풍입니다.

extendedVocab.english: deskmate, the person you sit next to
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 짝꿍 means "deskmate, the person you sit next to" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "deskmate, the person you sit next to" is 짝꿍 (jjakkkung). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 짝꿍이 되다 ("become deskmates"). Watch the particle attached to 짝꿍 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 자리 배치로 결정; 되다 + -이/가
자리를 바꿨을 때
떠들다 = make noise/chatter; 수업 중 흔한 일
자리 바꾸기(자리 배치 변경)

examples.en: Who's your deskmate?
examples.note: 반말 의문; 친구끼리 쓰는 가장 흔한 문장

examples.en: My deskmate lent me an eraser.
examples.note: 빌려주다 = lend (빌리다 'borrow'와 방향 반대!)

examples.en: I went to eat the school lunch with my deskmate.
examples.note: -(으)러 가다 = go in order to (do); 급식 = school-provided meal

extendedVocab.nuance: 짝꿍은 한자어가 아니라 순우리말로, '짝(둘이 한 쌍을 이룸)'에 친근한 접미사 '-꿍'이 붙어 만들어진 다정한 애칭이에요 — 교실에서 같은 책상에 나란히 앉는 옆자리 친구를 부르는 말입니다. 중립적인 '짝'이나 설명조의 '옆자리 친구'와의 차이는 온도예요. 짝꿍은 어린 학생들이 특히 즐겨 쓰는 귀엽고 친밀한 말이라, 어른들 사이에선 아주 가까운 단짝이나 부부를 장난스럽게 '내 짝꿍'이라 부르기도 합니다. 자연스러운 짝은 '짝꿍이 되다, 새 짝꿍, 짝꿍이랑 ~하다, 짝꿍을 바꾸다'. 영어식 함정: deskmate를 격식 있는 글이나 공식 문서에 그대로 짝꿍으로 옮기면 너무 구어적이라 어색하니 그땐 '옆자리 친구/같은 분단 학생'이라 하고, 또 혼자 앉는 1인 책상에는 짝꿍이 없습니다 — 둘이 나란히 앉을 때만 성립하는 말이에요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
짝꿍은 구어체 애칭이라 공식 문서·보고서엔 어울리지 않아요. 격식 있는 상황에선 '옆자리 친구'라고 하세요.
혼자 앉는 자리엔 짝꿍이 없습니다. 두 명이 나란히 앉을 때 성립하는 말이에요.
'짝꿍이 빌렸어요'로 lent를 말하면 방향이 반대예요. 남이 내게 빌려준 것이면 '빌려줬어요(빌려주다)'입니다.

structuredNuance.t: 한자어가 아니라 순우리말로, '짝(둘이 한 쌍을 이룸)'에 친근한 접미사 '-꿍'이 붙어 만들어진 다정한 애칭이에요 — 교실에서 같은 책상에 나란히 앉는 옆자리 친구를 부르는 말입니다. 짝꿍은 어린 학생들이 특히 즐겨 쓰는 귀엽고 친밀한 말이라, 어른들 사이에선 아주 가까운 단짝이나 부부를 장난스럽게 '내 짝꿍'이라 부르기도 합니다. 자연스러운 짝은 '짝꿍이 되다, 새 짝꿍, 짝꿍이랑 ~하다, 짝꿍을 바꾸다'.
중립적인 '짝'이나 설명조의 '옆자리 친구'와의 차이는 온도예요. 짝꿍은 더 귀엽고 친밀한 색을 띱니다.
deskmate를 격식 있는 글이나 공식 문서에 그대로 짝꿍으로 옮기면 너무 구어적이라 어색하니 그땐 '옆자리 친구/같은 분단 학생'이라 하고, 또 혼자 앉는 1인 책상에는 짝꿍이 없습니다 — 둘이 나란히 앉을 때만 성립하는 말이에요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 받아쓰기 means "dictation, spelling test" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 받아쓰기 (badasseugi) = "dictation, spelling test". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 받아쓰기 시험 ("dictation test") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 받아쓰기, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 시험(試驗) = test; 초등 저학년에서 자주 봄
명사화된 동작 + 하다
점(點) = point/mark; 만점을 받았을 때
연습(練習) = practice; 집에서 미리 함

examples.en: Is there a dictation today?
examples.note: 있다 의문; 일정 확인하는 기본 문장

examples.en: I got two wrong on yesterday's dictation.
examples.note: 틀리다 = get (it) wrong (맞다 'be correct'의 반대)

examples.ko: 선생님이 천천히 불러 주셔서 다 받아썼어요.
examples.romanization: seonsaengnimi cheoncheonhi bulleo jusyeoseo da badasseosseoyo.
examples.en: The teacher read it out slowly, so I wrote it all down.
examples.note: 불러 주다 = read aloud for someone (부르다 + -아 주다)

extendedVocab.nuance: 받아쓰기는 순우리말 합성어로, '받아(받다 '받아 적다'의 받아)' + '쓰기(쓰다의 명사형)' = 선생님이 불러 주는 말을 귀로 받아 정확한 맞춤법으로 적는 연습이자 시험이에요. 가장 헷갈리는 이웃이 '필기'와 '베끼기'인데, 받아쓰기는 칠판을 안 보고 '듣고' 적는 것이고, 칠판·교재를 보고 옮겨 적으면 그건 필기(筆記)나 베끼기라 갈림선이 분명합니다(영어로도 dictation은 '듣고 쓰기'). 주로 초등학교 저학년에서 한글 맞춤법을 익히려고 하지만, 외국어 학습에서도 듣기·철자 훈련으로 흔히 활용돼요. 자연스러운 짝은 '받아쓰기 시험, 받아쓰기를 하다, 받아쓰기 100점, 받아쓰기 연습'. 영어식 함정: 동사로 쓸 땐 한 단어 '받아쓰다(받아써요/받아썼어요)'를 쓰고, '받아쓰기하다'보다 '받아쓰기를 하다'가 더 자연스럽다는 점을 기억하세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
받아쓰기는 '듣고 적는' 것이에요. 칠판이나 책을 보고 옮겨 적는 건 받아쓰기가 아니라 '필기/베끼기'입니다.
동사로 쓸 땐 '받아쓰다'로 한 단어예요. '받아쓰기하다'보다 '받아쓰기를 하다'가 자연스럽습니다.
'받아적기'라고도 쓸 수 있지만, 학교 시험을 가리키는 표준 명칭은 '받아쓰기'입니다.

structuredNuance.t: 순우리말 합성어로, '받아(받다 '받아 적다'의 받아)' + '쓰기(쓰다의 명사형)' = 선생님이 불러 주는 말을 귀로 받아 정확한 맞춤법으로 적는 연습이자 시험이에요. 주로 초등학교 저학년에서 한글 맞춤법을 익히려고 하지만, 외국어 학습에서도 듣기·철자 훈련으로 흔히 활용돼요. 자연스러운 짝은 '받아쓰기 시험, 받아쓰기를 하다, 받아쓰기 100점, 받아쓰기 연습'.
가장 헷갈리는 이웃이 '필기'와 '베끼기'인데, 받아쓰기는 칠판을 안 보고 '듣고' 적는 것이고, 칠판·교재를 보고 옮겨 적으면 그건 필기(筆記)나 베끼기라 갈림선이 분명합니다(영어로도 dictation은 '듣고 쓰기').
동사로 쓸 땐 한 단어 '받아쓰다(받아써요/받아썼어요)'를 쓰고, '받아쓰기하다'보다 '받아쓰기를 하다'가 더 자연스럽다는 점을 기억하세요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 가정통신문 means "school-to-home notice, parent newsletter" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 가정통신문 (gajeongtongsinmun) means "school-to-home notice, parent newsletter". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 가정통신문을 받다 ("receive a school notice"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 가정통신문 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 보통 학생 편에 전달됨
확인(確認) = checking; 부모가 읽고 서명

usagePhrases.en: the reply slip for the school notice
usagePhrases.note: 회신(回信) = reply; 통신문에 딸려 잘라 보내는 답신 종이
-에 적혀 있다 = (info) is written in (상태)

examples.en: Did a school notice come (home)?
examples.note: 오다 의문; 부모가 자주 묻는 기본 문장

examples.ko: 엄마, 가정통신문에 사인 좀 해 주세요.
examples.romanization: eomma, gajeongtongsinmune sain jom hae juseyo.
examples.en: Mom, please sign the school notice.
examples.note: 사인하다 = to sign (loanword, casual); '서명하다'가 더 격식

examples.ko: 가정통신문을 안 내서 선생님이 다시 주셨어요.
examples.romanization: gajeongtongsinmuneul an naeseo seonsaengnimi dasi jusyeosseoyo.
examples.en: I didn't turn the notice in, so the teacher gave me another.
examples.note: 내다 = hand in / submit

extendedVocab.nuance: 가정통신문은 한자 家庭通信文(가정·통신·문), 글자 그대로 '가정(家庭)에 보내는 통신(通信)의 글(文)'로, 학교가 학부모에게 행사·준비물·일정을 알리려고 학생 편에 보내는 안내문이에요(요즘은 앱 알림으로도 옴). 일반 회사의 '공지(公知)'나 안내문과의 결정적 차이는 방향과 대상이에요 — 공지는 조직 안 구성원에게 두루 알리는 것이고, 가정통신문은 학교에서 '가정(부모)으로' 콕 집어 보내는 문서라 보통 부모가 읽고 서명하거나 회신서를 돌려보내야 합니다. 그래서 한국에서 아이를 키우는 사람이 꼭 알아야 하는 생활 단어예요. 자연스러운 짝은 '가정통신문을 받다/내다, 가정통신문 확인, 가정통신문에 서명하다, 회신서를 보내다'. 영어식 함정: notice를 그냥 '공지'로 옮기면 학교→가정 방향이 안 살고, 또 '받기만 하면 끝'이 아니라 서명·회신이 따르는 경우가 많으니 '확인하다'와 한 세트로 기억하세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
회사 '공지'와 혼동하지 마세요. 가정통신문은 학교가 '가정(부모)으로' 보내는 안내문입니다.
받는 걸로 끝나지 않을 때가 많아요. 서명·회신서가 필요한 경우가 흔하니 '확인하다'와 함께 기억하세요.
공식 서류엔 '사인'보다 '서명'이 적절해요. '사인'은 구어이고 학교 양식엔 '서명'을 씁니다.

extendedVocab.english: school snack shop, tuck shop, kiosk
extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 매점 means "school snack shop, tuck shop, kiosk" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "school snack shop, tuck shop, kiosk" is 매점 (maejeom). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 매점에 가다 ("go to the snack shop"). Watch the particle attached to 매점 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 쉬는 시간·점심시간에
인기 간식의 대명사
붐비다 = be crowded; 쉬는 시간엔 줄이 긺
운영하시는 분을 친근히 부르는 호칭

examples.en: Where is the snack shop?
examples.note: 위치 묻기; 장소 + 어디 있어요?

examples.en: At lunch I bought bread and milk at the snack shop.
examples.note: -에서 = the place where an action happens (구입 장소)

examples.ko: 쉬는 시간이 짧아서 매점은 늘 사람이 많아요.
examples.romanization: swineun sigani jjalbaseo maejeomeun neul sarami manayo.
examples.en: Because break is short, the snack shop is always crowded.
examples.note: 늘 = always; -아서로 이유 연결

extendedVocab.nuance: 매점은 한자 賣店(매·점), '팔 매(賣) + 가게 점(店)' = 학교·회사·병원·역 구내에 있는 작은 판매소로, 빵·음료·과자 같은 간단한 먹거리를 파는 곳이에요. 가장 헷갈리는 이웃이 '편의점'과 '가게'인데, 갈림선이 둘입니다 — 첫째, 매점은 보통 시설 '안(구내)'에 있고 거리의 독립 점포는 그냥 '가게/상점'이라 부르며, 둘째, 매점은 운영 시간(학교라면 수업 시간대)에만 열고 24시간·체인인 편의점(便宜店)과 규모·운영이 달라요. 학생에게는 쉬는 시간의 작은 즐거움이라 '매점 빵, 매점 가다'가 입에 붙습니다. 자연스러운 짝은 '매점에 가다, 매점에서 사다, 매점이 붐비다, 매점 아주머니'. 영어식 함정: store/shop을 무조건 매점이라 옮기면 안 돼요 — 길거리 상점은 가게, 동네 24시간 점포는 편의점이고, 매점은 어디까지나 시설 구내의 작은 판매소를 가리킵니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
거리의 일반 상점은 매점이 아니에요. 매점은 학교·회사·병원 등 시설 '안(구내)'의 작은 판매소입니다.
편의점과 혼동하지 마세요. 매점은 24시간 체인이 아니고 시설 운영 시간에만 엽니다.
물건을 사는 장소엔 -에서를 쓰세요. '매점에 빵 샀어요'가 아니라 '매점에서 빵 샀어요'가 맞습니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 등교 means "going to school, attending school" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 등교 (deunggyo) = "going to school, attending school". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 등교하다 ("go to school (in the morning)") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 등교, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about classroom communication, study plans, and asking for repetition or help and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 명사 + 하다 동사화
보통 아침 8시 반쯤
준비(準備) = preparation; 아침 루틴
거부(拒否) = refusal; 학교 가기를 거부하는 (심각한) 상태

examples.en: What time do you go to school?
examples.note: 시간 묻기 기본 문장; 명사 + 하다 의문형

examples.en: I usually go to school around eight.
examples.note: -쯤 = approximately (시간·수량 뒤)

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 등교 시간이 한 시간 늦춰졌어요.
examples.romanization: nuni mani waseo deunggyo sigani han sigan neutchwojyeosseoyo.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the school start time got pushed back an hour.
examples.note: 늦춰지다 = be delayed (늦추다의 피동)

extendedVocab.nuance: 등교는 한자 登校(등·교), '오를 등(登) + 학교 교(校)' = 아침에 학교로 가는 것이고, 짝이 되는 반대말은 수업이 끝나 집으로 가는 하교(下校, '내려갈 하')예요 — 登/下가 출근·퇴근의 出/退처럼 한 쌍을 이룹니다. 바로 이 점이 가장 중요한 갈림선인데, 회사에 가는 건 출근(出勤), 학교에 가는 건 등교라 대상이 다릅니다(학생판 출근이라고 생각하면 쉬워요). 한국에서는 등교 시간·등교 복장(교복) 같은 규칙이 꽤 엄격한 편이라 이 단어가 생활 속에 자주 등장합니다. 자연스러운 짝은 '등교하다, 등교 시간, 등교 준비, 등교 거부'. 영어식 함정 둘: go to school을 옮기며 '학교에 등교하다'라고 하면 등교에 이미 '학교(校)'가 들어 있어 의미가 겹치니 그냥 '등교하다'면 충분하고, 직장에 가는 것을 등교라 하면 어색하므로 그땐 출근을 쓰세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'학교에 등교하다'는 의미가 겹쳐 어색합니다. 등(登)과 교(校)에 이미 '학교에 감'이 들어 있으니 '등교하다'면 충분해요.
회사에 가는 것은 '출근'입니다. 학교에 가는 등교와 대상을 구분하세요.
집으로 돌아가는 것을 등교라 하면 틀려요. 반대 방향은 '하교(下校)'입니다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 사탕 means "candy" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 사탕 (satang) means "candy". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 사탕 하나 주세요 ("One candy, please"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 사탕 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about ordering food, explaining food restrictions, and asking what to eat together, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Count small candies with 하나/한 개; 하나 is the natural default at a counter.
까다 is the verb for peeling off a wrapper — never 열다 (open) for candy.
막대(stick) + 사탕, a fixed compound written as one word.

usagePhrases.en: to hold a candy in one's mouth
usagePhrases.note: 물다 (to hold in the mouth) fits hard candy you suck on, not chew.

examples.en: Do you like candy?
examples.note: Drop the subject in casual talk; context supplies 'you'.

examples.en: I bought a bag of candy at the convenience store.
examples.note: 봉지 is the counter for a bag/packet of snacks.

examples.ko: 목 아플 때 사탕 하나 입에 물고 있으면 좀 나아요.
examples.romanization: mok apeul ttae satang hana ibe mulgo isseumyeon jom naayo.
examples.en: When my throat hurts, keeping a candy in my mouth helps a bit.
examples.note: Throat-soothing candy is treated as a mild everyday remedy; 물고 있다 = keep held in the mouth.

extendedVocab.nuance: 사탕 means hard, sugar-based candy and lollipops — the kind you suck, not the chewy gummies (those are strictly 젤리) or 초콜릿. It is Sino-Korean, 砂糖 'sand-sugar' (the same 糖 'sugar' element in 설탕 table sugar and 당분 sugar content), which is why it sits in the sweets family rather than being a generic 'sweet treat'. Register is fully neutral: a child or an adult says it the same way. The pitfall for English speakers is the verb: you do not 열다 (open) a candy, you 까다 (peel/unwrap) it, and you 물다 or 빨다 (hold/suck) rather than 먹다 when sucking it. Seasonally it carries a faint romance: on White Day (3/14) men give 사탕 to answer the 초콜릿 women give on Valentine's Day.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling gummy candies 사탕 — soft chewy ones are 젤리, a separate category Koreans never merge with 사탕.
Saying 사탕을 열다 for 'unwrap a candy'; the correct verb is 사탕을 까다.
Using 먹다 for sucking a hard candy — when it stays in the mouth, 물다/빨다 is more accurate than 먹다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 초콜릿 means "chocolate" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "chocolate" is 초콜릿 (chokollit). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 초콜릿 한 개 ("one piece of chocolate"). Watch the particle attached to 초콜릿 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about ordering food, explaining food restrictions, and asking what to eat together first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 개 counts a single piece; a whole bar is 한 판.
녹다 (to melt) is the verb you hear in summer or in a warm hand.
Loanword modifiers 다크/밀크/화이트 sit directly before 초콜릿.
줄이다 = to reduce; standard health-talk phrasing.

examples.en: Do you like chocolate?
examples.note: Plain everyday question; subject dropped.

examples.ko: 피곤할 때 초콜릿 먹으면 기분이 좀 좋아져요.
examples.romanization: pigonhal ttae chokollin meogeumyeon gibuni jom joajyeoyo.
examples.en: When I'm tired, eating chocolate lifts my mood a bit.
examples.note: 기분이 좋아지다 = one's mood improves; -아지다 marks the gradual change.

examples.ko: 밸런타인데이에 좋아하는 사람한테 초콜릿 주려고 직접 만들었어요.
examples.romanization: baelleontaindeie joahaneun saramhante chokollit juryeogo jikjeom mandeureosseoyo.
examples.en: I made chocolate by hand to give to my crush on Valentine's Day.
examples.note: Handmade (직접 만든) 초콜릿 on Feb 14 is the big Korean custom; 주려고 = intending to give.

extendedVocab.nuance: 초콜릿 is a direct loanword from English 'chocolate', and the single most important thing to learn is the spelling: 초콜릿 is standard, while 초콜렛 is a widespread misspelling even among natives — write the former. Unlike the native-word sweets here, it takes loanword flavor modifiers (다크/밀크/화이트) placed before it. Counting trips people up: a flat bar is counted with 판 (한 판), individual squares or wrapped pieces with 개 (한 개), so 'one chocolate' is ambiguous until you pick the counter that matches the shape. Culturally it is the default Valentine's gift from women to men, mirrored by 사탕 on White Day. Pitfall: English lets 'chocolate' be a mass noun ('some chocolate'), but in Korean you still attach a counter, so 초콜릿 좀 (some) or 초콜릿 한 개 (one piece) rather than a bare count.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing 초콜렛 instead of the standard 초콜릿 — the second is correct even though both are heard.
Using 판 for a single square — a whole bar is 한 판, one piece is 한 개.
Treating it as an uncountable mass like English 'chocolate'; Korean still needs a counter, e.g. 초콜릿 한 조각/한 개.

examples.note: -(으)러 가다 = go in order to do; 갈래? is a casual invite.

extendedVocab.nuance: 과자 is Sino-Korean, 菓子 (菓 'confection/fruit' + 子 a noun suffix), and works as the umbrella term for crunchy packaged snacks — chips, crackers, biscuits, corn puffs, basically the salty-or-sweet bagged stuff in the snack aisle. Counting is by 봉지 (bag), not by piece, because these come bagged; you 뜯다 (tear) the bag open. Texture is 바삭하다 (crispy) when fresh, 눅눅하다 (soggy) when stale. Koreans love joking about 질소과자 — bags that feel mostly full of nitrogen gas rather than chips.

Using 과자 for a bakery/café cookie you'd call 쿠키 — 과자 implies packaged, mass-market snacks.
Counting bagged snacks by piece; the natural counter is 봉지 (한 봉지).
Lumping 사탕/젤리/초콜릿 under 과자 — 과자 is the crunchy salty/biscuit category, not candy.

extendedVocab.nuance: 호떡 is a chewy, griddle-fried wheat-flour pancake with a molten brown-sugar-and-cinnamon center, sold piping hot from winter street carts. The 호 in 호떡 is the 한자 胡, historically 'foreign/Chinese', marking its origin as an introduced food, attached to native 떡 — but here is the crucial distinction: although the name ends in 떡, 호떡 is NOT a rice cake. Real 떡 is made from pounded rice; 호떡 is a flour dough that is pan-fried, so do not assume the texture or ingredients of 떡. The second pitfall is taste: English speakers often expect a savory pancake, but the classic filling is sweet brown sugar (savory 야채 호떡 exists but is the exception). The verb is 굽다 (griddle), a ㅂ-irregular giving 구워요. The filling is dangerously hot, so locals genuinely warn 천천히 먹어 (eat slowly); trendy 씨앗 호떡 stuffed with seeds and nuts is a market favorite, famously around Busan's BIFF square.

Expecting 호떡 to be savory — the classic filling is sweet brown sugar and cinnamon.
Assuming 호떡 is a rice cake because of the 떡 in its name; it is a fried wheat-flour pancake, not pounded-rice 떡.

extendedVocab.nuance: 붕어빵 is a fish-shaped pastry of waffle-like batter filled with sweet red-bean paste, the iconic Korean winter street snack that pairs with 호떡 and 군고구마. The name is 붕어 (crucian carp) + 빵 (bread, itself a loanword via Portuguese pão), and the single biggest trap for English speakers is taking the fish part literally: 붕어빵 contains no fish whatsoever — it is named purely for the fish-shaped mold. Figuratively, 붕어빵 also means 'identical/spitting image' (e.g. 붕어빵처럼 똑같다) because they all come out of the same mold. Stalls have become rare enough that fans share locations via a 붕어빵 지도 app, and people fondly argue over eating head-first vs. tail-first.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Thinking 붕어빵 contains fish — it's named only for its fish shape; the classic filling is red bean.
Counting it with 마리 (the animal counter) because of the fish shape; pastries use 개.
Missing the idiom — 붕어빵 also means 'a spitting image' (붕어빵처럼 닮다), since they're all molded identically.

usagePhrases.note: A classic 분식 move; 국물 = the broth/sauce.

examples.en: I ordered sundae and fritters together at the snack shop.
examples.note: 분식집 = snack/street-food shop; 같이 시키다 = order together.

examples.ko: 순대는 소금이랑 먹을지 양념장이랑 먹을지 늘 고민돼요.
examples.romanization: sundaeneun sogeumirang meogeulji yangnyeomjangirang meogeulji neul gomindwaeyo.
examples.en: I always agonize over eating sundae with salt or with seasoned sauce.
examples.note: -(으)ㄹ지 ...-(으)ㄹ지 = whether to do A or B; regional tastes differ.

examples.ko: 속초 가면 일반 순대보다 훨씬 큰 아바이순대를 꼭 먹어 봐요.
examples.romanization: sokcho gamyeon ilban sundaeboda hwolssin keun abaisundaereul kkong meogeo bwayo.
examples.en: When I go to Sokcho I always try abai-sundae, which is much bigger than regular sundae.
examples.note: 아바이순대 is a famous Sokcho specialty; -아 보다 = try doing.

extendedVocab.nuance: 순대 is a steamed sausage made from pig intestine stuffed with 당면 (glass noodles), blood, and other fillings — a pillar of 분식 (snack-shop) culture alongside 떡볶이 and 튀김. The first thing for an English speaker to lock in is the false friend: the English dessert 'sundae' (ice cream) is completely unrelated; that is 선데이 or just 아이스크림 in Korean, while 순대 is a savory blood sausage. The nearest savory cousin is 소시지 (Western sausage), but 순대 is its own traditional category, not a type of 소시지. There is a genuine regional split — some dip it in plain 소금 (salt), others in 양념장 (seasoned sauce) — and it is sold by 인분 (portion), not by 개. The organ meats (내장) usually come on the side, and ordering without them is fine. A famous regional kind is 아바이순대 from Sokcho.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 순대 with an ice-cream sundae — the English word is a false friend; this is a savory blood sausage (the dessert is 선데이/아이스크림).
Ordering by 개 — 순대 is sold by 인분 (portion).
Calling 순대 a kind of 소시지 — it overlaps in shape but is its own traditional food, not Western sausage.

extendedVocab.explanation: 어묵 (eomuk) means "fish cake". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 어묵 한 꼬치 ("one skewer of fish cake"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 어묵 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about ordering food, explaining food restrictions, and asking what to eat together, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 꼬치 = skewer; the street form is folded onto a stick.
The hot 국물 (broth) is free and beloved in winter.
오뎅 is the very common colloquial (Japanese-origin) term.
셀프 = self-service; refill your own paper cup for free.

examples.ko: 어묵 꼬치 다섯 개 먹고 국물도 두 컵 마셨어요.
examples.romanization: eomuk kkochi daseot gae meokgo gungmuldo du keom masyeosseoyo.
examples.en: I ate five fish-cake skewers and drank two cups of broth too.
examples.note: Count 꼬치 (skewers) and 컵 (cups); 도 = also.

examples.ko: 추운 날 포장마차에서 어묵 국물 마시면 몸이 녹아요.
examples.romanization: chuun nal pojangmachaeseo eomuk gungmul masimyeon momi nogayo.
examples.en: Drinking fish-cake broth at a street tent on a cold day warms you right up.
examples.note: 포장마차 = street food tent; 몸이 녹다 = to thaw/warm up.

examples.ko: 부산 어묵이 워낙 유명해서 갈 때마다 선물로 사 와요.
examples.romanization: busan eomugi wonak yumyeonghaeseo gal ttaemada seonmullo sa wayo.
examples.en: Busan fish cake is so famous that I buy some as a gift every time I go.
examples.note: 워낙 = (so) by nature/famously; -ㄹ 때마다 = every time.

extendedVocab.nuance: 어묵 is the standard word for fish cake — ground fish paste shaped and cooked — and the register issue is the heart of this entry. In everyday speech most people, including at stalls, casually say 오뎅 (from Japanese おでん); 어묵 is the 'proper', recommended-Korean term you should default to in writing and polite contexts, while recognizing 오뎅 when you hear it. The 한자 is 魚 'fish' (어) + native 묵 (a set jelly/curd, as in 도토리묵 acorn jelly), so the word literally frames it as a 'fish curd'. The street form is folded onto a skewer (꼬치) and comes with an endlessly refilled, free hot 국물 in winter — and that broth is 셀프 (self-serve), so you do not pay per cup, a frequent point of confusion for visitors. Busan (부산어묵) is the celebrated home of it, and packaged 어묵 is both a soup ingredient and a common gift.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Assuming 오뎅 is simply wrong — it is extremely common in speech, just non-standard; 어묵 is the recommended term.
Forgetting the 국물 is self-serve and free; you refill your own cup rather than paying per serving.
Treating 어묵 and 묵 as the same thing — 묵 (e.g. 도토리묵) is a different set-jelly food; 어묵 is the fish version.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 튀김 means "deep-fried snacks, fritters (tempura-style)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "deep-fried snacks, fritters (tempura-style)" is 튀김 (twigim). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 튀김 모둠 주세요 ("An assorted fritter plate, please"). Watch the particle attached to 튀김 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about ordering food, explaining food restrictions, and asking what to eat together first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 모둠 = an assortment of mixed pieces.
Ingredient + 튀김 names each fritter; 오징어/새우/고구마.
바삭하다 = crispy, the key quality marker; opposite 눅눅하다.

usagePhrases.en: to dip the fritters in tteokbokki sauce
usagePhrases.note: The quintessential 분식 way to eat them.

examples.ko: 분식집에서 튀김이랑 순대 시켜서 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.romanization: bunsikjibeseo twigimirang sundae sikyeoseo nanwo meogeosseoyo.
examples.en: We ordered fritters and sundae at the snack shop and shared.
examples.note: 나눠 먹다 = to share food; -아서 chains the actions.

examples.ko: 갓 튀긴 튀김이 제일 바삭하고 맛있어요.
examples.romanization: gat twigin twigimi jeil basakago masisseoyo.
examples.en: Freshly fried fritters are the crispiest and tastiest.
examples.note: 갓 튀긴 = just-fried; note 튀긴 (verb) modifying 튀김 (noun).

examples.ko: 김말이 튀김은 겉은 바삭한데 안에 당면이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.romanization: gimmari twigimeun geoteun basakande ane dangmyeoni gadeuk deureo isseoyo.
examples.en: Gimmari fritters are crispy outside but packed with glass noodles inside.
examples.note: 김말이 = seaweed-rolled fritter; -는데 contrasts outside vs inside.

extendedVocab.nuance: 튀김 is a native noun built from the verb 튀기다 (to deep-fry) plus the nominalizing -ㅁ, literally 'a frying / a fried thing', and it means battered deep-fried snacks in the Korean tempura tradition — fried squid, shrimp, sweet potato, and 김말이 (seaweed-and-noodle rolls) — sold at 분식 stalls beside 떡볶이 and 순대. Because it comes from a verb, the number-one pitfall is mixing up 튀김 (the noun: the fried food) with 튀기다/튀긴 (the verb: to fry / fried), as in 갓 튀긴 튀김 'just-fried fritters', where both appear. A second trap is scope: a bare 튀김 usually implies a mixed assortment (모둠), so to order one specific kind you must name the ingredient — 오징어 튀김, 새우 튀김 — rather than just 튀김. The whole point is 바삭함 (crispiness), best 갓 튀긴 (just fried) and ruined when 눅눅하다 (soggy); dunking them in spicy 떡볶이 국물 is the classic move.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using the verb 튀기다 (to fry) when you mean the noun 튀김 (the fried food) — they share a root but aren't interchangeable.
Expecting one item from a bare 튀김 — it usually means an assortment; specify the ingredient (오징어 튀김 etc.) to order one kind.
Describing stale fritters with the wrong adjective — lost crunch is 눅눅하다, the opposite of 바삭하다.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 약과 means "yakgwa (honey fried cookie)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 약과 (yakgwa) = "yakgwa (honey fried cookie)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 약과 하나 먹을래요? ("Want to have a yakgwa?") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 약과, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about ordering food, explaining food restrictions, and asking what to eat together and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Counted by 개; traditionally offered with tea.
Bite-size 미니 약과 became a huge trend snack.
It is honey-soaked; 달다 (sweet) is a ㄹ-final adjective (달아요).
Packaged mini versions sell by the 봉지.

examples.en: Yakgwa is chewy outside and soft inside.
examples.note: 쫀득하다 = pleasantly chewy; -고 links two qualities.

examples.ko: 약과는 명절에 차례상에 꼭 올라가는 한과예요.
examples.romanization: yakgwaneun myeongjeore charyesange kkok ollaganeun hangwayeyo.
examples.en: Yakgwa is a traditional sweet that always goes on the holiday ritual table.
examples.note: 한과 = traditional confection; 차례상 = ancestral-rite table; 올라가다 = to be placed on.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들 사이에서 약과가 다시 유행이라 카페에서도 약과 디저트를 팔아요.
examples.romanization: yojeum jeolmeun saramdeul saieseo yakgwaga dasi yuhaengira kapeeseodo yakgwa dijeoteureul parayo.
examples.en: Yakgwa is trendy again among young people, so cafés even sell yakgwa desserts now.
examples.note: Part of the 할매니얼 (grandma + millennial) retro-snack craze; -이라 = because it is.

extendedVocab.nuance: 약과 is a traditional Korean confection (한과): a wheat-flour dough that is deep-fried and then steeped in honey or grain syrup, historically reserved for holidays and ritual tables. Its 한자 is the key insight — 藥菓, literally 'medicine-confection', because in old Korea honey was considered medicinal (藥 'medicine' is the same character as in 약 'medicine' and 한약 herbal medicine; 菓 'confection' is the same as in 과자). So the standout English-speaker pitfall is assuming the name means it contains medicine: it does not — it is simply a honey cookie whose historical luxury ingredient earned the 'medicine' label. The other boundary to keep straight is 약과 (a specific 한과) vs the broad 과자 (mass-market packaged snacks): 약과 is not a 과자, even though both share the 菓 character. Texture is 쫀득하다 (chewy-sticky) and it is quite sweet (달다). It has surged back into fashion among people in their 20s-30s as part of the 할매니얼 retro-snack trend, with cafés selling 미니 약과 and yakgwa-topped desserts.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Assuming 약과 contains medicine because of 약(藥) — the name reflects honey's old status as a remedy; it is just a honey cookie.
Grouping it with Western-style 과자 — 약과 is specifically a 한과 (traditional confection), a different category despite sharing the 菓 character.
Conjugating 달다 as 달어요 — it is a ㄹ-final adjective, so 'it's sweet' is 달아요.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 축구 means "soccer, football" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 축구 (chukgu) means "soccer, football". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 축구 좋아해요? ("Do you like soccer?"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 축구 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: By far the most common sport to open small talk with Korean coworkers and friends.

usagePhrases.en: Let's play a round of soccer
usagePhrases.note: 판 is the casual counter for a round/match; 한 판 하다 = 'play a round', breezier than 경기.

usagePhrases.en: Want to go watch a soccer game?
usagePhrases.note: 보러 가다 = 'go in order to watch'; the 러 attaches to the verb stem of the purpose.
조기(早起, 'rising early') 축구 is a fixed term for the weekend dawn matches older men famously play.

examples.en: I play soccer with my friends every weekend.
examples.note: 마다 = 'every'; in speech 축구(를) 하다 drops the 를, and 이랑 is the casual 'with'.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 손흥민 나오는 축구 경기 봤어요?
examples.romanization: eojetbame sonheungmin naoneun chukgu gyeonggi bwasseoyo?
examples.en: Did you watch the soccer match Son Heung-min was in last night?
examples.note: 나오다 = 'appear/be featured'; EPL games with 손흥민 are huge water-cooler talk.

examples.ko: 한국이 일본을 이겨서 축구 팬들이 다 난리 났어요.
examples.romanization: hangugi ilboneul igyeoseo chukgu paendeuri da nalli nasseoyo.
examples.en: Korea beat Japan, so all the soccer fans went wild.
examples.note: 난리 나다 = 'go into an uproar'; -아서 here marks the cause leading to the reaction.

extendedVocab.nuance: 축구 (蹴球, literally 'kick(蹴)-ball(球)') is the default national sport for casual conversation, and dropping a name like 손흥민 buys instant rapport, especially in men's chat. The verb splits by activity: 축구(를) 하다 for playing versus 축구(를) 보다 for watching — never one verb for both, and in speech the 를 is usually dropped. The big English-speaker pitfall is the word itself: do NOT say 풋볼, which Koreans hear as American football, nor 사커; the only natural word is 축구. A second trap is calling a real match 축구 게임 — for a broadcast or pro fixture it is 축구 경기, while 게임 sounds like a casual pickup kickabout. Recognize the cultural compound 조기 축구, the dawn amateur soccer older men play on weekends.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 풋볼 or 사커 — Koreans always say 축구, and 풋볼 specifically sounds like American football to them.
Using 게임 for a real match: a pro or broadcast match is 축구 경기, not 축구 게임 (게임 implies casual pickup).
Saying 축구를 보다 and 축구를 하다 interchangeably — you watch (보다) a match but play (하다) the sport; the verbs are not swappable.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 야구 means "baseball" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "baseball" is 야구 (yagu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 야구 좋아해요? ("Do you like baseball?"). Watch the particle attached to 야구 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Korea's most-attended pro sport (KBO); a safe, friendly small-talk opener.

usagePhrases.en: Which team do you root for?
usagePhrases.note: 응원하다 = 'cheer for'; asking someone's KBO team is a classic bonding move.

usagePhrases.en: Let's go to a baseball game
usagePhrases.note: 보러 가다 again; KBO stadiums are famous for loud, organized fan chants.
시즌 is the everyday loanword; the KBO season runs spring through fall.

examples.ko: 주말에 잠실 가서 야구 볼 거예요.
examples.romanization: jumare jamsil gaseo yagu bol geoyeyo.
examples.en: I'm going to Jamsil this weekend to watch baseball.
examples.note: Locals name the venue: 잠실 가다 rather than 야구장 가다; -ㄹ 거예요 = future plan.

examples.en: When you go to a baseball stadium, chicken and beer are a must.
examples.note: 치킨에 맥주 = 'chicken plus beer' (the 에 means 'added to'); 필수 = 'a must'.

examples.en: Our team came from behind in the 9th, it was such a thrill.
examples.note: 역전(逆轉)하다 = 'reverse the lead'; 9회 = the 9th inning, 에 marks the time point.

extendedVocab.nuance: 야구 (野球, literally 'field(野)-ball(球)') is arguably the sport Koreans are most passionate about attending in person — the stadium chants, team songs, and bringing your own 치맥 (치킨+맥주) form a whole culture. The verb pattern mirrors 축구: 야구(를) 하다 for playing, 야구(를) 보다 for watching. Asking 어느 팀 응원해요? signals you want to connect socially. Two pitfalls for English speakers: first, for a pro game Koreans usually name the stadium (잠실 가다, 고척 가다) — saying 야구장 가다 sounds like a generic or amateur field. Second, 회 here is the inning counter (1회, 9회), a homophone of 회 'raw fish'; the number and context disambiguate, so 9회 unambiguously means the ninth inning, never sashimi.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
For a pro game, saying 야구장 가다 instead of naming the venue (잠실 가다) — 야구장 sounds like a generic/amateur field.
Using 게임 for a KBO match — say 야구 경기; 게임 implies a casual or backyard game.
Reading 9회 as anything but the inning — 회 (inning) here is a counter, not 회 'raw fish'; the number marks it as the 9th inning.

structuredNuance.t: Arguably the sport Koreans are most passionate about attending in person — the stadium chants, team songs, and bringing your own 치맥 (치킨+맥주) form a whole culture. Asking 어느 팀 응원해요? signals you want to connect socially.
野球, literally 'field(野)-ball(球)'.
The verb pattern mirrors 축구: 야구(를) 하다 for playing, 야구(를) 보다 for watching.

First, for a pro game Koreans usually name the stadium (잠실 가다, 고척 가다) — saying 야구장 가다 sounds like a generic or amateur field. Second, 회 here is the inning counter (1회, 9회), a homophone of 회 'raw fish'; the number and context disambiguate, so 9회 unambiguously means the ninth inning, never sashimi.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 농구 means "basketball" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 농구 (nonggu) = "basketball". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 농구 할 줄 알아요? ("Do you know how to play basketball?") shows how it actually behaves. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.en: Do you know how to play basketball?
usagePhrases.note: 할 줄 알다 = 'know how to do'; the natural way to propose a pickup game.

usagePhrases.en: Let's play a game of basketball
usagePhrases.note: 게임 works for pickup hoops; 한 게임 = 'one game', unlike pro soccer where you'd want 경기.
골대 = the hoop/goal post; you'll see them at parks and schoolyards.
Many younger Koreans follow the NBA; the acronym is spelled out in English letters.

examples.en: After work I go play basketball with coworkers.
examples.note: 하러 가다 = 'go in order to play'; 퇴근하고 = 'after clocking out'.

examples.ko: 키 크면 농구 잘할 것 같다는 말 많이 들어요.
examples.romanization: ki keumyeon nonggu jalhal geot gatdaneun mal mani deureoyo.
examples.en: People often tell me I'd be good at basketball since I'm tall.
examples.note: 잘하다 = 'be good at'; -다는 말 듣다 = 'hear people say that...'.

examples.en: I played a game with strangers at the neighborhood court.
examples.note: 농구장 = 'basketball court'; pickup games (픽업 게임) with strangers are common.

extendedVocab.nuance: 농구 (籠球, literally 'basket(籠)-ball(球)') had a huge cultural moment in the 90s through the drama '마지막 승부' and the 'Slam Dunk' generation, and pickup games at neighborhood 농구장 remain popular among younger men. The verb is 농구(를) 하다 for playing, 농구(를) 보다 for watching. A useful register note for English speakers: unlike pro soccer, with basketball you can freely say 농구 게임 for a casual pickup game (한 게임 하자), though 농구 경기 is still the word for a formal or broadcast match — so 게임 here is not a mistake the way it would be for a pro 축구 fixture. The two pitfalls are the loanword 바스켓볼 (never used; only 농구) and calling the hoop 농구 문 ('basketball door') instead of the correct 골대.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 바스켓볼 — Koreans only say 농구.
Saying 농구 문 ('basketball door') for the hoop; the correct word is 골대 (or 농구 골대).
Forcing 경기 onto every casual game — for pickup hoops, 농구 한 게임 하자 is perfectly natural, unlike with pro soccer.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 배구 means "volleyball" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 배구 (baegu) means "volleyball". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 배구 좋아해요? ("Do you like volleyball?"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 배구 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Women's pro volleyball (V-리그) has a strong, growing fanbase in Korea.

usagePhrases.en: Did you watch the volleyball match?
usagePhrases.note: 경기 is the standard word for a formal match in any sport.
국가대표(國家代表) = 'national team', often heard around 김연경 and the Olympics.
배구 was a staple P.E. and 체육대회 (sports day) game for many Koreans.

examples.ko: 김연경 선수 덕분에 배구 팬이 많아졌어요.
examples.romanization: gimyeongyeong seonsu deokbune baegu paeni manajyeosseoyo.
examples.en: Thanks to Kim Yeon-koung, volleyball gained a lot of fans.
examples.note: 덕분에 = 'thanks to' (positive cause only); 선수 = 'athlete', a respectful tag after a name.

examples.ko: 우리 회사 체육대회 때 배구 시합 했어요.
examples.romanization: uri hoesa cheyukdaehoe ttae baegu siha paesseoyo.
examples.en: We had a volleyball match at our company sports day.
examples.note: 시합 = match/contest, interchangeable with 경기 in casual use; 때 = 'at the time of'.

examples.ko: 배구는 키가 큰 선수들이 유리한 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: baeguneun kiga keun seonsudeuri yurihan geot gatayo.
examples.en: It seems taller players have an advantage in volleyball.
examples.note: 유리하다 = 'be advantageous'; -ㄴ 것 같다 softens it to 'it seems'.

extendedVocab.nuance: 배구 (排球, literally 'push/arrange(排)-ball(球)', capturing how the ball is set and pushed over the net) surged in popularity through women's pro volleyball and especially 김연경 (Kim Yeon-koung), making it a warmer small-talk topic than before. It is also a nostalgic schoolyard and company sports-day (체육대회) game. For a match you can use 경기 or the slightly more casual, contest-flavored 시합 (試合) — the dividing line is that 시합 emphasizes the head-to-head contest while 경기 is the neutral all-purpose term. The pitfall for English speakers is the loanword 발리볼, which sounds foreign and is never used; say 배구. Also note 배구 is a clear two-syllable word, so it never gets confused in practice with the bare 배 (boat/stomach/pear).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 발리볼 — the Korean word is 배구.
Assuming 시합 and 경기 are different things — they overlap heavily; 시합 just leans toward 'contest/bout' while 경기 is neutral.
Dropping a syllable to 배 — the sport is always the full 배구; 배 alone means boat/stomach/pear.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 탁구 means "table tennis, ping-pong" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: "table tennis, ping-pong" is 탁구 (takgu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 탁구 칠 줄 알아요? ("Can you play table tennis?"). Watch the particle attached to 탁구 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: Note the verb: 탁구는 치다 ('hit'), not 하다 — like other paddle/racket sports.

usagePhrases.en: Shall we play a round of ping-pong?
usagePhrases.note: 치다 + 판; -ㄹ까요 makes it a soft 'shall we?' suggestion at a community center.
Dedicated 탁구장 are common in neighborhoods and apartment complexes.
The paddle is 라켓; the table itself is 탁구대.

examples.en: During lunch we play ping-pong in the office lounge.
examples.note: 휴게실 = 'break room'; note 탁구 쳐요 (from 치다), and 에서 marks the location of the action.

examples.ko: 탁구는 운동도 되고 재미도 있어서 좋아요.
examples.romanization: takguneun undongdo doego jaemido isseoseo joayo.
examples.en: Table tennis is good because it's both exercise and fun.
examples.note: 운동이 되다 = 'count as exercise'; -도...-도 = 'both...and'.

examples.ko: 아파트 주민센터에 탁구대가 있어서 자주 쳐요.
examples.romanization: apateu juminsenteoe takgudaega isseoseo jaju chyeoyo.
examples.en: There's a table tennis table at the apartment center, so I play often.
examples.note: 있어서 = 'there is, so'; the object 탁구 is dropped before 쳐요 because it's understood.

extendedVocab.nuance: 탁구 (卓球, literally 'table(卓)-ball(球)') is crucial for one reason English speakers stumble on: it takes the verb 치다 ('to hit/strike'), NOT 하다 — you say 탁구를 치다. This 치다 is the same verb used for hitting a ball with an implement (tennis, golf, drums), the dividing line from 하다, which is for sports you do with your whole body or feet (축구를 하다). It is an accessible, low-cost way to socialize, found in 탁구장, apartment community rooms, and office break rooms. Vocabulary to keep straight: the table is 탁구대 and the paddle is 라켓. A register pitfall: calling it 핑퐁 in conversation sounds childish or cutesy; adults say 탁구.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 탁구 하다 instead of the natural 탁구 치다 — paddle sports take 치다.
Calling it 핑퐁 in adult conversation — that sounds childish; say 탁구.
Mixing up 탁구대 (the table) and 라켓 (the paddle) — they are different pieces of equipment.

extendedVocab.shortExplanation: 테니스 means "tennis" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
extendedVocab.explanation: 테니스 (teniseu) = "tennis". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 테니스 쳐요? ("Do you play tennis?") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 테니스, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Like table tennis, tennis takes 치다 (to hit), not 하다.
-고 있다 = ongoing; 테니스 has boomed as a trendy lesson-based hobby for 20-30s.
예약하다 = 'reserve'; public 테니스장 fill up fast and are booked by app.
레슨 is the standard word; beginners often start with a 강습/레슨 package.

examples.ko: 요즘 테니스 배우는 사람 진짜 많아졌어요.
examples.romanization: yojeum teniseu baeuneun saram jinjja manajyeosseoyo.
examples.en: These days way more people are learning tennis.
examples.note: 많아지다 = 'become many/increase'; 요즘 sets the recent-trend frame.

examples.ko: 주말에 테니스장 잡기가 하늘의 별 따기예요.
examples.romanization: jumare teniseujang japgiga haneurui byeol ttagiyeyo.
examples.en: Booking a court on weekends is like picking a star from the sky.
examples.note: 하늘의 별 따기 = idiom for 'nearly impossible'; 잡다 here = 'secure/book'.

examples.ko: 테니스 치고 나면 온몸이 다 쑤셔요.
examples.romanization: teniseu chigo namyeon onmomi da ssusyeoyo.
examples.en: After playing tennis my whole body aches.
examples.note: -고 나면 = 'after (completing)'; 온몸이 쑤시다 = 'whole body aches'.

extendedVocab.nuance: 테니스 is a loanword (no hanja), and the key thing English speakers get wrong is the verb: it is 치다 ('to hit'), exactly like 탁구 and 골프, because you strike a ball with a racket — never 테니스를 하다. In recent years it has become a fashionable lifestyle hobby for Koreans in their 20s-30s, complete with 테니스 룩 (tennis outfits) for social media, so the word now signals a trendy, active social circle. Court booking (테니스장 예약) is genuinely competitive on weekends. One vocabulary contrast worth knowing: the older term 정구 refers specifically to soft tennis and sounds dated, so for the modern racket sport always say 테니스.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 하다 instead of 치다 — racket sports take 치다, so it is 테니스를 치다.
Saying 정구 for modern tennis — 정구 is the older soft-tennis term and sounds dated; say 테니스.
Translating 'book a court' word-for-word — Koreans say 테니스장 예약하다, with 예약 ('reservation'), not a literal rendering of 'book'.
