endingItems.whenToUse: This runs through all of Korean. Whenever an ending is written with (으) — like (으)면, (으)세요, (으)ㄹ 수 있다, (으)러, (으)니까 — you choose the form by the stem's last sound: 먹으면 vs 가면, 먹을 수 있다 vs 갈 수 있다.
endingItems.attachmentRule: Drop 다 to get the stem. If the stem ends in a VOWEL (no 받침), use the short form: -면, -세요, -ㄹ, -러, -니까, -ㄴ (가면, 가세요, 갈, 가러, 가니까). If the stem ends in a CONSONANT (받침 있음), insert 으: -으면, -으세요, -을, -으러, -으니까, -은 (먹으면, 먹으세요, 먹을, 먹으러, 먹으니까). ㄹ-final stems are special: the ㄹ stays for most endings (살면, 살아요) but DROPS before ㄴ/ㅂ/(으)-endings (살다 → 사세요, 사니까, 산).
endingItems.contrastWith: It is the SAME choice across many endings, so learn it once instead of memorizing each ending: 갈 거예요 / 먹을 거예요, 가면 / 먹으면, 가세요 / 먹으세요, 가니까 / 먹으니까.
sentenceFrames: (vowel) 가 + 면 → 가면   ·   (consonant) 먹 + 으면 → 먹으면
갈 수 있어요  ·  먹을 수 있어요

examples.en: Can I eat this?
If you go over there, it's there.
Please read slowly.
Let's go eat (in order to eat).

commonMistakes: Adding 으 after a vowel stem — 가으면 is wrong; it is 가면.
Forgetting 으 after a consonant stem — 먹면/먹세요 are wrong; it is 먹으면/먹으세요.
studyOrder: Find the stem (drop 다)
Check for a final consonant (받침)
Consonant → add 으 (먹으면); vowel → skip it (가면)
Watch ㄹ-stems: 살다 → 사세요
endingItems.beginnerExplanation: This is maybe THE most useful rule in Korean. Many endings are written with (으) in front — like (으)면 'if', (으)세요 'please', (으)ㄹ 수 있다 'can'. The 으 is just a little buffer vowel. If the verb stem ends in a consonant (먹-), add 으: 먹으면, 먹으세요, 먹을 수 있어요. If it ends in a vowel (가-), skip it: 가면, 가세요, 갈 수 있어요. Learn it once and it unlocks dozens of endings at the same time.

endingItems.title: Liaison — Linking Sounds (연음)
endingItems.plainEnglish: When a syllable ends in a consonant and the next starts with ㅇ (a vowel), that consonant slides over to begin the next syllable.
endingItems.whenToUse: This happens constantly in speech: 한국어 sounds like 한구거, 음악이 like 으마기, 꽃이 like 꼬치. The spelling never changes — only the sound links.
endingItems.attachmentRule: A final consonant (받침) before an ㅇ-initial syllable moves to become that syllable's onset: 꽃 + 이 → [꼬치], 음악 + 을 → [으마글], 옷 + 이 → [오시], 한국 + 어 → [한구거]. A double 받침 splits — one stays, one moves: 읽 + 어 → [일거], 앉 + 아 → [안자]. Liaison does not cross a clear pause between words.
endingItems.contrastWith: You still WRITE 꽃이, 음악을, 한국어 — only the pronunciation links. This is the #1 reason Korean sounds different from how it looks on the page.

examples.en: I study Korean. (sounds like 한구거)
The flowers are really pretty. (sounds like 꼬치)
I listen to music. (sounds like 으마글)
The clothes are too small. (sounds like 오시)

commonMistakes: Pronouncing each block separately (꼳-이 instead of 꼬치).
Forgetting a double 받침 splits: 읽어요 is [일거요], not [익어요].
studyOrder: Spot a 받침 followed by ㅇ
Slide the 받침 into the next syllable
For double 받침, keep one and move one
endingItems.beginnerExplanation: Korean is written in neat syllable blocks, but in speech a final consonant 'jumps' onto the next block when that block starts with a vowel (the silent ㅇ). So 한국어 is read 한구거, and 꽃이 is read 꼬치. You keep spelling it the normal way — only the sound links up. Once you expect this, listening gets much easier.

endingItems.title: Nasalization (비음화)
endingItems.plainEnglish: A stop consonant (ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ) turns into a nasal (ㅇ/ㄴ/ㅁ) when the next syllable starts with ㄴ or ㅁ.
endingItems.whenToUse: Why 감사합니다 sounds like 감사함니다 and 학년 like 항년. It happens whenever a stop 받침 bumps into ㄴ or ㅁ.
endingItems.attachmentRule: Before ㄴ or ㅁ: a ㄱ-type 받침 (ㄱㄲㅋㄳㄺ) → ㅇ (학년 → [항년], 국물 → [궁물]); a ㄷ-type 받침 (ㄷㅅㅆㅈㅊㅌㅎ) → ㄴ (받는 → [반는], 옛날 → [옌날]); a ㅂ-type 받침 (ㅂㅍㄼㄿ) → ㅁ (입니다 → [임니다], 앞문 → [암문]).
endingItems.contrastWith: Spelling stays the same (입니다, 학년). This is different from liaison: nasalization happens before ㄴ/ㅁ, while liaison happens before a vowel (ㅇ).

examples.en: Thank you. (sounds like 감사함니다)
I'm in third grade. (학년 sounds like 항년)
The broth is hot. (국물 sounds like 궁물)
This is Korean food. (입니다 sounds like 임니다)

commonMistakes: Pronouncing the hard 합니다 as written instead of [함니다].
Missing it in -습니다/-ㅂ니다 endings, which always nasalize to [-슴니다]/[-ㅁ니다].
studyOrder: Find a ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ 받침 before ㄴ or ㅁ
ㄱ→ㅇ, ㄷ→ㄴ, ㅂ→ㅁ
Apply it to every -ㅂ니다 ending
endingItems.beginnerExplanation: Some 받침 sounds soften when they run into ㄴ or ㅁ. A ㄱ-sound becomes ㅇ (학년 → 항년), a ㄷ-sound becomes ㄴ (받는 → 반는), and a ㅂ-sound becomes ㅁ (입니다 → 임니다). That's why the polite -습니다 ending is pronounced -슴니다. You don't change the spelling — just the sound.

endingItems.title: Palatalization (구개음화)
endingItems.plainEnglish: A final ㄷ or ㅌ turns into ㅈ or ㅊ when the next sound is 이 (or 히).
endingItems.whenToUse: Why 같이 is pronounced 가치 and 굳이 is 구지. It only happens with ㄷ/ㅌ + 이.
endingItems.attachmentRule: When a 받침 ㄷ/ㅌ meets the vowel 이: ㄷ + 이 → 지 (굳이 → [구지], 해돋이 → [해도지], 맏이 → [마지]); ㅌ + 이 → 치 (같이 → [가치], 끝이 → [끄치], 붙이다 → [부치다]). With 히 it also applies: 닫히다 → [다치다].
endingItems.contrastWith: This is a special case of liaison: normally ㅌ + 이 would just link to [티], but before 이 the sound shifts forward in the mouth to [치]. Only ㄷ/ㅌ do this, and only before 이/히.

examples.en: Shall we go together? (같이 sounds like 가치)
You don't have to come (no need). (굳이 sounds like 구지)
I can't see the end. (끝이 sounds like 끄치)
I stick on a sticker. (붙여 area, 붙이- → 부치-)

commonMistakes: Reading 같이 as [가티] — before 이 it becomes [가치].
Over-applying it: it only affects ㄷ/ㅌ before 이/히, not other consonants or vowels.
studyOrder: Spot a ㄷ or ㅌ 받침 right before 이/히
ㄷ → 지, ㅌ → 치
Remember the common word 같이 → 가치
endingItems.beginnerExplanation: When ㄷ or ㅌ at the end of a syllable meets 이, the sound slides forward and becomes ㅈ or ㅊ. So 같이 ('together') is said 가치, and 굳이 is 구지. It's a small rule, but 같이 is such a common word that getting it right (가치, not 가티) makes you sound much more natural.

endingItems.title: Aspiration (격음화)
endingItems.plainEnglish: ㅎ merges with a neighboring ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ/ㅈ to make the strong, breathy ㅋ/ㅌ/ㅍ/ㅊ.
endingItems.whenToUse: Why 좋다 sounds like 조타 and 축하해요 like 추카해요. It works in either order (ㅎ before or after the stop).
endingItems.attachmentRule: ㅎ + ㄱ (or ㄱ + ㅎ) → ㅋ: 축하 → [추카], 그렇게 → [그러케]. ㅎ + ㄷ → ㅌ: 좋다 → [조타], 많다 → [만타]. ㅎ + ㅂ → ㅍ: 입학 → [이팍], 잡히다 → [자피다]. ㅎ + ㅈ → ㅊ: 좋지 → [조치], 맞히다 → [마치다]. ㅅ-type 받침 + 해 also works: 못해 → [모태].
endingItems.contrastWith: The two plain sounds fuse into ONE aspirated sound — you don't hear ㅎ separately. Compare plain 다 vs aspirated 타 in 좋다 → [조타].

examples.en: The weather is really nice. (좋다 sounds like 조타)
Happy birthday! (축하 sounds like 추카)
I can't do that. (못해 sounds like 모태)
I entered university. (입학 sounds like 이팍)

commonMistakes: Trying to pronounce ㅎ as a separate sound — 좋다 is one fused [조타], not [조ㅎ다].
Missing it in 못해/안 해도 — 못해 is [모태].
studyOrder: Find a ㅎ next to ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ/ㅈ (either order)
Fuse them into ㅋ/ㅌ/ㅍ/ㅊ
Practice 좋다 → 조타 and 축하 → 추카
endingItems.beginnerExplanation: The letter ㅎ is 'breathy', and when it touches ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, or ㅈ, the two fuse into one strong aspirated sound: ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ, ㅊ. So 좋다 is said 조타, 축하 is 추카, and 못해 is 모태. You won't hear the ㅎ on its own — it gets absorbed into the harder sound.

items.prompt: Choose the Hangul word for “Hangul / Korean writing.”

items.hint: Break the syllable block into letters.

items.prompt: 먹어요 has three written chunks: 먹 + ____ + 요.

items.hint: As for me, I am Hana.

items.prompt: Choose “I am busy, so I cannot go.”
Build: “If you have time, please call.”
Choose “It looks like it’s going to rain.”

tracks.title: Arrival & Connectivity
tracks.summary: Your first hours in Korea: clear the airport and immigration, plan your ARC, grab a SIM, and load a T-money card — with the survival Korean to do each one.

units.title: Clear immigration and plan your ARC
units.situation: At the airport arrivals hall, at the immigration desk and the help counter right after you land.
units.goal: I can answer basic immigration questions, ask for help in line, and know I must apply for my ARC within 90 days.

keyPhrases.note: Polite all-purpose greeting; say it as you step up to the immigration desk.
Simple reason for visit. For study or work, swap in 공부하러 왔어요 / 일하러 왔어요.
Uses the 'can' pattern. A polite way to check before continuing in English.
Your single most useful survival line when someone speaks too fast.

keyPhrases.en: I'm not sure / I don't understand.
keyPhrases.note: Say this instead of guessing; the officer will usually rephrase.

keyPhrases.en: Where do I apply for the Alien Registration Card?
keyPhrases.note: 외국인등록증 (ARC) is your key ID in Korea; you apply at an immigration office.
어디예요? = 'where is it?'. Swap 화장실 for any place you need.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.en: What is the purpose of your visit?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: I'm here to study. Please speak slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.en: Okay, got it. How long will you stay?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: One year. Where do I apply for the ARC?

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.en: You apply at the immigration office.

beginnerGuide.title: What the ARC is and the 90-day rule
beginnerGuide.body: The 외국인등록증 (Alien Registration Card, ARC) is the ID that lets you open a bank account, get a long-term phone plan, and more. If you're staying over 90 days, you must apply at an immigration office, generally within 90 days of arrival. Book your visit on HiKorea before you go — walk-in slots are scarce.

beginnerGuide.title: 해요체: the polite ending you'll hear most
beginnerGuide.body: Most phrases here end in -요 (왔어요, 신청해요, 모르겠어요). This 해요체 is polite but friendly — the right default with officials and strangers. You don't need the stiffer -습니다 form to be respectful.

beginnerGuide.title: Asking 'where' with 어디
beginnerGuide.body: 어디 means 'where'. 어디예요? asks 'where is it?' (화장실이 어디예요?), while 어디에서 marks where an action happens (어디에서 신청해요? = 'where do I apply?'). Hear the difference: 어디예요 = location of a thing, 어디에서 = location of an action.

checkpoints: I can greet the officer and state my reason for visiting (여행/공부하러/일하러 왔어요).
I can ask someone to slow down (천천히 말해 주세요) and say when I don't understand (잘 모르겠어요).
I can ask where to apply for my ARC (외국인등록증은 어디에서 신청해요?).
I know I must apply for the ARC at an immigration office within 90 days for a long stay.

drills.note: Swap 화장실 for 출구 (exit) or 택시 (taxi) to ask for other places.
Practice the V + ㄹ/을 수 있어요 'can' shape; try 도와줄 수 있어요? (can you help?).

steps: Have your passport, arrival card, and accommodation address ready at the immigration desk.
After immigration, collect baggage and pass through customs (declare items if asked).
If staying over 90 days, book an ARC appointment on HiKorea and gather documents (passport photo, application form, fee).

deepLinks.label: HiKorea (immigration & ARC)
deepLinks.note: Official portal to book immigration office visits and check ARC requirements.

units.costs: ARC application fee is typically around 30,000 KRW (pay at the immigration office); have a passport photo ready.
units.notes: Bring the exact documents listed on your visa type's HiKorea page; missing a photo or the fee is the most common reason for a wasted trip.

units.title: Buy a SIM or eSIM
units.situation: At an airport telecom booth or a neighborhood phone shop, choosing between prepaid and a plan.
units.goal: I can ask for a SIM, choose prepaid vs. a plan, ask the price, and confirm it will work in my phone.

keyPhrases.en: I'd like to buy a SIM.
keyPhrases.note: Uses the 'want' pattern V고 싶어요. 유심 = USIM, the standard word for a SIM card here.
N 주세요 = 'please give me N'. Add 데이터 for a data-focused SIM.
The essential price question. Works for anything you can point at.
Useful when comparing a monthly plan; 한 달 = one month.

keyPhrases.en: Do you have a prepaid SIM?
keyPhrases.note: 선불 = prepaid, 후불 = pay-later/plan. 있어요? = 'do you have?'

keyPhrases.en: Can I use it in my phone?
keyPhrases.note: Uses the 'can' pattern to confirm compatibility before paying. 폰 = phone.
V아/어 주세요 asks someone to do something for you; 개통 = activation.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Hello. I'd like to buy a SIM.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Would you like prepaid or a plan?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: A prepaid SIM, please. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: It's 30,000 won. Your passport, please.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Here you go. Please activate it here.

beginnerGuide.title: Prepaid (선불) vs. plan (후불)
beginnerGuide.body: 선불 (prepaid) is the easiest as a newcomer: pay up front, no contract, and usually only a passport is needed. 후불 (a monthly plan) is cheaper long-term but often requires your ARC and a Korean bank account, so most people start prepaid and switch after their ARC arrives.

beginnerGuide.title: Two ways to ask a price
beginnerGuide.body: 얼마예요? means 'how much is it?' for a one-time price. To compare monthly plans, add a time word: 한 달 얼마예요? ('how much per month?'). The pattern is just [time/thing] + 얼마예요?

beginnerGuide.title: 고 싶어요 vs. 주세요
beginnerGuide.body: Use V고 싶어요 to state what YOU want to do (사고 싶어요 = 'I want to buy'), and N 주세요 to ask the seller to hand you something (유심 주세요 = 'give me a SIM'). For an action done for you, use V아/어 주세요 (개통해 주세요 = 'please activate it for me').

checkpoints: I can say I want to buy a SIM (유심 사고 싶어요) and ask for a specific one (데이터 유심 주세요).
I can ask the price (얼마예요?) and the monthly price (한 달 얼마예요?).
I can tell prepaid from a plan (선불 / 후불) and ask if they have prepaid (선불 유심 있어요?).
I can confirm it works in my phone (제 폰에서 쓸 수 있어요?) and ask them to activate it (개통해 주세요).

drills.en: I'd like to buy a top-up card.
drills.note: Reuse V고 싶어요 with a new noun; swap 충전 카드 for 유심.

drills.ko: 이거 제 폰에서 쓸 수 있어요?
drills.romanization: igeo je poneseo sseul su isseoyo?
drills.en: Can I use this in my phone?
drills.note: 이거 = 'this one' (point at it). Practice the 'can' question form.

steps: Decide prepaid vs. plan: prepaid for the first weeks (passport only), a plan later once you have your ARC.
Check your phone is unlocked and supports Korean bands or eSIM before you buy.
Hand over your passport for registration and ask the staff to activate the SIM on the spot.

deepLinks.label: Naver Map (find a phone shop)
deepLinks.note: Search a carrier name to find a nearby shop and its hours.

units.costs: Airport prepaid SIMs commonly run ~25,000–50,000 KRW depending on data and days; monthly plans vary by carrier.
units.notes: eSIM works only on supported phones — confirm 제 폰에서 쓸 수 있어요? before paying, since prepaid SIMs are often non-refundable once opened.

units.title: Buy and charge a T-money card
units.situation: At a convenience store or a subway station machine, getting the transit card you'll tap on every bus and train.
units.goal: I can buy a T-money card, load cash onto it, check whether card payment works, and ask for my balance.

keyPhrases.note: N 주세요. 티머니 is the standard rechargeable transit card sold at convenience stores.
V아/어 주세요 + amount. 만 원 = 10,000 won; 충전 = top-up/charge.

keyPhrases.en: Can I charge it with a card?
keyPhrases.note: 카드로 uses the -로/으로 'by means of' particle. Many stores only top up T-money with cash.
잔액 = remaining balance; 확인해 주세요 = 'please check (for me)'.
현금으로 = 'with cash' (-으로 after a consonant). Use this if card top-up isn't available.
오천 원 = 5,000 won; -만 = 'just/only' that amount.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Hello. A T-money card, please.

dialogue.ko: 네, 사천 원이에요. 충전도 해 드릴까요?
dialogue.romanization: ne, sacheon wonieyo. chungjeondo hae deurilkkayo?
dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.en: Sure, it's 4,000 won. Shall I charge it too?

dialogue.ko: 네, 만 원 충전해 주세요. 카드로 충전돼요?
dialogue.romanization: ne, man won chungjeonhae juseyo. kadeuro chungjeondwaeyo?
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Yes, please charge 10,000 won. Can I charge it with a card?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.en: Top-ups are cash only.

dialogue.ko: 그럼 현금으로 충전할게요. 잔액 확인해 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom hyeongeumeuro chungjeonhalgeyo. janae kwaginhae juseyo.
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Then I'll charge with cash. Please check the balance.

beginnerGuide.title: Why T-money first
beginnerGuide.body: 티머니 is a prepaid card you tap on buses, the subway, and even many taxis and convenience stores. Buy the card once (about 2,500–4,000 KRW, non-refundable) at any convenience store, then top it up with cash as you go — no app or registration needed to start.

beginnerGuide.title: The -로/으로 particle ('by means of')
beginnerGuide.body: Attach -로 after a vowel and -으로 after a consonant to say HOW you do something: 카드 → 카드로 ('by card'), 현금 → 현금으로 ('by cash'). So 카드로 충전돼요? literally asks 'does it charge by card?' Keep cash handy — store top-ups are usually cash only.

beginnerGuide.title: 충전해 주세요 = asking for the favor
beginnerGuide.body: 충전 ('charge/top-up') becomes a request with 해 주세요: 만 원 충전해 주세요 = 'please charge 10,000 won (for me)'. Put the amount first, then the verb. The same 확인해 주세요 ('please check') works for your balance: 잔액 확인해 주세요.

checkpoints: I can buy a T-money card (티머니 카드 주세요).
I can ask to load a specific amount (만 원 충전해 주세요 / 오천 원만 충전해 주세요).
I can ask if card payment works (카드로 충전돼요?) and say I'll pay cash instead (현금으로 충전할게요).
I can ask the clerk to check my balance (잔액 확인해 주세요).

drills.note: Swap the amount: 오천 원 (5,000) or 이만 원 (20,000) + 충전해 주세요.

drills.en: Can I charge it with a card?
drills.note: Change the means: 현금으로 충전돼요? ('can I charge with cash?').

steps: Buy the T-money card at any convenience store (GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) or a subway vending machine.
Top up with cash at the counter or a station machine; tell the clerk the amount (e.g. 만 원).
Tap on entry (and exit on the subway/some buses); recharge before the balance runs low.

deepLinks.label: T-money official site
deepLinks.note: Card types, balance/refund info, and where T-money is accepted.

deepLinks.label: Naver Map (find a store/station)
deepLinks.note: Locate a nearby convenience store or subway station to buy and recharge.

units.costs: Card itself ~2,500–4,000 KRW (non-refundable); top up any amount in cash. Card top-ups at stores are usually cash only.
units.notes: Keep a small balance buffer — being short at a turnstile or on a bus is the most common T-money snag, and store recharges rarely take credit cards.

tracks.title: Transport & Navigation
tracks.summary: Survival Korean for getting around Korea: the subway and bus with T-money, booking KTX/SRT trains, and taking taxis.

units.title: Subway & Bus with T-money
units.situation: You need to ride the subway and bus across the city, tap a T-money card, transfer lines, and figure out which stop to get off at.
units.goal: Find a subway station, tap T-money, ask where to transfer, and confirm your stop in polite Korean.

keyPhrases.note: Your go-to question for finding the nearest station. Swap 지하철역 for 버스 정류장 to ask for the bus stop.
정류장 means bus stop. Same '어디예요?' (where is it?) pattern as the subway question.
환승 = transfer (between subway lines or bus-to-subway). 어디서 = 'at where', using the 에서 particle for the place an action happens.

keyPhrases.en: Can I transfer with this card?
keyPhrases.note: Tap your T-money again within the time limit and transfers are usually free. 카드로 = 'with the card', using the 로/으로 particle.

keyPhrases.en: I get off at the next stop.
keyPhrases.note: 내려요 = get off. 다음 정류장 = the next stop. Works for both bus and subway.
A quick check with the driver or a fellow passenger. 여기서 = 'at here'.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the subway station?

dialogue.speaker: Passerby
dialogue.en: It's over there on the right.

dialogue.ko: 감사합니다. 시청역 가고 싶어요. 어디서 환승해요?
dialogue.romanization: gamsahamnida. sicheongyeok gago sipeoyo. eodiseo hwanseunghaeyo?
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Thank you. I want to go to City Hall Station. Where do I transfer?

dialogue.speaker: Passerby
dialogue.en: Transfer to Line 2 at the next station.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Please speak slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Passerby
dialogue.en: Okay. You transfer at the next station.

beginnerGuide.title: Tap in AND tap out
beginnerGuide.body: On the subway and most city buses you tap your T-money card on the reader when you board and again when you get off. Tapping out is what makes free transfers (환승) work and charges the correct distance-based fare. If you forget to tap out, you may be charged the maximum fare next time.

beginnerGuide.title: What 환승 really means
beginnerGuide.body: 환승 = transfer. Within about 30 minutes of tapping out, your next bus or subway ride is free or discounted as a transfer. Just keep using the same T-money card and tap normally each time — the system links the rides automatically.

beginnerGuide.title: Boarding the right bus
beginnerGuide.body: Bus numbers are color-coded: blue for long trunk routes, green for short neighborhood loops, red for express to the suburbs. Buses don't always stop unless someone is waiting and visible, so stand near the 정류장 sign and raise a hand as your bus approaches.

checkpoints: I can ask '지하철역 어디예요?' and '버스 정류장 어디예요?' to find a station or stop.
I can ask '어디서 환승해요?' and understand a direction like '다음 역에서 갈아타세요'.
I remember to tap my T-money both when boarding and when getting off.
I can say '다음 정류장에서 내려요' to signal where I'll get off.

drills.note: Practice swapping the place noun: 버스 정류장 / 화장실 / 출구.
Listen for the answer pattern '...역에서 갈아타세요'.

drills.en: I get off at the next stop.
drills.note: Change 다음 to 이번 (this one) or 시청역 (a named stop).

steps: Buy a T-money card at any convenience store (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven) and ask to load it: '충전해 주세요'.
Tap the card on the reader as you enter the gate or board the bus.
Check the line map or app for where to transfer (환승).
Tap out as you exit the gate or leave the bus to lock in your fare and transfer credit.

deepLinks.label: Naver Map (routes & transfers)
deepLinks.note: Search a destination for door-to-door subway and bus directions with transfer points.

deepLinks.label: T-money official site
deepLinks.note: Card balance, refunds, and where to buy or reload.

units.costs: T-money card: about 2,500–4,000 KRW (one-time). Base subway/bus fare from roughly 1,400 KRW with the card, plus small distance add-ons; transfers within ~30 min are usually free.
units.notes: 여기 세워 주세요 ('please stop here') is for taxis, not buses — on a bus you press the stop button and say '내려요'. Save it for Unit 3.

units.title: Booking a KTX or SRT Ticket
units.situation: You're traveling between cities and need to buy or reserve a high-speed train ticket at the station counter or in the app.
units.goal: Ask whether tickets to your destination exist, pick a departure time, and buy or confirm your ticket politely.

keyPhrases.note: 한 장 = one (flat object). Use 두 장 for two, 세 장 for three. The 주세요 pattern means 'please give me'.

keyPhrases.en: Do you have a ticket going to Busan?
keyPhrases.note: Swap 부산 for any city. 가는 = 'that goes', and 있어요? asks if it exists/is available.
거 = 'one/thing'. A natural way to ask which departure times are available.

keyPhrases.en: I want to take the next one.
keyPhrases.note: 타고 싶어요 = 'want to ride', using the V고 싶어요 pattern. 다음 거 = the next one.

keyPhrases.en: Which time shall I go with?
keyPhrases.note: 할까요? = 'shall I do?', a soft way to decide. Pairs with the staff suggesting options.
Say this at the gate or counter if you already booked in the app.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Hello. Do you have a ticket going to Busan?

dialogue.ko: 네, 있어요. 몇 시 거 드릴까요?
dialogue.romanization: ne, isseoyo. myeot si geo deurilkkayo?
dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, we do. What time would you like?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Um, what times do you have?

dialogue.ko: 두 시하고 세 시 거 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: du sihago se si geo isseoyo.
dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: We have the two o'clock and the three o'clock.

dialogue.ko: 그럼 두 시 거 한 장 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom du si geo han jang juseyo.
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Then one for two o'clock, please.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Okay, that's 59,000 won.

beginnerGuide.title: KTX vs. SRT
beginnerGuide.body: Both are high-speed trains. KTX is run by Korail and uses Seoul Station and Yongsan; SRT is a separate operator that mainly departs from Suseo Station in southern Seoul. They serve overlapping cities like Busan and Daegu, so check which station is closer to you and book on the matching app.

beginnerGuide.title: Counting tickets with 장
beginnerGuide.body: Tickets, sheets, and other flat things are counted with the counter 장: 한 장 (one), 두 장 (two), 세 장 (three). So '표 두 장 주세요' = 'two tickets, please.' This counter shows up for paper money, photos, and pizza slices too.

beginnerGuide.title: Reserved seats
beginnerGuide.body: High-speed train seats are reserved, so your ticket shows a car number (호차) and seat number. Standing tickets (입석) exist when seats sell out. If you booked in the app, you usually don't need a paper ticket — just show the screen or say '예약했어요'.

checkpoints: I can ask '부산 가는 표 있어요?' for any destination city.
I can ask '몇 시 거 있어요?' and choose a time.
I can buy a ticket with '표 한 장 주세요' and the right number + 장.
I can say '예약했어요' when I've already booked in the app.

drills.note: Practice 두 장, 세 장; combine with a destination: '부산, 표 두 장 주세요'.

drills.en: Do you have a ticket going to Busan?
drills.note: Swap the city: 대구, 광주, 대전.
Then answer for yourself: '세 시 거 주세요'.

steps: Decide your departure station — Seoul/Yongsan for KTX, Suseo for SRT — based on what's nearest.
Check times and book in the app or at a counter/kiosk.
At the counter, ask '부산 가는 표 있어요?' then '몇 시 거 있어요?'.
Confirm the time and buy: '두 시 거 한 장 주세요'. Note your 호차 (car) and seat number.

deepLinks.label: Korail (KTX) booking
deepLinks.note: Official KTX timetables and reservations; departs Seoul Station / Yongsan.

deepLinks.label: SRT booking
deepLinks.note: Official SRT reservations; mainly departs Suseo Station.

units.costs: Seoul–Busan high-speed runs roughly 50,000–60,000 KRW one way in standard class; shorter routes cost less. Prices vary by distance and seat class.
units.notes: If you don't catch the price, fall back to '얼마예요?' (how much is it?). Times are often spoken in pure-Korean hours: 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00).

units.title: Taking a Taxi & Giving Directions
units.situation: You're taking a taxi and need to give the destination, ask to stop, and pay — possibly by card.
units.goal: Tell the driver where to go, ask them to stop, confirm card payment, and check the fare in polite Korean.

keyPhrases.note: Show the address on your phone and say this. 주소로 = 'to the address' (로/으로 particle); 가 주세요 uses the V아/어 주세요 'please do for me' pattern.
세워 주세요 = 'please stop (the car)'. This is the correct taxi phrase — don't use it on a bus.
A polite way to say you're getting out at this spot.
Most taxis take cards, but it's polite to confirm. 돼요? = 'does it work / is it okay?'
Ask at the end of the ride to confirm the fare before paying.
Use it if you don't catch the fare or the driver's question.

dialogue.speaker: Driver
dialogue.en: Where are you going?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Please go to this address.

dialogue.speaker: Driver
dialogue.en: Okay, got it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Please stop in front of that traffic light.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Can I pay by card? How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Driver
dialogue.en: Yes, card is fine. It's 8,000 won.

beginnerGuide.title: Show, don't just say
beginnerGuide.body: Korean addresses can be hard to pronounce, so the easiest move is to pull up the destination in a map app and show the screen while saying '이 주소로 가 주세요'. Many drivers will type it into their own navigation. Hailing through the Kakao T app skips the talking entirely — the address is already set.

beginnerGuide.title: Stopping where you want
beginnerGuide.body: Use '여기 세워 주세요' (please stop here) or point to a landmark: '저기 편의점 앞에서 세워 주세요' (please stop in front of that convenience store over there). 앞에서 = 'in front of', a handy way to be precise without an exact address.

beginnerGuide.title: Paying and tipping
beginnerGuide.body: Tipping is not expected in Korea. Cards work in nearly all taxis, but confirm with '카드 돼요?' just in case. The meter sets the fare, so '얼마예요?' is mostly to hear the final number — there's no haggling.

checkpoints: I can give a destination with '이 주소로 가 주세요' while showing my phone.
I can ask the driver to stop with '여기 세워 주세요'.
I can confirm payment with '카드 돼요?' and check the fare with '얼마예요?'.
I can ask the driver to repeat with '다시 말해 주세요'.

drills.note: Swap in a place: '서울역으로 가 주세요'.
Add a landmark: '편의점 앞에서 세워 주세요'.
Follow up with '얼마예요?' to confirm the fare.

steps: Hail a taxi on the street (a red 빈차 light means it's free) or call one in the Kakao T app.
Show the destination on your map and say '이 주소로 가 주세요'.
Near your stop, say '여기 세워 주세요' or name a landmark with 앞에서.
Confirm payment and fare: '카드 돼요? 얼마예요?'.

deepLinks.label: Kakao Mobility (Kakao T)
deepLinks.note: Korea's main taxi-hailing app; sets your pickup and destination automatically.

deepLinks.label: Naver Map (find an address)
deepLinks.note: Search your destination and show the screen to the driver.

units.costs: Standard taxi base fare is roughly 4,800 KRW in Seoul (varies by region), rising with distance and time; late-night rides add a surcharge.
units.notes: If unsure of the amount, combine '다시 말해 주세요' with '얼마예요?'.

tracks.title: Housing, Banking & Admin
tracks.summary: Survival Korean for renting a home, opening a bank account, and sorting your trash in your first weeks in Korea.

units.title: Find a Place & Understand the Lease
units.situation: You walk into a real-estate office (부동산) to look at a studio or one-room and need to ask about rent, deposit, and move-in.
units.goal: Ask about monthly rent (월세) and deposit (보증금), check maintenance fees, and confirm when you can move in.

keyPhrases.en: How much is the monthly rent?
keyPhrases.note: 월세 = monthly rent. 얼마예요? asks the price. The most common question in any 부동산.
보증금 = deposit. With 월세 the deposit is usually smaller (a few hundred to a few thousand 만원).
이사 가다 = to move (house). V-ㄹ/을 수 있어요 = can/be able to. Use this to confirm the available move-in date.
관리비 = monthly building maintenance fee (often separate from rent, covers cleaning, security, sometimes water/internet). 있어요? = is there?

keyPhrases.en: I would like to see the room.
keyPhrases.note: 방 = room. V-고 싶어요 = I want to. Polite way to ask for a viewing.

keyPhrases.en: Does this place have internet and gas?
keyPhrases.note: 하고 = and (connects nouns). 돼요? = does it work / is it available?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Excuse me. I'd like to see a one-room (studio).

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.en: Sure, how about this room? It's clean.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: How much is the monthly rent? How much is the deposit?

dialogue.ko: 보증금 천만 원에 월세 오십만 원이에요. 관리비는 오만 원이에요.
dialogue.romanization: bojeunggeum cheonman wone wolse osimman wonieyo. gwallibineun oman wonieyo.
dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.en: The deposit is 10 million won and the rent is 500,000 won. The maintenance fee is 50,000 won.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: When can I move in?

dialogue.ko: 다음 주에 이사 올 수 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: daeum jue isa ol su isseoyo.
dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.en: You can move in next week.

beginnerGuide.title: 월세 vs 전세 — two ways to rent
beginnerGuide.body: 월세 (monthly rent): you pay a smaller deposit (보증금) plus rent every month — this is what most newcomers choose. 전세 (jeonse): instead of monthly rent, you hand the landlord one very large lump-sum deposit (often tens of thousands of 만원), pay no monthly rent, and get the entire amount back when you leave. 전세 needs a huge amount of cash up front, so as a newcomer you'll almost always start with 월세.

beginnerGuide.title: Your deposit comes back
beginnerGuide.body: 보증금 (deposit) is NOT a fee — the landlord holds it and returns it to you when you move out (이사 갈 때), as long as there's no unpaid rent or damage. Always get the lease (계약서) in writing and keep a copy. 관리비 (maintenance fee), by contrast, is a real monthly cost you do not get back.

beginnerGuide.title: Reading a price out loud
beginnerGuide.body: Rent and deposits are spoken in 만원 (10,000-won units). 오십만 원 = 500,000 won. 천만 원 = 10,000,000 won. When the agent says a number fast, use 천천히 말해 주세요 (please speak slowly) and 잘 모르겠어요 (I don't understand) to slow things down.

checkpoints: Ask the monthly rent and deposit using 월세가 얼마예요? and 보증금이 얼마예요?
Confirm the move-in date with 언제 이사 갈 수 있어요?
Ask whether there is a maintenance fee with 관리비가 있어요?
Explain in one sentence the difference between 월세 and 전세.

drills.note: Swap 보증금 for 월세 or 관리비 to ask about each cost.

drills.en: I'd like to see this room.
drills.note: Practice V-고 싶어요: 계약하고 싶어요 (I want to sign), 이사 가고 싶어요 (I want to move).

drills.ko: 다음 달에 이사 갈 수 있어요?
drills.romanization: daeum dare isa gal su isseoyo?
drills.en: Can I move in next month?
drills.note: V-ㄹ/을 수 있어요 = can. Try 더 싼 방 있어요? (Is there a cheaper room?).

steps: Visit a 부동산 (real-estate office) near the neighborhood you want, or browse listings online first.
Tell the agent your budget and ask 방을 보고 싶어요.
For each room ask 월세가 얼마예요?, 보증금이 얼마예요?, and 관리비가 있어요?.
Confirm the move-in date and what the deposit covers, then ask to see the 계약서 (lease) before signing.

deepLinks.label: Naver Real Estate (네이버 부동산)
deepLinks.note: Browse 월세/전세 listings by neighborhood with photos and prices before visiting an office.

units.costs: Typical studio 월세: deposit 보증금 5,000,000–10,000,000 won + monthly rent 400,000–700,000 won; 관리비 (maintenance) often 30,000–100,000 won extra. 전세 needs a far larger lump-sum deposit.
units.notes: Bring your 외국인등록증 (ARC) to sign a lease. A Korean-speaking friend or agent can help review the 계약서.

units.title: Open a Bank Account
units.situation: You go to a bank branch to open your first Korean account (계좌) so you can receive your salary and pay rent.
units.goal: Open a bank account, show your ARC, request a debit card, and ask about internet banking.

keyPhrases.en: I'd like to open a bank account.
keyPhrases.note: 계좌 = account. 만들다 = to make/open. V-고 싶어요 = I want to. This opens the whole conversation at the teller window.

keyPhrases.en: I have my Alien Registration Card.
keyPhrases.note: 외국인등록증 = ARC (foreigner ID). 있어요 = I have it. Banks require it plus a Korean phone number.

keyPhrases.en: Please make me a debit card too.
keyPhrases.note: 체크카드 = debit (check) card, drawn directly from your account. 도 = also/too. V-아/어 주세요 = please do (for me).
인터넷뱅킹 = online/mobile banking. 돼요? = is it possible / does it work? Ask so you can transfer money from your phone.

keyPhrases.en: Do you also need my passport?
keyPhrases.note: 여권 = passport. 필요해요 = is needed. Some branches ask for passport plus ARC, so confirm what to bring.
송금하다 = to send money/transfer. V-ㄹ/을 수 있어요 = can. Useful for paying rent or sending money home.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Hello. I'd like to open a bank account.

dialogue.speaker: Teller
dialogue.en: Sure, do you have your Alien Registration Card?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Yes, I have my ARC. Do you also need my passport?

dialogue.speaker: Teller
dialogue.en: Please give me your passport too. And I also need your phone number.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Please make me a debit card too. Is internet banking available?

dialogue.speaker: Teller
dialogue.en: Yes, it is. Please install the app.

beginnerGuide.title: What to bring
beginnerGuide.body: To open an account you almost always need: (1) your 외국인등록증 (ARC) — the bank cannot open an account without proof of legal residence, (2) a Korean mobile phone number for verification, and often (3) your 여권 (passport). Bring all three to be safe. Without an ARC yet, some banks open only a limited 'foreigner' account, so it's easiest once your ARC has arrived.

beginnerGuide.title: 체크카드 vs 신용카드
beginnerGuide.body: A 체크카드 (debit card) pulls money directly from your account — easy to get and the right first card for newcomers. A 신용카드 (credit card) is a loan and usually needs Korean credit history, so it's hard to get at first. Ask for a 체크카드 with 체크카드도 만들어 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Set up mobile banking
beginnerGuide.body: Most banking happens in the bank's app (인터넷뱅킹 / 모바일뱅킹). After opening the account, ask 인터넷뱅킹 돼요? and let the teller help you register so you can check your balance and send transfers (송금) from your phone. If the teller talks too fast, say 천천히 말해 주세요.

checkpoints: State your purpose with 계좌를 만들고 싶어요.
Confirm you have your ARC with 외국인등록증 있어요.
Request a debit card using 체크카드도 만들어 주세요.
Ask about online banking with 인터넷뱅킹 돼요?.

drills.en: I want to open an account.
drills.note: Swap the noun: 체크카드를 만들고 싶어요 (I want to make a debit card).

drills.en: Please make a debit card too.
drills.note: V-아/어 주세요 = please do for me. Try 천천히 말해 주세요 (please speak slowly).
V-ㄹ/을 수 있어요 = can. Try 인터넷뱅킹 할 수 있어요? (Can I use internet banking?).

steps: Take a number ticket at the branch and wait for a teller window (창구).
Say 계좌를 만들고 싶어요 and hand over your 외국인등록증 (and 여권 if asked).
Give your Korean phone number for verification.
Request a 체크카드 and ask 인터넷뱅킹 돼요?, then register for the mobile app.

deepLinks.label: Woori Bank Global Banking
deepLinks.note: Major bank with English-language services and foreigner account guidance.

deepLinks.label: Hana Bank (KEB Hana)
deepLinks.note: Another major bank widely used by foreign residents for first accounts and transfers.

units.costs: Opening a basic account is free. 체크카드 issuance is usually free or about 1,000–3,000 won. Domestic transfers via app are often free or a few hundred won; international 송금 carries higher fees that vary by bank.
units.notes: Banks have tightened anti-fraud rules, so a brand-new foreigner account may start with daily transfer limits. Keep your ARC and phone number consistent across services to avoid verification problems.

units.title: Sort Your Trash
units.situation: You're settling into your new place and need to figure out recycling (분리수거) and where to buy the official volume-rate trash bag (종량제봉투).
units.goal: Buy the correct trash bag, learn how to sort recycling, and find out where to put food waste — without breaking your district's rules.

keyPhrases.note: 종량제봉투 = the official pay-as-you-throw bag sold at convenience stores/supermarkets. Add a size: 이십 리터 (20L). Only general waste goes in this bag.

keyPhrases.en: How do I do the recycling sorting?
keyPhrases.note: 분리수거 = separating recyclables. 어떻게 해요? = how do I do it? Ask a neighbor or your landlord; rules differ by building.

keyPhrases.en: Where do I throw out food waste?
keyPhrases.note: 음식물 쓰레기 = food waste (collected separately!). 어디에 = where. 버리다 = to throw away. -에 marks the place/destination.

keyPhrases.en: May I throw it away here?
keyPhrases.note: 여기에 = here (place). V-아/어도 돼요? = is it okay if / may I? Polite way to check before dumping trash in the wrong spot.

keyPhrases.en: Where do I buy the trash bags?
keyPhrases.note: 어디에서 = at where (-에서 marks where an action happens). 사다 = to buy. Usually the nearest 편의점 (convenience store) or supermarket.

keyPhrases.en: Please don't throw it away here.
keyPhrases.note: V-지 마세요 = please don't. You'll see this on signs; recognizing it keeps you from getting fined.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Excuse me. A volume-rate trash bag, please.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.en: What size (how many liters) would you like?

dialogue.ko: 이십 리터 주세요. 분리수거 어떻게 해요?
dialogue.romanization: isim niteo juseyo. bullisugeo eotteoke haeyo?
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: A 20-liter one, please. How do I sort the recycling?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.en: You have to throw out plastic and paper separately.

dialogue.ko: 음식물 쓰레기는 어디에 버려요? 여기에 버려도 돼요?
dialogue.romanization: eumsingmul sseuregineun eodie beoryeoyo? yeogie beoryeodo dwaeyo?
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Where do I throw out food waste? May I throw it here?

dialogue.ko: 음식물은 따로 버려야 해요. 여기에 버리지 마세요.
dialogue.romanization: eumsingmureun ttaro beoryeoya haeyo. yeogie beoriji maseyo.
dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.en: Food waste has to go separately. Please don't throw it here.

beginnerGuide.title: Three streams: general, recycling, food
beginnerGuide.body: Korean trash splits into three: (1) general waste — must go in the paid 종량제봉투 (volume-rate bag); (2) 분리수거 (recyclables) — plastic, paper, glass, cans, PET bottles, rinsed and separated; (3) 음식물 쓰레기 (food waste) — collected on its own, often in a special small bag or a designated bin. Putting general trash out without the official bag, or mixing food waste in, can get you a fine.

beginnerGuide.title: Rules change by 구 (district)
beginnerGuide.body: The 종량제봉투 is printed for a specific 구 (district) or 시 (city) — a bag from another district may be rejected. Bag colors, food-waste systems, and collection days all vary locally. When in doubt, ask a neighbor or your landlord 분리수거 어떻게 해요? and check your district office (구청) notice, or look it up on the government services portal.

beginnerGuide.title: Buying and using the bag
beginnerGuide.body: Buy 종량제봉투 at the nearest 편의점 (convenience store) or supermarket — say 종량제봉투 주세요 and a size like 이십 리터 (20L) or 오십 리터 (50L). Use V-아/어도 돼요? (여기에 버려도 돼요?) to check a drop-off spot, and recognize V-지 마세요 (버리지 마세요 = don't throw here) on signs so you don't break the rules.

checkpoints: Buy a trash bag and state a size, e.g. 종량제봉투 주세요 / 이십 리터 주세요.
Ask how to sort recycling with 분리수거 어떻게 해요?
Ask where food waste goes with 음식물 쓰레기는 어디에 버려요?
Politely check a spot using 여기에 버려도 돼요?.

drills.en: Please give me a trash bag.
drills.note: Add a size + counter: 십 리터 / 이십 리터 / 오십 리터 주세요.

drills.en: May I throw it away here?
drills.note: V-아/어도 돼요? = may I? Try 여기에 주차해도 돼요? (May I park here?).

drills.en: Food waste must be thrown out separately.
drills.note: V-아/어야 해요 = must. 따로 = separately. Try 봉투를 사야 해요 (I must buy a bag).

steps: Buy the 종량제봉투 for your district at a 편의점 or supermarket (say a size).
Put only general waste in the official bag.
Rinse and separate recyclables (plastic, paper, glass, cans) for 분리수거.
Take 음식물 쓰레기 (food waste) to its designated bag/bin, and check your building's collection days and spots.

deepLinks.label: Government Services (gov.kr)
deepLinks.note: Government portal — search your district (구) for local waste-disposal and recycling rules and notices.

units.costs: 종량제봉투 prices depend on district and size: roughly 300–500 won for a 10L bag, more for larger sizes; food-waste bags are sold similarly. Improper disposal can result in fines.
units.notes: Collection days and times are set per neighborhood — putting trash out on the wrong day or place is the most common newcomer mistake. Ask your landlord or a neighbor early, and keep the right district's bags on hand.

tracks.title: Food, Shopping & Health
tracks.summary: Survival Korean for ordering and paying at restaurants, getting medicine at a pharmacy or clinic, and handling parcels and daily weather.

units.title: Ordering & Paying Out
units.situation: You sit down at a small Korean restaurant or step up to a cafe counter. There may be no English menu, and you need to call the staff over, order, and pay by card.
units.goal: Call a server, order food or drinks, ask if you can pay by card, and request takeout — using polite 해요체.

keyPhrases.note: The standard way to call staff in a Korean restaurant. Say it clearly, not too loudly. 저기요 works the same way.
Point at the menu or a dish while you say it. 이거 = this thing. Works for almost any item.
Water and side dishes (반찬) are usually free and self-serve, but it's fine to ask. 주세요 = please give me.
메뉴판 = the physical menu. Useful when only a wall menu is posted.

keyPhrases.en: Please ring me up. / The bill, please.
keyPhrases.note: In Korea you usually pay at the front counter, not at the table. 계산 = payment/calculation.
Almost everywhere takes card, but tiny shops or street stalls may be cash only. 돼요? = is it okay / does it work?

keyPhrases.en: To go, please. / Please pack it up.
keyPhrases.note: 포장 = packaging. For takeout. To eat in, say 여기서 먹을게요 (I'll eat here).

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Excuse me! Can I get a menu?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure, here you go. What can I get you?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: This one, please. And some water.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Okay, one moment.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Excuse me, I'd like to pay. Do you take card?

dialogue.ko: 네, 카드 돼요. 여기서 찍어 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, kadeu dwaeyo. yeogiseo jjigeo juseyo.
dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, card is fine. Please tap here.

beginnerGuide.title: 주세요 is your power phrase
beginnerGuide.body: Attach 주세요 (please give me) to almost any noun to order it: 물 주세요, 김치 주세요, 이거 주세요. To ask someone to DO something for you, use the verb stem + 아/어 주세요, as in 포장해 주세요 (please pack it) or 계산해 주세요 (please ring me up).

beginnerGuide.title: Calling staff is expected
beginnerGuide.body: It is completely normal and polite to call out 여기요! or 저기요! to get a server's attention — they will not come unless you do. Make eye contact, say it once, and wait. You do not need to raise your hand awkwardly or wait to be noticed.

beginnerGuide.title: You usually pay at the counter
beginnerGuide.body: In most Korean eateries you bring the bill (or just walk) to the front register to pay, rather than paying at your table. Card is accepted nearly everywhere; carry a little cash for small or older shops that may be cash only.

checkpoints: Call a server's attention with 여기요 or 저기요 without hesitating.
Order at least two items using 이거 주세요 and 물 주세요.
Ask whether card is accepted with 카드 돼요? and request the bill with 계산해 주세요.
Choose correctly between eating in (여기서 먹을게요) and takeout (포장해 주세요).

drills.note: Swap 이거 for any noun: 물 / 김치 / 커피 주세요.
Contrast with 여기서 먹을게요 = I'll eat here.
Reuse 돼요? for other yes/no checks: 여기 돼요? (is here okay?).

steps: Enter and seat yourself, or wait briefly if a sign says 안내 (you'll be seated).
Call the server: 여기요! and ask for the menu: 메뉴판 주세요.
Point and order: 이거 주세요. Add drinks/water: 물 주세요.
When finished, go to the counter: 계산해 주세요, then 카드 돼요?
For leftovers or takeout, say 포장해 주세요.

deepLinks.label: Find restaurants near you (Naver Map)
deepLinks.note: Search a dish or 맛집 (good restaurant) plus your neighborhood to see reviews, hours, and whether they do takeout.

units.costs: A casual single-dish meal (kimbap, noodles, rice bowl) typically runs about 6,000–10,000 KRW. Cafe drinks are roughly 3,000–6,000 KRW. No tipping is expected anywhere in Korea.
units.notes: Side dishes (반찬) and water are usually free and often self-serve — look for a water/utensil station near the entrance.

units.title: Pharmacy & Clinic
units.situation: You feel sick or have a headache. You need to describe what hurts at a clinic (병원), pick up medicine (약), and find or use a pharmacy (약국) — possibly with a prescription (처방전).
units.goal: Say where it hurts, find a pharmacy, hand over or ask for a prescription, and ask how to take your medicine — using 해요체 and want/must forms.

keyPhrases.note: The core word for feeling unwell or being in pain. Use it alone or with a body part: 머리가 아파요.
What staff will ask you. 어디 = where, 가 marks the subject (the part that hurts).

keyPhrases.en: My head hurts. / I have a headache.
keyPhrases.note: Swap the body part: 배가 아파요 (stomach), 목이 아파요 (throat). 가/이 marks what hurts.
Common cold symptom. 콧물 = nasal mucus, 나요 = it comes out. Also 기침이 나요 (I have a cough).
약국 = pharmacy, marked by 이. Pharmacies show a green cross sign. 약 alone = medicine.

keyPhrases.en: May I have the prescription, please.
keyPhrases.note: 처방전 = prescription slip. The clinic gives you this to take to a separate pharmacy.

keyPhrases.en: How do I take this medicine?
keyPhrases.note: 어떻게 = how, 먹어요 = take/eat. Koreans say 약을 먹다 (eat medicine) for taking pills.
V + 고 싶어요 = want to. For over-the-counter remedies you can buy directly at the 약국 without a 처방전.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.en: Where does it hurt?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: My head hurts. And I have a runny nose.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.en: It's a cold. I'll give you a prescription.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Thank you. Where is a pharmacy?

dialogue.speaker: Pharmacist
dialogue.en: Your prescription, please. Here's your medicine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: How do I take this medicine?

dialogue.speaker: Pharmacist
dialogue.en: Three times a day, after meals.

beginnerGuide.title: Clinic first, pharmacy second
beginnerGuide.body: In Korea, the doctor (병원/의원) diagnoses you and prints a 처방전 (prescription), but does NOT give you the pills. You take that slip to a nearby 약국 (pharmacy) — almost always within a short walk — to actually receive your medicine. For minor issues like a headache or cold, you can skip the clinic and buy over-the-counter medicine straight from the pharmacy.

beginnerGuide.title: Describe symptoms with [part]가/이 아파요
beginnerGuide.body: Name the body part, add 가 or 이, then 아파요: 머리가 아파요 (head), 배가 아파요 (stomach), 목이 아파요 (throat). For other symptoms use [thing]이/가 나요: 콧물이 나요 (runny nose), 기침이 나요 (cough), 열이 나요 (fever).

beginnerGuide.title: Want vs. must when getting medicine
beginnerGuide.body: Use V + 고 싶어요 to say what you want — 약 사고 싶어요 (I want to buy medicine). The pharmacist may tell you what you MUST do with V + 아/어야 해요 — 식후에 먹어야 해요 (you have to take it after meals). Listen for 하루에 ~번 (~ times a day) and 식후/식전 (after/before meals).

checkpoints: State at least two symptoms, e.g. 머리가 아파요 and 콧물이 나요.
Ask for directions to a pharmacy with 약국이 어디예요?
Hand over or request a prescription using 처방전 주세요.
Ask how to take the medicine with 이 약 어떻게 먹어요? and understand 하루에 세 번 / 식후에.

drills.note: Swap the part: 배가 / 목이 / 이가 아파요.
V고 싶어요 = want to. Try 쉬고 싶어요 (I want to rest).

drills.en: How do I take this medicine?
drills.note: Listen for 하루에 세 번 (3x a day) and 식후에 (after meals) in the answer.

steps: At the clinic reception, say 아파요 and answer 어디가 아파요? with [part]가/이 아파요.
Receive the 처방전 from the doctor (or skip to a pharmacy for minor symptoms).
Find a green-cross 약국 nearby; ask 약국이 어디예요? if needed.
Hand over the slip: 처방전 주세요 / 처방전 있어요.
Before leaving, ask 이 약 어떻게 먹어요? and note the timing (하루에 ~번, 식후/식전).
units.costs: A clinic visit with national health insurance is often about 5,000–15,000 KRW out of pocket; prescription medicine is usually a few thousand won. Over-the-counter cold or headache medicine at a pharmacy is typically 3,000–8,000 KRW.
units.notes: Pharmacies (약국) display a green cross. Most cold, headache, and digestive remedies are sold over the counter. Pharmacies often close in the evening and on Sundays; look for a 24-hour 약국 or a hospital pharmacy for late-night needs.

units.title: Parcels & Daily Weather
units.situation: You're expecting a 택배 (parcel) and want to know when it arrives or where it was left, and you want to check the weather and 미세먼지 (fine dust) before heading out.
units.goal: Ask whether and when a parcel has arrived, tell the courier where to leave it, and ask about today's fine dust — using 있어요/없어요 and request forms.

keyPhrases.note: 택배 = courier parcel, 왔어요 = came (past of 와요). 가 marks the subject. Very common to ask a guard or housemate.
언제 = when. Couriers often send an SMS with a rough time window. 와요 = comes.
있어요 = there is / exists. Ask the building's security desk (경비실). Opposite: 없어요 (there isn't).

keyPhrases.en: Please leave it at the door.
keyPhrases.note: 문 앞 = in front of the door, 놔 주세요 = please put/leave it. A standard delivery instruction.
경비실 = the guard/security office in an apartment building, 맡겨 주세요 = please entrust it. Common when you're out.
미세먼지 = fine dust (air pollution), 어때요? = how is it? A daily small-talk and health question in Korea.

keyPhrases.en: There's a lot of fine dust.
keyPhrases.note: 많아요 = there's a lot / it's high. On these days wear a mask (마스크). Opposite: 미세먼지가 적어요 (low).

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Hello. Is there a parcel for me?

dialogue.speaker: Guard
dialogue.en: What's your name?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Unit 504. Did a parcel come?

dialogue.speaker: Guard
dialogue.en: Yes, there's one. Here you go.

dialogue.ko: 감사합니다. 다음에는 문 앞에 놔 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: gamsahamnida. daeumeneun mun ape nwa juseyo.
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Thank you. Next time, please leave it at the door.

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.en: How's the fine dust today?

dialogue.ko: 미세먼지가 많아요. 마스크 쓰는 게 좋아요.
dialogue.romanization: misemeonjiga manayo. maseukeu sseuneun ge joayo.
dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: There's a lot of fine dust. It's better to wear a mask.

beginnerGuide.title: 있어요 / 없어요 for parcels
beginnerGuide.body: 있어요 means 'there is / I have it' and 없어요 means 'there isn't / I don't have it.' Ask 택배 있어요? (is there a parcel?) at the security desk; the answer is 네, 있어요 or 아니요, 없어요. To ask if it arrived, use the past tense: 택배가 왔어요? (did it come?).

beginnerGuide.title: Tell the courier where to leave it
beginnerGuide.body: Most parcels are left without a signature. Tell the driver via the app or a note where to put it: 문 앞에 놔 주세요 (leave it at the door) or 경비실에 맡겨 주세요 (leave it with security). 경비실 is the staffed guard office found in most Korean apartment buildings.

beginnerGuide.title: Check fine dust like you check rain
beginnerGuide.body: 미세먼지 (fine dust, PM10/PM2.5) is part of daily life in Korea, especially in spring. People routinely ask 오늘 미세먼지 어때요? On bad days (미세먼지가 많아요) many wear a mask (마스크) outdoors. Check an air-quality app or AirKorea before going out, the same way you'd check the weather.

checkpoints: Ask whether a parcel arrived (택배가 왔어요?) and whether one is being held (택배 있어요?).
Ask when it will come with 택배 언제 와요?
Give a delivery instruction: 문 앞에 놔 주세요 or 경비실에 맡겨 주세요.
Ask and answer about fine dust with 오늘 미세먼지 어때요? / 미세먼지가 많아요.

drills.note: 있어요/없어요 to answer: 네, 왔어요 / 아니요, 안 왔어요.

drills.en: Please leave it at the door.
drills.note: Swap the place: 경비실에 / 택배함에 맡겨 주세요.

drills.en: There's a lot of fine dust.
drills.note: Opposite: 미세먼지가 적어요 (it's low). Pair with 마스크 쓰는 게 좋아요.

steps: When expecting a parcel, check your delivery SMS or app for the time window (택배 언제 와요?).
Leave an instruction for the driver: 문 앞에 놔 주세요 or 경비실에 맡겨 주세요.
If it's missing, ask the guard: 택배 있어요? / 택배가 왔어요?
Before going out, check air quality: 오늘 미세먼지 어때요?
On high-dust days (미세먼지가 많아요), wear a mask outdoors.

deepLinks.label: CJ Logistics parcel tracking
deepLinks.note: Korea's largest courier. Enter your tracking number to see your 택배 status.

deepLinks.label: Korea Post (EMS / domestic mail)
deepLinks.note: Track government postal parcels and registered mail; also for sending packages.

deepLinks.label: AirKorea fine dust index
deepLinks.note: Official real-time 미세먼지 (PM10/PM2.5) levels by region — check before heading out.

deepLinks.label: KMA weather forecast
deepLinks.note: Korea Meteorological Administration: official daily weather and air-quality forecasts.

units.costs: Standard domestic courier (택배) shipping is typically about 3,000–5,000 KRW when you send a box; most online purchases include free or low-cost delivery. Checking weather and fine dust apps is free.
units.notes: Korean apartment deliveries are usually contactless — drivers leave parcels at the door, in a parcel box (택배함), or with the security office (경비실). Save your tracking number to follow the parcel online.

dialogues.title: Opening a Bank Account
dialogues.situation: You go to a bank to open your first account and get a debit card.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. What brings you in today?
lines.note: standard bank greeting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I would like to open an account.
lines.note: 통장 = bankbook/account

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Did you bring your ID?
lines.note: 신분증 = ID card

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, here is my alien registration card.
lines.note: 외국인등록증 = ARC, the foreigner ID

lines.ko: 여기 신청서에 성함하고 연락처 적어 주세요.
lines.romanization: yeogi sincheongseoe seonghamhago yeollakcheo jeogeo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please write your name and phone number on this form here.
lines.note: 성함 = honorific for name

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Can I get a debit card with it too?
lines.note: 체크카드 = debit card

lines.ko: 네, 가능해요. 비밀번호 네 자리 눌러 주세요.
lines.romanization: ne, ganeunghaeyo. bimilbeonho ne jari nulleo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that is possible. Please enter a four-digit PIN.
lines.note: 비밀번호 = password/PIN

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I would also like to sign up for internet banking.

lines.ko: 그럼 휴대폰으로 본인 인증 한번 할게요.
lines.romanization: geureom hyudaeponeuro bonin injeung hanbeon halgeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then let me verify your identity with your phone.
lines.note: 본인 인증 = identity verification

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: When does the card come out?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I will issue it right now. One moment please.
lines.note: 발급 = issue

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, thank you.

dialogues.tip: Bring your 외국인등록증 (ARC) and a Korean phone number, since banks verify your identity by phone. New foreign accounts often start with a low daily transfer limit for fraud protection.

dialogues.title: Asking About a Transfer
dialogues.situation: You go to the bank counter to send money and ask about the transfer limit and fee.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. I came to make a transfer.
lines.note: 계좌이체 = bank transfer

lines.ko: 네, 받는 분 계좌번호 알고 계세요?
lines.romanization: ne, banneun bun gyejwabeonho algo gyeseyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, do you know the recipient's account number?
lines.note: 받는 분 = the person receiving

lines.ko: 네, 여기 적어 왔어요. 백만 원 보내고 싶어요.
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi jeogeo wasseoyo. baengman won bonaego sipeoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I wrote it down here. I want to send one million won.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Have you by any chance checked your transfer limit?
lines.note: 이체 한도 = transfer limit

lines.ko: 한도가 얼마예요? 오늘 다 보낼 수 있어요?
lines.romanization: handoga eolmayeyo? oneul da bonael su isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What is the limit? Can I send it all today?

lines.ko: 하루 한도가 백만 원이라서 딱 돼요.
lines.romanization: haru handoga baengman woniraseo ttak dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Your daily limit is one million won, so it works exactly.
lines.note: -라서 = because (giving a reason)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much is the fee?
lines.note: 수수료 = fee

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If it is the same bank, it is free.
lines.note: -(으)면 = if

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What if it is a different bank?

lines.ko: 오백 원 붙어요. 비밀번호 눌러 주세요.
lines.romanization: obaek won buteoyo. bimilbeonho nulleo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There is a 500 won charge. Please enter your PIN.
lines.note: 붙다 = to be added on

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Did it go through? Will I get a confirmation text?

lines.ko: 네, 이체 완료됐어요. 문자 갈 거예요.
lines.romanization: ne, iche wallyodwaesseoyo. munja gal geoyeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, the transfer is complete. A text will be sent.
lines.note: 완료 = completion

dialogues.tip: If you hit your daily 이체 한도, you can raise it in the bank app or in person, though raising it usually needs extra verification. Transfers within the same bank are free, while inter-bank transfers add a small fee.

dialogues.title: Move-in Report at the Community Center
dialogues.situation: You go to the 주민센터 to report a change of address and pick up a residence document.

lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 번호표 뽑고 잠시만 기다려 주세요.
lines.romanization: annyeonghaseyo. beonhopyo ppopgo jamsiman gidaryeo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. Please take a number and wait a moment.
lines.note: 번호표 = number ticket

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay. I came to file a move-in report.
lines.note: 전입신고 = move-in/address report

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What is your new address?
lines.note: polite way to ask for info

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I moved to Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu.
lines.note: -(으)로 = marks destination

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you show me your ID and lease contract?
lines.note: 계약서 = contract

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here you go. How many days until it is processed?
lines.note: 처리되다 = to be processed

lines.ko: 오늘 바로 처리돼요. 여기 서명해 주세요.
lines.romanization: oneul baro cheoridwaeyo. yeogi seomyeonghae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It is processed today right away. Please sign here.
lines.note: 서명 = signature

lines.ko: 그리고 주민등록등본도 한 통 떼고 싶어요.
lines.romanization: geurigo jumindeungnokdeungbondo han tong ttego sipeoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: And I would also like to get one copy of a residence certificate.
lines.note: 등본 한 통 떼다 = print one copy of a certificate

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The fee is 400 won—would you like to pay by card?
lines.note: -(으)ㄴ데 = and/so (background)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: By any chance, can I get the document in English too?
lines.note: -(으)로 된 = made in/written in

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: An English document has to be requested separately.
lines.note: -아/어야 되다 = have to

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see. Then just the certificate please. Thank you.

dialogues.tip: You must report a move within 14 days. Bring your ID and lease, and you can print a 주민등록등본 (residence certificate) at the same visit. Foreign residents may instead report at an immigration office, so check which applies to your visa.

dialogues.title: Viewing a One-Room with a Real Estate Agent
dialogues.situation: You found a 원룸 listing online and meet a 부동산 agent to view a monthly-rent (월세) studio in person.

lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 인터넷에서 보고 연락드렸는데요, 그 원룸 보러 왔어요.
lines.romanization: annyeonghaseyo. inteoneseseo bogo yeollakdeuryeonneundeyo, geu wollum boreo wasseoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. I called after seeing it online — I came to view that one-room.
lines.note: 보고 연락드렸는데요 = a polite, natural way to say 'I contacted you after seeing it'; 드리다 humbles the verb

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, yes. Shall we go right up and take a look? It's on the 4th floor.
lines.note: 보실까요 = 'shall we look?'; -(으)ㄹ까요 suggests doing something together

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What are the deposit and the monthly rent?
lines.note: 어떻게 돼요 = the standard way to ask 'what is it / how much is it' for set figures

lines.ko: 보증금 천만 원에 월세 오십이에요. 관리비는 따로 칠만 원이고요.
lines.romanization: bojeunggeum cheonman wone wolse osibieyo. gwallibineun ttaro chilman wonigoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's a ten-million-won deposit with 500,000 a month. The maintenance fee is 70,000 separately.
lines.note: 보증금 천에 월세 오십 = how Koreans say rent: deposit 'X' with monthly 'Y'; 만 원 is dropped in speech

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What's included in the maintenance fee? Is water included too?
lines.note: 포함되다 = to be included; 수도세 = water bill

lines.ko: 수도세랑 인터넷은 포함이고, 전기세랑 가스비는 따로 내셔야 돼요.
lines.romanization: sudoserang inteoneseun pohamigo, jeongiserang gaseubineun ttaro naesyeoya dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Water and internet are included, but you have to pay electricity and gas separately.
lines.note: -셔야 돼요 = honorific of -아/어야 돼요 (have to); 따로 = separately

lines.ko: 옵션은 뭐가 있어요? 세탁기랑 에어컨 있어요?
lines.romanization: opsyeoneun mwoga isseoyo? setakgirang eeokeon isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What options does it come with? Is there a washing machine and air conditioner?
lines.note: 옵션 = built-in appliances/furnishings that come with the unit

lines.ko: 풀옵션이에요. 냉장고, 세탁기, 에어컨, 인덕션 다 있어요.
lines.romanization: puropsyeonieyo. naengjanggo, setakgi, eeokeon, indeoksyeon da isseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's fully furnished. Fridge, washing machine, AC, and an induction stove — it has everything.
lines.note: 풀옵션 = 'full option', the common term for a fully equipped studio

lines.ko: 방이 좀 어두운 것 같은데, 햇빛은 잘 들어와요?
lines.romanization: bangi jom eoduun geot gateunde, haetbicheun jal deureowayo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The room seems a bit dark — does it get good sunlight?
lines.note: 햇빛이 들어오다 = (sun)light comes in; 채광 is the noun for natural lighting

lines.ko: 남향이라서 낮에는 햇빛 잘 들어와요. 곰팡이 걱정은 없으실 거예요.
lines.romanization: namhyangiraseo najeneun haetbit jal deureowayo. gompangi geokjeongeun eopseusil geoyeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It faces south, so it gets good light during the day. You won't have to worry about mold.
lines.note: 남향 = south-facing, a big selling point; 곰팡이 = mold, a real concern in cheap 원룸

lines.ko: 마음에 들어요. 다음 달 초에 입주 가능해요?
lines.romanization: maeume deureoyo. daeum dal choe ipju ganeunghaeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I like it. Can I move in early next month?
lines.note: 입주 = moving in; 다음 달 초 = early next month

lines.ko: 네, 가능해요. 계약하시려면 가계약금 먼저 넣으시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, ganeunghaeyo. gyeyakasiryeomyeon gagyeyakgeum meonjeo neoeusimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible. If you want to sign, you just put down a holding deposit first.
lines.note: 가계약금 = a small holding deposit to reserve the unit before the full contract

dialogues.tip: Rent is quoted as '보증금 / 월세' (deposit / monthly), and 관리비 (maintenance fee) is almost always extra — always ask what it covers. Check 옵션 (appliances), 채광/방향 (light & direction), and look for 곰팡이 (mold). Never wire a 가계약금 until you've confirmed the listed owner matches the property register (등기부등본).

dialogues.title: Calling the Landlord About a Broken Boiler and Leak
dialogues.situation: Your hot water stopped working and there's a water leak under the sink, so you call your 집주인 to ask for repairs.

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: Hello, sir. This is the tenant in unit 402.
lines.note: 사장님 = a common, respectful way tenants address a landlord; 여보세요 = 'hello' on the phone

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Yes, is something the matter?
lines.note: 무슨 일 있으세요 = 'is something wrong?', a natural phone opener

lines.ko: 어제부터 보일러가 고장 나서 따뜻한 물이 안 나와요.
lines.romanization: eojebuteo boilleoga gojang naseo ttatteutan muri an nawayo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: The boiler has been broken since yesterday, so no hot water comes out.
lines.note: 고장 나다 = to break down; 어제부터 ... 안 나와요 = '(it) hasn't come out since yesterday'

lines.ko: 아이고, 추운데. 온수만 안 나와요, 아니면 난방도 안 돼요?
lines.romanization: aigo, chuunde. onsuman an nawayo, animyeon nanbangdo an dwaeyo?
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Oh no, and it's cold out. Is it only the hot water, or is the heating out too?
lines.note: 온수 = hot water (formal); 난방 = heating — boilers in Korea handle both

lines.ko: 난방도 안 돼요. 그리고 싱크대 밑에서 물이 새요.
lines.romanization: nanbangdo an dwaeyo. geurigo singkeudae miteseo muri saeyo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: The heating is out too. And water is leaking under the sink.
lines.note: 물이 새다 = to leak; 싱크대 밑 = under the sink

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: A leak on top of that? Has a lot of water pooled on the floor?
lines.note: 누수 = water leakage (the noun you'll see on repair bills); 물이 고이다 = water pools up

lines.ko: 네, 수건으로 막아 놨는데 계속 새요. 빨리 좀 고쳐 주셨으면 좋겠어요.
lines.romanization: ne, sugeoneuro maga nwanneunde gyesok saeyo. ppalli jom gochyeo jusyeosseumyeon jokesseoyo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: Yes, I blocked it with a towel but it keeps leaking. I'd really appreciate it if you could fix it soon.
lines.note: 고쳐 주셨으면 좋겠어요 = a polite, indirect request: 'I'd be grateful if you'd fix it'

lines.ko: 알겠어요. 오늘 바로 기사님 보낼게요. 몇 시에 집에 계세요?
lines.romanization: algesseoyo. oneul baro gisanim bonaelgeyo. myeot sie jibe gyeseyo?
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Understood. I'll send a technician right away today. What time will you be home?
lines.note: 기사님 = repair technician (honorific); 보낼게요 = 'I'll send', the landlord's promise

lines.ko: 저녁 7시 이후에 집에 있어요. 그 전엔 회사라서요.
lines.romanization: jeonyeok 7si ihue jibe isseoyo. geu jeonen hoesaraseoyo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: I'm home after 7 p.m. Before that I'm at work.
lines.note: -라서요 = trailing 'because...', softens the reason

lines.ko: 그럼 7시 반쯤 기사님이 연락드릴 거예요. 수리비는 제가 낼게요.
lines.romanization: geureom 7si banjjeum gisanimi yeollakdeuril geoyeyo. suribineun jega naelgeyo.
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Then the technician will contact you around 7:30. I'll cover the repair cost.
lines.note: 수리비 = repair fee; landlords pay for repairs to fixtures like the boiler

lines.ko: 감사합니다. 혹시 못 고치면 보일러 교체도 가능할까요?
lines.romanization: gamsahamnida. hoksi mot gochimyeon boilleo gyochedo ganeunghalkkayo?
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: Thank you. If it can't be fixed, would replacing the boiler be possible too?
lines.note: 교체 = replacement; -(으)ㄹ까요 here softly checks possibility

lines.ko: 기사님이 보고 판단할 거예요. 너무 걱정 마세요.
lines.romanization: gisanimi bogo pandanhal geoyeyo. neomu geokjeong maseyo.
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: The technician will decide after looking. Don't worry too much.
lines.note: 걱정 마세요 = 'don't worry', a reassuring set phrase

dialogues.tip: Repairs to fixed installations — 보일러 (boiler), 누수 (leaks), 변기 (toilet) — are normally the landlord's (집주인) responsibility, so report them fast by phone. Take photos and a quick video as evidence, and confirm who pays (수리비) before the 기사님 (technician) arrives. Address your landlord as 사장님 or 사모님 to keep it polite.

dialogues.title: Buying Cold Medicine at the Pharmacy
dialogues.situation: You catch a cold and go to a 약국 to describe your symptoms and buy over-the-counter medicine.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Welcome. What's bothering you?
lines.note: 어디가 안 좋으세요 = a softer, common way to ask what's wrong

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I've felt a cold coming on since yesterday.
lines.note: 감기 기운 = signs/onset of a cold, a very natural phrase

lines.ko: 증상이 어떻게 되세요? 콧물이나 기침 있으세요?
lines.romanization: jeungsangi eotteoke doeseyo? konmurina gichim isseuseyo?
lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: What are your symptoms? Do you have a runny nose or a cough?
lines.note: 증상 = symptom; ~이나 lists options

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a runny nose and my throat feels a bit scratchy.
lines.note: 따끔거리다 = to feel prickly/scratchy

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: What about a fever? Do you have one too?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: No fever, but I feel a bit chilly and shivery.
lines.note: 으슬으슬하다 = the chilly, shivery feeling of a cold

lines.ko: 그럼 종합감기약 드릴게요. 졸린 성분이 들어 있어요.
lines.romanization: geureom jonghapgamgiyak deurilgeyo. jollin seongbuni deureo isseoyo.
lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Then I'll give you a combination cold medicine. It has a drowsy ingredient in it.
lines.note: 종합감기약 = all-in-one cold medicine

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How many times a day do I take it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Take it three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
lines.note: 식후 30분 = 30 minutes after eating, the standard dosing line

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is it okay to drive after taking this?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: It may make you drowsy, so avoid driving.
lines.note: ~(으)니까 = because/so; gives a reason before advice

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Got it. How much is it?

dialogues.tip: For colds, fevers, and minor pain you can buy medicine straight from a 약국 without a prescription. Just describe your 증상 (symptoms) clearly. For most antibiotics you'll need a doctor's prescription (처방전) first.

dialogues.title: Registering at a Clinic Front Desk
dialogues.situation: You arrive at a 의원 (clinic) for the first time and check in at the front desk before seeing the doctor.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. Let me help you check in. Is this your first visit?
lines.note: 접수 = registration/check-in; 처음 오셨어요 asks if you're a new patient

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, it's my first time.

lines.ko: 그럼 이 문진표 좀 작성해 주세요. 신분증 있으세요?
lines.romanization: geureom i munjinpyo jom jakseonghae juseyo. sinbunjeung isseuseyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then please fill out this form. Do you have an ID?
lines.note: 문진표 작성하다 = to fill out a medical questionnaire; 신분증 = ID card

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is an Alien Registration Card okay too?
lines.note: 외국인등록증 = ARC, the ID foreigners carry in Korea

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Do you have health insurance?
lines.note: 건강보험 = national health insurance

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I have insurance through my job.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What are you here to see the doctor about?
lines.note: 어디가 불편하세요 = a polite, standard way to ask your reason for visiting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I've had a cough that won't stop for a few days.
lines.note: 며칠째 = for several days now; ~아서/어서요 trails off to give a reason

lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 저쪽에서 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 성함 부를게요.
lines.romanization: algetseumnida. jeojjogeseo jamsiman gidaryeo juseyo. seongham bureulgeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Got it. Please wait over there for a moment. I'll call your name.
lines.note: 성함 = honorific for 'name'; 부르다 = to call

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, do I pay the consultation fee after I'm done?
lines.note: 진료비 = medical/consultation fee

lines.ko: 네, 진료 끝나고 여기서 수납하시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, jillyo kkeunnago yeogiseo sunapasimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can settle the payment here after your consultation.
lines.note: 수납하다 = to pay/settle the bill, common at clinic desks

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. I'll wait.

dialogues.tip: First-time patients fill out a short 문진표 (medical questionnaire) and show ID (your 외국인등록증 works). If you're enrolled in 건강보험, clinic visits are cheap. You usually see the doctor first and pay (수납) at the desk on your way out, then take any 처방전 to a nearby pharmacy.

dialogues.title: Part-time job interview
dialogues.situation: You go to a cafe to interview for an 알바 (part-time job) after seeing a 'staff wanted' notice.

lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: Hello. Are you here for the part-time job interview?
lines.note: 면접 보다 = to have/do an interview. 알바 is the everyday short form of 아르바이트.

lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, that's right. I'm the one who called yesterday.
lines.note: 전화드리다 is the humble form of 전화하다, polite toward the boss.

lines.ko: 네, 여기 앉으세요. 혹시 카페에서 일해 본 적 있어요?
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi anjeuseyo. hoksi kapeeseo ilhae bon jeok isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: Okay, please have a seat. Have you ever worked at a cafe before?
lines.note: -아/어 본 적 있다 = 'have you ever (done)?', asking about experience.

lines.ko: 네, 전에 다른 카페에서 6개월 정도 일했어요.
lines.romanization: ne, jeone dareun kapeeseo 6gaewol jeongdo ilhaesseoyo.
lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, I worked at another cafe for about 6 months before.
lines.note: 정도 = 'about/approximately', softens the number.

lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: That's good. Can you come in on weekends too?
lines.note: 나오다 here means 'to come in (to work)'. -ㄹ 수 있다 = can/be able to.

lines.ko: 네, 주말은 다 괜찮고, 평일은 저녁에만 가능해요.
lines.romanization: ne, jumareun da gwaenchanko, pyeongireun jeonyeogeman ganeunghaeyo.
lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, weekends are all fine, and weekdays I'm only available in the evening.
lines.note: -만 = 'only'. 가능하다 = to be possible/available.

lines.ko: 시급은 만 원이고, 4대 보험은 안 돼요. 괜찮아요?
lines.romanization: sigeubeun man wonigo, 4dae boheomeun an dwaeyo. gwaenchanayo?
lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: The hourly wage is 10,000 won, and there's no employment insurance package. Is that okay?
lines.note: 시급 = hourly wage. 4대 보험 = the four major insurances; small 알바 jobs often skip it.

lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. When can I start working?
lines.note: -(으)면 되다 = 'it's enough to / I just need to (do)'; here, 'when should I start?'

lines.ko: 이번 주 토요일부터 나오면 돼요. 11시까지 오세요.
lines.romanization: ibeon ju toyoilbuteo naomyeon dwaeyo. 11sikkaji oseyo.
lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: You can start this Saturday. Please come by 11.
lines.note: -부터 = from (starting point). -까지 = by/until (time limit).

lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Okay, understood. I'll see you on Saturday!
lines.note: 뵙겠습니다 = humble 'I will see you', polite and professional toward an employer.

dialogues.tip: Always confirm the 시급 (hourly wage), schedule, and start date out loud before you leave. For any 알바, you have the legal right to a written contract (근로계약서) and at least the minimum wage, so it's fine to ask 근로계약서 써요? if they don't mention it.

dialogues.title: Calling in sick to your manager
dialogues.situation: You wake up sick and have to phone your 점장 (store manager) to say you can't make your shift today.

lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Hello?
lines.note: 여보세요 is the standard way to answer the phone in Korean.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Manager, it's me, Minsu. Is it okay to talk right now?
lines.note: 통화 괜찮으세요? = 'Is it a good time to talk?', a polite phone opener.

lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Oh, Minsu. What's up?
lines.note: 무슨 일이에요? = 'What's the matter?' / 'What's going on?'

lines.ko: 제가 아침부터 몸이 너무 안 좋아서요. 열도 나고 계속 토해요.
lines.romanization: jega achimbuteo momi neomu an joaseoyo. yeoldo nago gyesok tohaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I've been feeling really unwell since this morning. I have a fever and keep throwing up.
lines.note: 몸이 안 좋다 = 'to feel unwell'. -아/어서요 ends a sentence by giving a reason.

lines.ko: 아이고, 많이 아파요? 병원은 가 봤어요?
lines.romanization: aigo, mani apayo? byeongwoneun ga bwasseoyo?
lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Oh no, are you very sick? Have you been to the doctor?
lines.note: 아이고 is a sympathetic exclamation. 병원 가다 = 'to go to the hospital/clinic'.

lines.ko: 지금 가려고요. 죄송한데 오늘 출근 못 할 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: jigeum garyeogoyo. joesonghande oneul chulgeun mo tal geot gatayo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm about to go now. I'm sorry, but I don't think I can come in to work today.
lines.note: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 = 'I think / it seems'; softens bad news. 출근하다 = to go to work.

lines.ko: 음... 그럼 어쩔 수 없죠. 오늘은 푹 쉬어요.
lines.romanization: eum... geureom eojjeol su eopsjyo. oneureun puk swieoyo.
lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Hmm... well, then it can't be helped. Get plenty of rest today.
lines.note: 어쩔 수 없다 = 'there's no choice / it can't be helped'. 푹 쉬다 = to rest well.

lines.ko: 정말 죄송해요. 혹시 대신 나올 사람 제가 알아볼까요?
lines.romanization: jeongmal joesonghaeyo. hoksi daesin naol saram jega arabolkkayo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm really sorry. Should I try to find someone to cover for me?
lines.note: 대신 = 'instead/in place of'. 알아보다 = to look into / find out. Offering to help shows responsibility.

lines.ko: 아니에요, 그건 내가 알아볼게요. 몸조리 잘하고요.
lines.romanization: anieyo, geugeon naega arabolgeyo. momjori jalhagoyo.
lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: No, I'll take care of that. Just take good care of yourself.
lines.note: 몸조리 잘하다 = 'take good care of your health', a common get-well phrase.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, thank you. I'll definitely come in tomorrow.
lines.note: 꼭 = 'for sure/definitely'. -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses a promise to the listener.

dialogues.tip: Call as early as possible and always offer a clear reason plus an apology. Saying 죄송한데... before the bad news and offering to help find a 대타 (a fill-in) makes a great impression. If you visited a clinic, you can ask for a 진료확인서 (proof of treatment) in case your manager wants it.

dialogues.title: Ordering delivery food by phone
dialogues.situation: You phone a fried-chicken place to order 배달 (delivery) to your apartment.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, this is Kyochon Chicken. May I take your order?
lines.note: 주문 도와드릴까요? = 'May I help you with your order?', a standard restaurant greeting.

lines.ko: 네, 배달 되죠? 후라이드 한 마리 주문하려고요.
lines.romanization: ne, baedal doejyo? huraideu han mari jumunharyeogoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, you do delivery, right? I'd like to order one whole fried chicken.
lines.note: 배달 되죠? = 'you do delivery, right?'. 한 마리 = 'one (whole) chicken'; 마리 counts animals.
